### BT19-001 — Pickmons

Card lane 1. Base `23eee9e5a`. Module IR unchanged; only the test file was extended.

#### Card summary

Catalog (`packages/shared/src/cards/data/cards.json`): Red Digi-Egg, Lv2, In-Training,
Minor, type [Xros Heart], play cost -1, DP 0, no evoCosts, rarity C, max 4.

Printed clauses (Digi-Eggs have no main effect):

1. Inherited: `[When Attacking] [Once Per Turn] By placing 1 Digimon card with the
[Xros Heart]/[Blue Flare] trait from your hand under any of your Tamers, ＜Draw 1＞.`

The catalog previously read `rom your hand`; the coordinator corrected it to
`trait from your hand` in `packages/shared/src/cards/data/cards.json` and rebuilt
shared. This file asserts no printed text directly (`BT19-catalog-sync.test.ts` owns
the exact bytes), so no test assertion needed changing.

#### Q&A ids

`docs/audits/BT19-reaudit/KB-INDEX.md` lists `None` for this card, and
`node tools/kb/query.mjs card BT19-001` returns no rulings. Nothing to cover.

#### Clause -> test -> IR

Clause 1 -> `effects[0]`: `trigger: "WhenAttacking"`, `isInherited: true`,
`frequency: "OncePerTurn"`, one `Draw` action (`controller: "mine"`, `amount: 1`,
`optional: true`, `abortOnDecline: true`) whose `cost` is
`kind: "place"` with target filter `controller: "mine", zone: "hand", kind: ["Digimon"]`
and `nameOrTrait: [{ tokens: ["Xros Heart","Blue Flare"], match: "trait" }]`
(exact trait match — correct for "with the [X] trait"), `count: 1`, and
`underFilter: { controller: "mine", kind: ["Tamer"] }`.

Tests in `apps/api/src/cards/BT19/BT19-001.test.ts`:

- `places only a qualifying Digimon from hand under a Tamer and draws` — seeded
  stack: places the [Blue Flare] BT19-016, leaves the off-trait BT19-067 in hand,
  draws the deck top (asserted by instance id), and refuses a second placement/draw on
  a second same-turn attack.
- `may decline the placement cost and does not draw` — `autoDeclineOptional`:
  Tamer stack stays empty, hand unchanged (`abortOnDecline` proved).
- `carries the inherited draw through the real Digi-Egg route and is once per turn`
  — full lifecycle, all public intents:
  - `hatchEgg` in the production Breeding window puts BT19-001 in breeding, egg
    deck empties.
  - `digivolve` intent puts the Red Lv3 BT3-009 (Red Lv2, cost 0) onto the egg in
    breeding; `breeding.stack` is exactly the egg instance and the battle area still
    holds only the seeded Tamer.
  - `moveFromBreeding` on the next own turn carries the stack into the battle area;
    the carrier's `stack` is the same egg instance id.
  - The carrier attacks: exactly the [Xros Heart] BT10-007 lands under the Tamer and
    exactly one card comes off the deck top (asserted by instance id).
    `preferInstanceIds` biases the cost selection toward the off-trait BT19-067, so a
    filter accepting it would fail here — this is the near-miss peer.
  - Same turn, after `verb.unsuspend`, a second attack changes neither the Tamer
    stack nor the hand (Once Per Turn refusal).
  - Turn 5 through the real turn loop: the clause fires again from the same stack,
    the second [Xros Heart] copy is placed and one more card is drawn; the off-trait
    peer is still in hand. `pendingDecision` is undefined at the end.
- `does nothing when there is no Tamer to place the card under` — no Tamer in play:
  the qualifying card stays in hand and the deck is untouched.

No injected timing (`fire`, `fireTiming`, `fireSubTrigger`) anywhere in the file;
`verb.unsuspend` is used only to re-arm the attacker inside a turn, not to fire a
timing. Fixtures carry no Digi-Egg in security or deck (the two seeded-stack tests previously
seeded the Digi-Egg BT1-001 in the main deck; they now use the inert BT1-009/BT1-013)
and no numeric `security: <n>` form.

### BT19-004 — Tokomon

Card lane 2. Base main `23eee9e5a`, branch `audit-bt19-reaudit`. Module IR unchanged;
only the test file was rewritten. No resync of `effects.json` needed.

#### Card summary

Catalog (`packages/shared/src/cards/data/cards.json`): Green Digi-Egg, level 2,
form In-Training, attribute `-`, type Lesser, `playCost: -1`, `dp: 0`,
`evoCosts: []`, rarity C, `maxCountInDeck: 4`. No `effectText`.

Printed clauses (one, inherited only):

1. `[Your Turn] While you have another green Digimon, this Digimon gets +2000 DP.`

#### Q&A ids

`docs/audits/BT19-reaudit/KB-INDEX.md` row 12 lists **None** for BT19-004.
Confirmed independently:

```
node tools/kb/query.mjs card BT19-004
  -> BT19-004 Tokomon
       (no knowledge-base entries)
```

No Q&A id applies, so no id is left uncovered.

| Id     | Covered by                    |
| ------ | ----------------------------- |
| (none) | KB has no entry for this card |

Rules consulted instead of card rulings: comprehensive §3-4-7 (raising-area cards are
not referenced by ordinary effects), which is why breeding is excluded from the count.

#### Clause -> test -> IR

Clause 1 -> `compiled.effects[0]`: `trigger: "YourTurn"`, `isInherited: true`, one
`Aura` action whose `target.filter` is `{ isSelfRef: true }` with `isSelf: true`,
`effect: { kind: "modifyDP", amount: 2000 }`, and
`while: { kind: "youHave", filter: { controllerDefault: "mine", excludeSelf: true,
kind: ["Digimon"], colors: ["Green"] } }`.

Each IR field is pinned by a behavioural endpoint:

- `amount: 2000` and `isSelf` — "gives its host +2000 DP on your turn while you have
  another green Digimon": host BT1-064 Goblimon (printed 3000 DP) reads 5000 while the
  green peer BT1-065 Mushroomon stays at its printed 4000 and the opponent's blue
  BT1-028 Elecmon at 3000. Deleting the peer drops the host back to 3000 in the same
  tick, so the Aura is continuous, not a one-shot buff.
- `excludeSelf: true` — "does not count the host itself...": the host is itself a green
  Digimon and is alone on your side; DP stays 3000.
- `kind: ["Digimon"]` — same test: BT1-088 Izzy Izumi is a **green Tamer** beside the
  host and does not satisfy the count. (Izzy's only printed effect is `[Main]`, so it
  is inert unless activated.)
- `controllerDefault: "mine"` — same test: the opponent's green BT1-065 does not count.
- Battle-area scope — same test: green Digimon in your hand, your trash and your
  breeding area do not count. The IR omits `zone: "battleArea"`; `countMatching`
  (`apps/api/src/engine/effects/interpreter/scaling.ts`) defaults an absent `zone` to a
  per-permanent battle-area scan and only counts breeding when the filter names it, so
  the omission is harmless here. The same test then adds a real second green Digimon to
  the battle area and the DP jumps to 5000, proving the count is live rather than
  simply always false.
- `trigger: "YourTurn"` — "applies only on your turn, proved across a real turn
  boundary": through `engine.startTurnLoop()`, 5000 in your main phase, 3000 in the
  opponent's main phase, 5000 again on your next turn. No `state.turnSeat` poking.

#### Peer / stack proof

"carries the DP bonus through the real Digi-Egg route: hatch -> digivolve in breeding ->
battle area" exercises the full lifecycle through public intents only:

1. `hatchEgg` in the production Breeding window moves BT19-004 from the egg deck to the
   breeding area (egg deck emptied, breeding top card asserted by card id).
2. `digivolve` puts the Green Lv3 BT1-064 onto the egg **inside the breeding area**
   (Green Lv2, cost 0). The egg's instance id is asserted as the sole entry of
   `breeding.stack`, and BT1-064 has left the hand.
3. Two `endPhase` hops later, `moveFromBreeding` carries the stack into the battle area
   on the next own turn; the carrier's top card and stack identity are asserted again.
4. Only then does the inherited Aura matter. Beside the blue near-miss peer BT1-028 the
   carrier reads its printed 3000; adding the green BT1-065 raises it to 5000 while the
   peer itself stays at 4000 and the blue peer at 3000.

Near-miss peers used: BT1-028 Elecmon (Blue Lv3 — right level and kind, wrong colour),
BT1-088 Izzy Izumi (green, yours, but a Tamer), the opponent's BT1-065 (green Digimon,
wrong controller).

#### Q&A ids

`docs/audits/BT19-reaudit/KB-INDEX.md` row 13 lists **None** for BT19-005.

| (none) | KB has no entry for this card |

Keyword rules consulted instead (`node tools/kb/query.mjs rules "Reboot"`):
comprehensive §16-11-1 (a Digimon with ＜Reboot＞ is unsuspended during the opponent's
unsuspend phase) and §16-11-2 (it is a persistent effect). Those are what make the
clause behaviourally observable rather than a keyword-flag assertion.

#### Clause -> test -> IR

Clause 1 -> `compiled.effects[0]`: `trigger: "OpponentsTurn"`, `isInherited: true`, one
`Aura` action with `target.filter: { isSelfRef: true }`, `isSelf: true`,
`effect: { kind: "keyword", keyword: { keyword: "Reboot" } }`, and
`while: { kind: "opponentHas", filter: { controllerDefault: "opponent", kind: ["Digimon"] } }`.

- `isSelf` / `isSelfRef` — "grants only its host ＜Reboot＞...": the host BT2-052
  Hagurumon has the keyword; a second own BT2-052 without the egg does not, and the
  opponent's own BT1-028 Elecmon does not.
- `trigger: "OpponentsTurn"` — same test (keyword absent on your turn) and, through the
  real turn loop, the two unsuspend tests below.
- `kind: ["Digimon"]` on the opponent side — same test: after the opponent's only
  Digimon is deleted, their remaining permanent is the Tamer BT1-088 Izzy Izumi and the
  keyword is gone. The battle-area contents are asserted by permanent id so the
  near-miss peer is provably still there.
- `keyword: "Reboot"` — proved by its printed §16-11-1 consequence, not just the flag:
  "actually unsuspends the host during the opponent's unsuspend phase, while a plain
  peer stays suspended". Through `engine.startTurnLoop()`, the host and an identical
  BT2-052 peer (both at 20 000 DP so they survive the security check) each attack the
  player on your turn; both are asserted suspended with `turnSeat` still 0; at the
  opponent's main phase the host is unsuspended and the peer is still suspended.
- `while` condition, negative — "leaves the host suspended through the opponent's turn
  when the opponent has no Digimon": the same flow with only the Tamer BT1-088 on the
  opponent's board leaves the host down and the keyword absent.

Both turn-loop tests keep a spare playable card (BT1-013) in hand so the Main phase
stays open after the attacks instead of auto-passing.

#### Peer / stack proof

"carries ＜Reboot＞ through the real Digi-Egg route: hatch -> digivolve in breeding ->
battle area" exercises the full lifecycle through public intents only:

1. `hatchEgg` moves BT19-005 from the egg deck into breeding (egg deck emptied,
   breeding top card asserted).
2. `digivolve` puts the Black Lv3 BT2-052 Hagurumon onto the egg inside the breeding
   area (Black Lv2, cost 0); the egg instance id is the sole `breeding.stack` entry,
   BT2-052 has left the hand, and the battle area is still empty.
3. `moveFromBreeding` on the next own turn carries the stack into the battle area; top
   card and stack identity asserted again.
4. On your own main phase the carrier has no ＜Reboot＞; on the following opponent turn
   it does, while the opponent's own BT1-028 does not.

Near-miss peers: BT1-028 Elecmon (opponent Digimon that satisfies the condition but
gains nothing itself), BT1-088 Izzy Izumi (opponent permanent that is not a Digimon),
and a bare BT2-052 with no Hopmon under it (identical card, no keyword, stays
suspended).

### BT19-006 — Pagumon

Card lane 2. Base main `23eee9e5a`, branch `audit-bt19-reaudit`. Module IR unchanged;
only the test file was rewritten. No resync of `effects.json` needed.

#### Card summary

Catalog (`packages/shared/src/cards/data/cards.json`): Purple Digi-Egg, level 2,
form In-Training, attribute `-`, type Lesser, `playCost: -1`, `dp: 0`,
`evoCosts: []`, rarity C, `maxCountInDeck: 4`. No `effectText`.

Printed clauses (one, inherited only):

1. `[On Deletion] If deleted other than by battle, return 1 level 3 purple Digimon card
from your trash to the hand.`

#### Q&A ids

`docs/audits/BT19-reaudit/KB-INDEX.md` row 14 lists **None** for BT19-006.
Confirmed independently:

```
node tools/kb/query.mjs card BT19-006
  -> BT19-006 Pagumon
       (no knowledge-base entries)
```

| Id     | Covered by                    |
| ------ | ----------------------------- |
| (none) | KB has no entry for this card |

Rules consulted instead (`node tools/kb/query.mjs rules "inherited effect On Deletion"`):
comprehensive §4-14-1 (deletion trashes the card), §4-14-2 (a trigger-type effect
written on a deleted card triggers in the area where the card was deleted) and
§15-16-4-1 (`[On Deletion]` triggers at the point the card is deleted). Together these
decide the ordering question this card raises — see "host's own card" below.

#### Clause -> test -> IR

Clause 1 -> `compiled.effects[0]`: `trigger: "OnDeletion"`, `isInherited: true`, one
`Return` action with `to: "hand"`,
`target.filter: { zone: "trash", controller: "mine", kind: ["Digimon"], colors: ["Purple"], levels: [3] }`,
`count: 1`, and
`condition: { kind: "not", condition: { kind: "triggerRemovalCause", removalCause: "byBattle" } }`.

Fixtures pair the single legal candidate against one near-miss per filter axis:

| Trash card       | Colour / level / kind                      | Expected |
| ---------------- | ------------------------------------------ | -------- |
| BT10-071 Gazimon | Purple, Lv3, Digimon                       | returns  |
| ST6-07 Youkomon  | Purple, **Lv4**, Digimon                   | stays    |
| BT1-028 Elecmon  | **Blue**, Lv3, Digimon                     | stays    |
| BT19-006 Pagumon | Purple, **Lv2**, **Digi-Egg**              | stays    |
| seat 1's BT2-067 | Purple, Lv3, Digimon, **opponent's trash** | stays    |

- `levels: [3]`, `colors: ["Purple"]`, `kind: ["Digimon"]`, `controller: "mine"`,
  `count: 1`, `to: "hand"` — "returns exactly one level 3 purple Digimon from your trash
  after a non-battle deletion". The endpoint is exact: `hand` equals `["BT10-071"]`, your
  trash equals the four remaining cards plus the deleted stack (host BT3-083 and the
  Pagumon, both asserted by instance id), the opponent's trash is untouched, the battle
  area is empty and no decision is left pending.
- `colors` is inclusion, not exact match — "counts a multicolour purple level 3 Digimon
  and still returns only one card": the Green/Purple BT16-040 Wormmon is a legal
  candidate. Two candidates are present; `preferInstanceIds` names the Wormmon so the
  endpoint is deterministic, and exactly one card moves.
- Empty candidate set — "does nothing when your trash holds no level 3 purple Digimon":
  hand stays empty, both trashes are asserted whole, no pending decision.
- `§4-14-1 / §4-14-2` ordering — "can return the host's own card, which reaches your
  trash before the effect resolves": the host BT2-067 DemiDevimon is itself a level 3
  purple Digimon, so after a non-battle deletion of an otherwise-empty board it is the
  only candidate and comes straight back. The endpoint is asserted by **instance id**,
  so it is provably the very card that was just deleted. This is the behaviour the
  rules require and it is now pinned rather than left to chance. (The isolating tests
  above therefore use the Purple **Lv4** BT3-083 Meramon as the host, so the host is not
  a competing candidate.)
- `condition` (`not byBattle`) — "does not fire when the host is deleted by battle": a
  1000 DP suspended BT2-067 host with BT10-071 in trash is attacked by a 5000 DP
  BT1-009 through the public `attack` intent. Nothing is returned even though a legal
  candidate — and the host card itself — is sitting in the trash.

#### Peer / stack proof

"carries the return through the real Digi-Egg route: hatch -> digivolve in breeding ->
battle area" exercises the full lifecycle through public intents only:

1. `hatchEgg` moves BT19-006 from the egg deck into breeding (egg deck emptied,
   breeding top card asserted).
2. `digivolve` puts the Purple Lv3 BT2-067 DemiDevimon onto the egg inside the breeding
   area (Purple Lv2, cost 0); the egg instance id is the sole `breeding.stack` entry and
   the battle area is still empty.
3. `moveFromBreeding` on the next own turn carries the stack into the battle area; top
   card and stack identity asserted again.
4. A non-battle deletion of that carrier fires the inherited clause from under the real
   host: exactly one BT10-071 joins the hand (hand grows by exactly one, counted against
   the drawn cards), the three near-miss trash peers stay put, the opponent's purple Lv3
   in their own trash is untouched, and the battle area is empty.

Near-miss peers appear on four axes (level, colour, kind, controller) plus the
multicolour positive and the battle-deletion negative.

```
  -> Test Files 1 passed (1); Tests 6 passed (6)

pnpm --filter @aegis/api typecheck
  -> 1 error, in another lane's file: src/cards/BT19/BT19-010.test.ts(169,28) TS2345 "hand" not assignable to CardZone.
     No error in BT19-006.ts or BT19-006.test.ts.
```

#### Defects

None in the module. The IR was correct on the single printed clause, including the
`levels: [3]` gate and the `not byBattle` condition.

The **pre-existing test** is replaced. Its weaknesses:

- Its positive assertion was `hand).toContain("BT10-071")` plus
  `trash).toEqual(arrayContaining([...]))` — neither pins how many cards moved. Its
  host BT19-067 Impmon is Purple Lv3 and so is itself a legal candidate, and its trash

### BT19-007 — Guilmon

Lane 3, card lane. Independent re-audit; the 10/10 claim in
`docs/audits/BT19-AUDIT.md` was not used as evidence.

#### Card summary

- Red Digimon, Lv.3 Rookie, play cost 3, DP 1000, Virus / Reptile.
- Digivolve cost: Red Lv.2 for 0.
- Printed clause 1: `[Start of Your Main Phase] If you have [Takato
Matsuki]/[Calumon], gain 1 memory.`
- Printed clause 2 (inherited): `[All Turns] While you have 0 or less memory,
add 2000 to this Digimon's DP deletion effects' maximums.`

#### Q&A ids

| id    | ruling                                                                                                                                                  | covered by                                                                                                                                                                       |
| ----- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Q3059 | "while you have 0 or less memory" is fulfilled when the gauge is at 0 through 10 on the OWNER's side at the moment a DP-based deletion effect activates | `applies the +2000 maximum only while its owner has 0 or less memory (memory 0 / memory 1)` — the 0 edge deletes, the 1 edge does not                                            |
| Q3060 | "add X000 to the maximum" raises the printed numeric maximum of a DP-based deletion effect                                                              | `applies the +2000 maximum ... (memory 0)` and `still raises the printed maximum for a target the bonus alone brings into range` (8000 -> 10000: 10000 DP deleted, 11000 DP not) |
| Q3061 | the maximum is NOT raised for an effect that references a Digimon's DP instead of a printed number                                                      | `does not add to a DP maximum that references the source Digimon's DP (Q3061)`                                                                                                   |

#### Clause -> test -> IR

##### `[Start of Your Main Phase] If you have [Takato Matsuki]/[Calumon], gain 1 memory.`

IR: `effects[0]` — trigger `StartOfYourMainPhase`, condition
`youHave { controller: "mine", zone: "battleArea", nameOrTrait: [{ tokens:
["Calumon", "Takato Matsuki"], match: "nameExact" }] }`, action
`GainMemory 1`.

- `gains 1 memory with Calumon in the battle area` — the real turn loop
  (`engine.runOneTurn()` + `advance.waitForMainPhase(0)`), memory read INSIDE
  the open Main phase: 0 -> 1.
- `gains 1 memory with Takato Matsuki in the battle area` — 0 -> 4 (Takato's
  own `[Start of Your Turn]` sets 0 to 3 first, then this clause adds 1).
- `does not gain memory for a near-miss Tamer that is not Takato Matsuki` —
  BT19-081 Kiriha Aonuma on the board, memory stays 0.
- `does not count the opponent's Calumon` — BT19-077 under the opponent's
  control, memory stays 0 (proves the `controller: "mine"` leg).

##### Inherited `[All Turns] While you have 0 or less memory, add 2000 ...`

IR: `effects[1]` — trigger `AllTurns`, `isInherited: true`, action
`DeletionMaxDpModifier { amount: 2000, scope: "self", duration: "permanent",
condition: memoryAtMost 0 controller "mine" }`.

The deletion effect used for proof is a different card's printed clause reached
through a public intent, never injected timing: BT19-015 Gallantmon's
`[When Digivolving] Delete 1 of your opponent's Digimon with 8000 DP or less`,
digivolved onto a BT19-012 stack that carries BT19-007 in its digivolution
cards.

- `applies the +2000 maximum only while its owner has 0 or less memory` — the
  Gallantmon route costs 4, so the gauge lands on exactly 0 or exactly 1 when
  the effect resolves. At 0 the 9000 DP target is deleted (8000 + 2000);
  at 1 it survives. Endpoints asserted: memory (0 -> 2 via Gallantmon's own
  "gain 2 memory" on the deleting branch, 1 -> 1 on the other), top card
  `BT19-015`, stack `["BT19-007", "BT19-012"]`, opponent battle area, no
  pending decision.
- `leaves the printed 8000 maximum alone without Guilmon in the digivolution
cards` — identical board with an inert BT1-009 under the stack; the 9000 DP
  target survives. This is the peer/stack near-miss that attributes the
  deletion to Guilmon.
- `still raises the printed maximum for a target the bonus alone brings into
range` — 10000 DP deleted, 11000 DP survives, pinning the new maximum at
  exactly 10000.
- `does not add to a DP maximum that references the source Digimon's DP
(Q3061)` — BT19-014 Shoutmon EX6's `[When Attacking] delete 1 of your
opponent's Digimon with as much or less DP as this Digimon` with Guilmon
  underneath; its 12000 DP does not become 14000 against a 13000 DP target.

```
  -> 11 passed (11)     (docs/audits/BT19-reaudit/logs/BT19-007-vitest.log)
```

#### Defects fixed locally

1. The two start-of-main tests both asserted `memory === -3` after
   `runTurn(0)`. That is the post-turn-pass value, identical with and without

2. IR `match: "name"` (substring) for a bracketed `[Takato Matsuki]/[Calumon]`

3. IR condition `memoryAtMost` had no `controller`, so it read the raw gauge

### BT19-008 — Shoutmon

Card lane 4. Base main `23eee9e5a`, branch `audit-bt19-reaudit`.
Module IR CHANGED (one defect fixed) — `packages/shared/src/effects/effects.json`
is now stale for BT19-008 and `BT19-catalog-sync.test.ts` fails for it until the
coordinator resyncs.

#### Card summary

Catalog (`packages/shared/src/cards/data/cards.json`): Red/Yellow Digimon, Lv3,
Rookie, Data, Mini Dragon / Xros Heart, play cost 4, DP 1000, evoCosts Red Lv2
and Yellow Lv2 at 1 memory, rarity U, max 4.

Printed clauses:

1. `[Digivolve]Lv.2 w/[Xros Heart] trait: Cost 0` — alternate route, EXACT trait.
2. `[On Play] This Digimon may digivolve into [OmniShoutmon] under your Tamers
without paying the cost.` — exact name, source zone "under your Tamers",
   optional, cost waived (requirements are NOT waived).
3. `[On Deletion] Reveal the top 3 cards of your deck. Play 1 Tamer card with the
[Xros Heart] trait among them without paying the cost. Return the rest to the
bottom of the deck. Then, ＜Save＞.`
4. Inherited: `[Your Turn] This Digimon with the [Xros Heart] trait gains ＜Rush＞.`

Note on wording: this card uses the EXACT trait form ("[Xros Heart] trait"),
unlike BT10-008 Shoutmon which uses the substring form ("[Xros Heart] in
traits"). The IR is right to use `match: "trait"` on both trait filters.

#### Q&A ids

`node tools/kb/query.mjs card BT19-008` returns 2 Q&A, both covered.

| Id                                                                                                                     | Covered by                                                                                        |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Q3062 — can [On Play] digivolve this into BT11-018 Shoutmon DX? No: you cannot ignore the digivolution requirements.   | `does not ignore OmniShoutmon digivolution requirements (Q3062)`                                  |
| Q3063 — after playing a Tamer with [On Deletion], can the ＜Save＞ after "then" place this card under that Tamer? Yes. | `plays an Xros Heart Tamer from the top 3, bottoms the rest, then Saves under that Tamer (Q3063)` |

Q3062 is a real test, not a name mismatch by accident: BT11-018 prints "The name
of this card/Digimon is also treated as [OmniShoutmon]", so it passes the `into`
name filter. It is refused because it is a Lv6 needing a Lv5 Red source, which a
Lv3 Shoutmon cannot satisfy. The comparison case is BT19-012 OmniShoutmon, which
prints `[Digivolve][Shoutmon]: Cost 4` and therefore IS a legal target.

Rules read for this card:

- comprehensive 16-20-1 — ＜Save＞ places THIS card under 1 of your Tamers.
- comprehensive 16-20-3 — the processing from ＜Save＞ is OPTIONAL.
- comprehensive 4-3 — a Save'd card goes to the BOTTOM of an existing Tamer stack.

#### Clause -> test -> IR

- Clause 1 -> `compiled.digivolutionRequirement`
  `[{ level: 2, traits: ["Xros Heart"], cost: 0, isAlternate: true }]`.
  - `offers its cost-0 alternate route only over a level-2 Xros Heart base`:
    BT10-005 Monimon (Lv2 Digi-Egg, Xros Heart) -> cost 0; near-miss BT19-005
    Hopmon (Lv2, Baby Dragon) -> undefined; near-miss BT19-031 Starmons (Xros
    Heart but Lv3) -> undefined.
  - `takes the cost-0 route through the real breeding stack and refuses the
non-Xros-Heart egg`: the realistic stack case. Public intents only —
    `hatchEgg` -> `digivolve` with `useAlternateCost: true` in breeding ->
    `moveFromBreeding` on the next own turn, driven by `startTurnLoop`. Endpoints:
    memory unchanged at 3 (cost 0), hand length preserved (one played, one drawn),
    breeding stack is exactly the egg instance, carrier top card is BT19-008 in
    the battle area. Seat 1 runs the same intent over BT19-005 and is refused
    (`ok: false`), with its breeding top card still BT19-005.
- Clause 2 -> `effects[0]` `OnPlay` / `Digivolve`, `optional: true`,
  `payCost: false`, `from: ["underTamers"]`,
  `into.nameOrTrait [{ tokens: ["OmniShoutmon"], match: "name" }]`,
  `onto.filter { controller: "mine", kind: ["Tamer"] }`.
  - `digivolves into a legal OmniShoutmon from under a Tamer without paying the
cost`: BT19-012 under BT19-079 Taiki Kudo. Endpoints: the OmniShoutmon
    permanent's stack is exactly the Shoutmon instance id, the Tamer's stack is
    empty, memory 4 -> 0 (the 4 is the PLAY cost of Shoutmon; the digivolve was
    free), no pending decision.
  - Q3062 negative as tabled above, with full endpoints: Shoutmon on the field
    with an empty stack, BT11-018 still under the Tamer and never in the battle
    area, memory 0, no pending decision.
- Clause 3 -> `effects[1]` `OnDeletion`, `keywords: [{ keyword: "Save" }]`,
  actions `RevealAdd` (`revealCount: 3`, `rest: "deckBottom"`, add filter
  `kind: ["Tamer"]` + `nameOrTrait [{ tokens: ["Xros Heart"], match: "trait" }]`,
  `count: 1`, `to: "play"`) then `PlaceUnder` (`target.isSelf`,
  `underFilter { controller: "mine", kind: ["Tamer"], excludeToken: true }`,
  `optional: true`).
  - Q3063 positive with a near-miss peer: the top 3 are BT19-081 Kiriha Aonuma
    (Tamer, General/Blue Flare — the near miss), BT19-079 Taiki Kudo (Tamer,
    General/Xros Heart) and BT1-009. Endpoints: Taiki is played, its stack is
    exactly the Shoutmon instance id, Shoutmon is NOT in the trash, Kiriha is
    never in the battle area, and the deck reads
    `["BT1-010","BT1-011","BT19-081","BT1-009"]` — the untouched remainder first,
    then the two bottomed cards. Memory unchanged, no pending decision.
  - Declined branch: `leaves the deleted Shoutmon in the trash when the optional
＜Save＞ is declined` — `autoDeclineOptional`, Tamer stack empty, Shoutmon
    instance id in the trash.
- Clause 4 -> `effects[2]` `YourTurn`, `isInherited: true`, `GainKeyword` Rush,
  target filter `isSelfRef` + exact `Xros Heart` trait, `duration: "permanent"`.
  - `grants inherited Rush only to an Xros Heart host and only during its
controller's turn`: BT19-012 (Dragonkin/Xros Heart) has Rush; the near-miss
    peer BT19-015 Gallantmon (Holy Warrior/Royal Knight, same colour, same seat)
    does not; flipping `turnSeat` removes it.
  - Behavioural consequence, not just the grant flag: `lets the inherited Rush
host attack the turn it arrived while the near-miss host cannot` — both hosts
    `enteredThisTurn`, the Gallantmon attack intent is refused and it stays
    unsuspended, the OmniShoutmon attack is accepted, a security check fires
    (seat 1 security 2 -> 1) and the attacker is suspended.

No injected timing (`advance.fire`, `fireTiming`, `fireSubTrigger`) anywhere in
the file. The only Advance-Surface use is `verb.deletePermanent` for the two
[On Deletion] cases, because no public intent deletes an own Digimon on demand.
Fixtures carry no Digi-Egg in security or deck (the only Digi-Egg, BT10-005, is
in the egg deck, where it belongs) and no numeric `security: <n>` form.

#### Defects

**Fixed locally: ＜Save＞ was mandatory.** The `PlaceUnder` action carried
`abortOnDecline: true` but no `optional: true`, and the effect did not declare the
`Save` keyword. Comprehensive 16-20-3 states the processing from ＜Save＞ is
optional, and the accepted BT10-008 module (the other printed ＜Save＞ on a
Shoutmon) uses exactly `optional: true` plus
`keywords: [{ keyword: "Save", raw: "＜Save＞" }]`. Reproduced before the fix: with
`autoDeclineOptional: true` the deleted Shoutmon still landed under the Tamer and
never reached the trash; the only decision raised in the whole flow was an
`orderCards`. `abortOnDecline` was also dead weight — it aborts SUBSEQUENT actions
and ＜Save＞ is the last action in the sequence — so it was dropped in the same
edit. The declined branch is now a passing test.

No red tests retained.

#### Remaining gaps

- The alternate route's "cost 0" cannot be told apart from a paid route by memory
  alone in breeding, because the printed evoCosts (1 memory) differ from 0 only by
  1; the test pins memory at exactly 3 before and after, so the 1-memory normal
  route would have shown. The stronger isolation is the seat-1 refusal over a
  non-Xros-Heart Lv2 base.
- ＜Save＞ placing the card at the BOTTOM of a Tamer that already has cards under
  it (comprehensive 4-3) is not asserted; in every fixture here the Tamer stack is
  empty when the Save resolves.
- `excludeToken: true` on the Save's `underFilter` is unexercised — no Tamer token
  fixture exists in this lane's allowed files.

#### Catalog discrepancies

None. Every asserted field matches the official printing. One formatting note: the
catalog's `inheritedEffectText` uses a full-width ＜ ＞ pair whose bytes differ from
a hand-typed literal, so the catalog test asserts the structured fields and leaves
the inherited text to the IR-shape test rather than a byte comparison.

### BT19-009 — Growlmon

Lane 3, card lane. Independent re-audit; the 10/10 claim in
`docs/audits/BT19-AUDIT.md` was not used as evidence.

#### Card summary

- Red Digimon, Lv.4 Champion, play cost 5, DP 5000, Virus / Dark Dragon.
- Digivolve cost: Red Lv.3 for 2.
- Printed clause 1: `[When Digivolving] If you have 1 or fewer Tamers, you may
play 1 [Takato Matsuki] from your hand without paying the cost.`
- Printed clause 2 (inherited): `[All Turns] While you have 0 or less memory,
add 2000 to this Digimon's DP deletion effects' maximums.`

#### Q&A ids

| id    | ruling                                                                                                                                                  | covered by                                                                                                                                                                       |
| ----- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Q3064 | "while you have 0 or less memory" is fulfilled when the gauge is at 0 through 10 on the OWNER's side at the moment a DP-based deletion effect activates | `applies the +2000 maximum only while its owner has 0 or less memory (memory 0 / memory 1)` — the 0 edge deletes, the 1 edge does not                                            |
| Q3065 | "add X000 to the maximum" raises the printed numeric maximum of a DP-based deletion effect                                                              | `applies the +2000 maximum ... (memory 0)` and `still raises the printed maximum for a target the bonus alone brings into range` (8000 -> 10000: 10000 DP deleted, 11000 DP not) |
| Q3066 | the maximum is NOT raised for an effect that references a Digimon's DP instead of a printed number                                                      | `does not add to a DP maximum that references the source Digimon's DP (Q3066)`                                                                                                   |

#### Clause -> test -> IR

##### `[When Digivolving] If you have 1 or fewer Tamers, you may play 1 [Takato Matsuki] from your hand without paying the cost.`

IR: `effects[0]` — trigger `WhenDigivolving`, action `PlayWithoutCost
{ optional: true, payCost: false, from: ["hand"], target: nameExact
["Takato Matsuki"], condition: youHave kind ["Tamer"] countMax 1 }`.

- `plays Takato for free through the digivolve intent with 0 / 1 Tamer(s)` —
  the real `digivolve` intent onto a BT19-007 base. Endpoints: memory 2 -> 0
  (only the digivolution cost of 2 paid; Takato's play cost 3 was not), top
  card `BT19-009`, stack `["BT19-007"]`, Takato's exact instance on the board,
  hand holding only the digivolve bonus draw, no pending decision. The bonus
  draw itself confirms a legal digivolve route rather than a bare `{ok:true}`.
- `does not play Takato when it already has 2 Tamers` — the `countMax: 1`
  boundary; Takato stays in hand and the battle area keeps 3 permanents.
- `does not play a near-miss Tamer that is not Takato Matsuki` — BT19-079
  Taiki Kudo in hand instead; nothing is played (the `nameExact` leg).
- `declines the optional play when the controller says no` — `autoDeclineOptional`;
  Takato stays in hand, proving the clause is a "may".

##### Inherited `[All Turns] While you have 0 or less memory, add 2000 ...`

IR: `effects[1]` — trigger `AllTurns`, `isInherited: true`, action
`DeletionMaxDpModifier { amount: 2000, scope: "self", duration: "permanent",
condition: memoryAtMost 0 controller "mine" }`.

The deletion effect used for proof is a different card's printed clause reached
through a public intent, never injected timing: BT19-015 Gallantmon's
`[When Digivolving] Delete 1 of your opponent's Digimon with 8000 DP or less`,
digivolved onto a BT19-012 stack that carries BT19-009 in its digivolution
cards.

- `applies the +2000 maximum only while its owner has 0 or less memory` — the
  Gallantmon route costs 4, so the gauge lands on exactly 0 or exactly 1 when
  the effect resolves. At 0 the 9000 DP target is deleted (8000 + 2000); at 1
  it survives. Endpoints asserted: memory, top card `BT19-015`, stack
  `["BT19-009", "BT19-012"]`, opponent battle area, no pending decision.
- `leaves the printed 8000 maximum alone without Growlmon in the digivolution
cards` — identical board with an inert BT1-009 under the stack; the 9000 DP
  target survives. Peer/stack near-miss attributing the deletion to Growlmon.
- `still raises the printed maximum for a target the bonus alone brings into
range` — 10000 DP deleted, 11000 DP survives, pinning the new maximum at
  exactly 10000.
- `does not add to a DP maximum that references the source Digimon's DP
(Q3066)` — BT19-014 Shoutmon EX6's `[When Attacking] delete 1 of your
opponent's Digimon with as much or less DP as this Digimon` with Growlmon
  underneath; its 12000 DP does not become 14000 against a 13000 DP target.

#### Defects fixed locally

1. IR `match: "name"` (substring) for the bracketed `[Takato Matsuki]` name.
   Corrected to `nameExact`. No catalog card currently makes the two modes
   diverge for this token, so the fix is fidelity, not a behaviour change.
2. Fixture defect: the Q3066 test seeded `security: ["BT1-001"]` and
   `deck: ["BT1-002"]`, both Digi-Eggs, in main-deck zones no game can reach.
   Replaced with the inert BT1-009 Monodramon.
3. Fixtures gave the opponent no security, so every digivolve test tripped the

4. The Tamer tests asserted only `hand` contents; they did not pin the
   digivolution cost, the resulting stack, Takato's instance identity, or the
   absence of a pending decision. Endpoints added.
5. No decline case and no near-miss name case existed for the optional play.
   Both added.

### BT19-010 — Shoutmon X4

Card lane 4. Base main `23eee9e5a`, branch `audit-bt19-reaudit`.
Module IR UNCHANGED — the only module edit is `export` on the `compiled` const so
the test can assert the IR shape. No resync needed for this card.

#### Card summary

Catalog (`packages/shared/src/cards/data/cards.json`): Red/Yellow Digimon, Lv4,
Champion, Data, Composite / Xros Heart, play cost 8, DP 8000, `evoCosts: []`
(no printed digivolution route — it is played by DigiXros), rarity C, max 4.

Printed clauses:

1. `[All Turns] When this Digimon would leave the battle area, you may place up to
3 Digimon cards with the [Xros Heart] trait from this Digimon's digivolution
cards under 1 of your Tamers.`
2. `[DigiXros -2] [Shoutmon] x [Ballistamon] x [Dorulumon] x [Starmons]`

#### The prior audit's Save-source change: verified correct

The brief flagged that the prior audit narrowed this card to source only from its
OWN Digimon's digivolution cards. That is right, and it is what the card prints:
"from **this Digimon's** digivolution cards". The IR encodes it as
`target.filter.hostFilter: { isSelfRef: true }` alongside
`zone: "digivolutionCards"`. Without the `hostFilter` the effect would drain every
friendly stack, which the printed text does not permit. The test
`saves only this Digimon's Xros Heart sources when another stack also qualifies`
pins it: an adjacent BT19-009 Growlmon carrying an Xros Heart BT19-012 keeps that
card while only X4's own BT19-008 is placed.

Two related notes from the KB:

- This clause is NOT the ＜Save＞ keyword (comprehensive 16-20-1 places THIS card
  under a Tamer), and it is not ＜Material Save＞ (16-21-1, which is worded off the
  top card's DigiXros requirements and fires on deletion only). It is spelled out
  in full on this card, so the module correctly declares no keyword.
- comprehensive 4-3: cards placed under a Tamer that already holds cards go to the
  bottom. Not exercised here — see Remaining gaps.

#### Q&A ids

`node tools/kb/query.mjs card BT19-010` returns 1 Q&A.

| Id                                                                                                                                                                                | Covered by                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Q3067 — "when [...] would leave the battle area" means placed in the trash, returned to hand/deck, placed in the security stack, moved to breeding, or placed under another card. | Three of the six routes have tests: trash (`saves up to 3 Xros Heart Digimon from its own stack when deleted in battle (Q3067)`), hand (`also triggers before a hand return (Q3067) and may be declined`), deck (`also triggers before a return to the deck (Q3067)`). |

#### Clause -> test -> IR

- Clause 1 -> `effects[0]` `AllTurns` / `Replacement`, `event: "wouldLeavePlay"`,
  `sourceFilter: { isSelfRef: true }`, `optional: true`, inner `PlaceUnder` with
  `target { count: 3, upTo: true, from: ["digivolutionCards"], filter { zone:
"digivolutionCards", kind: ["Digimon"], hostFilter: { isSelfRef: true },
nameOrTrait [{ tokens: ["Xros Heart"], match: "trait" }] } }` and
  `underFilter { controller: "mine", kind: ["Tamer"] }`.
  - Realistic deletion route: X4 (8000 DP) attacks a 12000 DP suspended opponent
    Digimon through the public `attack` intent and loses the battle. Its stack is
    BT19-008, BT19-012, BT19-009 Growlmon (Dark Dragon — the near-miss source) and
    BT19-031 Starmons. Endpoints: exactly the three Xros Heart instance ids under
    the Tamer, Growlmon and X4 itself in the trash, X4 gone from the battle area,
    the opposing wall still on the board, no pending decision. This proves the
    "up to 3" cap, the exact-trait filter and that the Digimon still leaves.
  - Q3067 hand route, declined: `autoDeclineOptional` -> X4 in hand, Tamer stack
    empty, both digivolution cards in the trash.
  - Q3067 deck route: `verb.returnToDeck(..., { toTop: true })` -> X4 is deck[0],
    both Xros Heart sources under the Tamer, trash empty.
  - Own-stack scoping test as described in the section above.
- Clause 2 -> `compiled.digiXrosRequirement`
  `[{ materials: [{names:["Shoutmon"]},{names:["Ballistamon"]},
{names:["Dorulumon"]},{names:["Starmons"]}], count: 2 }]`.
  - Full DigiXros: BT10-008 / BT10-049 / BT10-034 / BT10-029 from hand.
    Comprehensive 7-2-2-1 and 7-2-3-3: the play cost is reduced by 2 PER placed
    card, so 8 - (4 x 2) = 0. Endpoints: stack instance ids equal the four
    materials, memory 0 -> 0, hand empty, no pending decision.
  - Partial DigiXros (3 materials): 8 - (3 x 2) = 2 paid, memory 2 -> 0, stack
    length 3. This is what distinguishes "-2 each" from a flat cost.
  - Near-miss material pair in one test: BT5-014 OmniShoutmon has "Shoutmon" as a
    SUBSTRING of its name and no treated-as clause, and the intent is refused with
    `{ ok: false, reason: "invalid-material" }` — board empty, hand still 5, memory
    unchanged. The positive control on the same board is BT19-012 OmniShoutmon,
    which prints "This card is also treated as [Shoutmon] for a DigiXros": the same
    slot then plays for `{ ok: true }` and BT19-012 is in the stack. DigiXros
    material names are exact, and the treated-as clause is honoured.

Injected timing (`advance.fire`, `fireTiming`, `fireSubTrigger`) is not used. The
primary deletion case runs off a real battle; `verb.returnToHand`,
`verb.returnToDeck` and one `verb.deletePermanent` cover zone changes no public
intent reaches. Fixtures contain no Digi-Egg and no numeric `security: <n>` form.

#### Defects

None found. The IR is correct on both printed clauses, including the
`hostFilter: { isSelfRef: true }` scoping the brief asked to be re-checked. The
pre-existing test file was sound but thin: it asserted `{ok:true}` on the DigiXros
without any material negative or cost-per-card proof, drove the deletion case
through `verb.deletePermanent` rather than a battle, and did not assert the
catalog or the IR shape. Those gaps are closed. No red tests retained.

#### Remaining gaps

- Q3067 lists six leave routes; the security-stack, breeding and placed-under-
  another-card routes are untested. No public intent or Advance-Surface verb in
  this lane's reach moves a battle-area permanent into the security stack or into
  breeding, and `verb.placeUnder` takes card instances rather than a whole
  permanent.
- comprehensive 4-3 bottom-placement ordering under a Tamer that already holds
  cards is unasserted — every fixture's Tamer starts empty.
- The `mode: "instead"` on the Replacement is not literally a replacement here: the
  Digimon still leaves in every route. The tests assert the leave happens, so the
  behaviour is right, but the IR's `mode` value is a modelling choice this audit
  did not change.
- `expanderPermanentIds` (BT19-079 Taiki Kudo's "place cards from under your
  Tamers for a DigiXros") is always `[]`; that interaction belongs to the Taiki
  lane.

#### Catalog discrepancies

None. Every asserted field matches the official printing, including the empty
`evoCosts`.

### BT19-011 — WarGrowlmon

`docs/audits/BT19-AUDIT.md` was not used as evidence.

#### Card summary

- Red Digimon, Lv.5 Ultimate, play cost 5, DP 8000, Virus / Cyborg, ACE with
  Overflow ＜3＞.
- Digivolve cost: Red Lv.4 for 3.
- Printed clause 1: `[Hand] [Counter] ＜Blast Digivolve＞`.
- Printed clause 2: `[On Play] [When Digivolving] Delete any of your opponent's
Digimon with DP adding up to 3000. For each of your opponent's Digimon, add
2000 to this DP-Based deletion effect's maximum. Then, for each Digimon
deleted by this effect, gain 1 memory.`
- Printed clause 3 (inherited): `[All Turns] Add 3000 to this Digimon's DP
deletion effects' maximums.`

#### Q&A ids

| id    | ruling                                                                                                                                      | covered by                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| ----- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Q6016 | if the source is removed from the battle area while the first process of this effect is resolving, the part after "then" is still processed | `finishes the 'then' clause even when the source leaves mid-resolution (Q6016)` — BT6-064 Mamemon's `[On Deletion]` fires from inside this effect's own `deletePermanent` call and deletes WarGrowlmon (play cost 5); the memory gain still resolves, and the ACE Overflow ＜3＞ is charged. Endpoints: 10 − 5 (play) + 1 (gain) − 3 (overflow) = 3, WarGrowlmon in trash, opposing 20000 DP bystander untouched |

The interleave Q6016 literally describes is an immediate-type "would leave"
replacement removing the source. No catalog card pair reaches that shape (no
printed "when this Digimon would leave the battle area" clause deletes an
opponent's Digimon). The route above is the closest reachable one and does put
the source in the trash before the "then" step runs, because deletion triggers
fire inside `deletePermanent` (`apps/api/src/engine/effects/primitives.ts:3296`)
and that call is awaited before the `GainMemory` action.

#### Clause -> test -> IR

##### `[Hand] [Counter] ＜Blast Digivolve＞`

IR: `effects[0]` — trigger `Counter`, `isFromHand: true`, keyword
`BlastDigivolve`, empty action list (the keyword is routed by
`registerBlastDigivolveFromEffects`, not by the marker's actions).

- `blast digivolves from hand in the opponent's counter window without paying
the cost` — real turn loop (`startTurnLoop`), seat 1 attacks, and seat 0
  answers the open counter window with
  `respondCounter { effectKey: "blast-digivolve:<permanentId>" }`. Endpoints:
  top card `BT19-011`, stack `["BT19-009"]`, memory unchanged (the cost is
  waived entirely, not reduced), the digivolve bonus draw in hand, the 20000 DP
  attacker still on the board (out of the 5000 maximum), attack resolved. A bare
  `digivolve` intent cannot reach this window, so the route itself is the proof.

##### `[On Play] [When Digivolving] Delete ... adding up to 3000 (+2000 each) ... then gain 1 memory each`

IR: `effects[1]` (`OnPlay`) and `effects[2]` (`WhenDigivolving`), identical
action lists — `DeleteByDPBudget { baseBudget: 3000, budgetBonus: { per: 2000,
unit: "cards", filter: opponent Digimon }, target: all opponent Digimon }` then
`GainMemory { amount: 1, scaling: { per: 1, unit: "cards", filter:
deletedByThisEffect Digimon } }`.

- `deletes the whole opposing board within the scaled budget and gains 1 memory
per deletion` — `playCard` from hand. 3 opponent Digimon give 3000 + 3 × 2000
  = 9000, and 2000 + 3000 + 4000 = 9000 exactly. Endpoints: opponent battle area
  empty, opponent trash in order, controller's own 1000 DP Digimon untouched
  (the opponent-only leg), memory 10 − 5 + 3 = 8, spare hand card left, no
  pending decision.
- `pins the single-Digimon maximum at exactly 5000 (target 5000/6000 DP)` — one
  opponent Digimon, so the maximum is 3000 + 2000. 5000 dies and gives 1 memory;
  6000 survives and gives none, which also pins the "then" clause to what was
  actually deleted.
- `counts only battle-area Digimon for the +2000, not the opponent's breeding
Digimon` — 1 battle-area Digimon at 7000 DP plus an opponent breeding Digimon.
  Counting breeding would make the maximum 7000 and delete it; it survives.
- `resolves the same clause through a real digivolve, and refuses an illegal
source` — the `digivolve` intent onto BT19-009 (Red Lv.4). The Lv.3 BT19-008
  base is rejected `invalid-evolution` first. Endpoints: stack `["BT19-009"]`,
  memory 5 − 3 + 1 = 3, bonus draw, opponent board empty.
- Q6016 test above.

##### Inherited `[All Turns] Add 3000 to this Digimon's DP deletion effects' maximums`

IR: `effects[3]` — trigger `AllTurns` (not `Static`), `isInherited: true`,
`DeletionMaxDpModifier { amount: 3000, scope: "self", duration: "permanent" }`.

- `raises a host's printed numeric maximum only from under it (BT19-011 /
BT1-009)` — BT19-015 Gallantmon's printed `[When Digivolving] delete 1 of your
opponent's Digimon with 8000 DP or less`, reached through the real digivolve
  intent onto a BT19-012 stack. 8000 + 3000 = 11000 deletes an 11000 DP target;
  the same board with an inert BT1-009 in the digivolution cards leaves it
  alive. Stack identity asserted in both rows.
- `stacks the inherited +3000 onto its own aggregate maximum` — WarGrowlmon
  digivolving over a stack that already carries WarGrowlmon: 3000 + 2000 + 3000
  = 8000 deletes an 8000 DP target. The dedicated budget bonus and the generic
  deletion-maximum bonus are shown to combine on the aggregate action.

#### Defects fixed locally

1. The test file proved both timings only through injected timing
   (`advance.fire(EffectTiming.OnPlay/WhenDigivolving, ...)`), which earns no
   behavioural credit. Every clause is now driven by a public intent
   (`playCard`, `digivolve`, `attack` + `respondCounter`).
2. `[Hand] [Counter] ＜Blast Digivolve＞` was proved only by asserting the IR
   marker's shape — no game ever entered the counter window. A real
   opponent-turn counter-window blast digivolve was added.
3. The old inherited-effect test seeded a three-card `under: [...]` stack and
   fired `WhenDigivolving` by hand; it never proved the bonus was WarGrowlmon's.
   Replaced with a real digivolve plus a same-board control that swaps
   WarGrowlmon for an inert Lv.3.
4. No boundary, no negative and no own-side control existed. Added the exact
   5000/6000 maximum edge, the zero-deletion memory case, an own Digimon that
   must not be a candidate, and the illegal-source digivolve rejection.
5. No catalog assertion existed. Added a field-by-field `getCardDefinition`
   check including `isAce` / `overflowMemory`.

Module change: `compiled` is now exported so the test can assert the IR
directly (the accepted BT19-009 shape). **The IR content itself is unchanged**,
so no `effects.json` resync is needed for this card.

None.

- `budgetBonus` carries no `zone`, which is correct here:
  `countMatching`'s default scan is the battle area only

  test pins that behaviour. Adding `zone: "battleArea"` would be cosmetic and
  would cost an `effects.json` resync, so it was not made.

and Overflow value match the official card.

#### Clause -> test -> IR

##### `[Digivolve][Shoutmon]: Cost 4` and `[Digivolve]Lv.4 w/[Xros Heart] trait: Cost 3`

IR: `digivolutionRequirement` — `[{ namesExact: ["Shoutmon"], cost: 4,
isAlternate: true }, { level: 4, traits: ["Xros Heart"], cost: 3, isAlternate:
true }]`.

target: self }`.

##### `[On Play] [When Digivolving] -3000 DP, then delete 1 with 3000 DP or less`

IR: `effects[1]` / `effects[2]` — `ModifyDP { amount: -3000, duration:
"forTheTurn", target: 1 opponent Digimon }` then `Delete { target: 1 opponent
Digimon, dp lte 3000 }`.

- `reduces one opposing Digimon by 3000 and then deletes it at the 3000 DP

##### `[On Deletion] Place 1 [Xros Heart]/[Blue Flare] Digimon from hand or trash under your Tamers`

IR: `effects[3]` — `PlaceUnder { target: { count: 1, from: ["hand", "trash"],
filter: { controller: "mine", kind: ["Digimon"], nameOrTrait: [{ tokens:
["Xros Heart", "Blue Flare"], match: "trait" }] } }, underFilter: {
controllerDefault: "mine", kind: ["Tamer"] } }`. `match: "trait"` is the exact

IR: `effects[4]` — trigger `YourTurn` (not `Static`), `isInherited: true`,

   is the SUBSTRING gate ("[X] in name",

   took the named route at cost 4 instead of the Lv.4 [Xros Heart] route at cost
   3 — a real, reachable rules error on a bracketed `[Shoutmon]` requirement.
   Corrected to `namesExact: ["Shoutmon"]`; the near-miss test pins it.

   for two bases but used no near-miss whose name CONTAINS "Shoutmon", so it
   could not see defect 1.
3. Both printed timings were proved by `advance.fireForPermanent` — injected
   timing with no endpoints. Replaced with `playCard` and both real digivolve
   routes, asserting memory, stack, hand and DP.
4. The `[On Deletion]` clause was driven by `advance.verb.deletePermanent`.
   Replaced with a real battle death, and given the missing endpoints (trash
   contents, hand contents, the opponent's own matching card left alone, the
   no-Tamer branch).
5. The digivolve tests asserted only `{ ok: true }` and never pinned which route
   was charged. The gauge now starts at exactly the route cost.
6. No catalog assertion and no full IR assertion existed; both added, including
   the `Static` vs `YourTurn` trigger split.
7. The old inherited-Rush test had no behavioural consequence; a real
   summoning-sickness-defeating attack was added.

#### Defect fixed locally

`BT19-013.ts` carried the play-cost ceiling as `playCost: { op: "lte", value: 4 }`. That object
form is only honored for PERMANENT targets (`interpreter/matching/permanent.ts`); the loose-card
matcher used for `zone: "underTamers"` reads `playCostLte`
(`interpreter/matching/definition.ts:148-157`), so the ceiling was silently dropped and the
`[On Deletion]` clause could play a card of ANY cost from under a Tamer. Proved by the pre-
existing test "saves only this Digimon's Xros Heart sources when another stack also qualifies",
which asserted the cost-7 BT19-012 arriving in the battle area. Changed to `playCostLte: 4`;
that test now asserts BT19-012 staying under the Tamer, and a dedicated negative covers cost 7
and the missing trait.

This is an IR change, so `effects.json` is stale for BT19-013.

- The save is driven by `advance().verb.deletePermanent` in five of six cases; one case runs
  through a real opponent-turn battle, which is what carries the behavioural credit for the
  `[All Turns]` window.

### BT19-015 — Gallantmon

Lane 7, card lane. Independent re-audit; the 10/10 claim in
`docs/audits/BT19-AUDIT.md` was not used as evidence.

#### Card summary

- Red Digimon, Lv.6 Mega, play cost 12, DP 12000, Virus / Holy Warrior /
  Royal Knight.
- Digivolve cost: Red Lv.5 for 4.
- Printed clause 1: `[When Digivolving] Delete 1 of your opponent's Digimon
with 8000 DP or less.`
- Printed clause 2: `If this effect didn't delete, this Digimon gains
＜Piercing＞ and gets +3000 DP until the end of your opponent's turn.`
- Printed clause 3: `[Your Turn] [Once Per Turn] When an opponent's Digimon is
deleted, gain 2 memory.`
- No inherited effect.

#### Q&A ids

| id    | ruling                                                                                       | covered by                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| ----- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Q3070 | the delete is mandatory: if the opponent has a choosable Digimon you MUST choose it          | `deletes the eligible target even when every optional prompt is declined (Q3070)` — the whole run uses `autoDeclineOptional`, and the 8000 DP body is still deleted with no Piercing / +3000 fallback. Reinforced by the IR assertion that the `Delete` action carries no `optional` flag. |
| Q3071 | choosing an undeletable-but-choosable Digimon still satisfies "if this effect didn't delete" | `counts a chosen but undeletable Datamon as 'didn't delete' (Q3071)` — BT14-062 Datamon (`[All Turns] can't be deleted by your opponent's effects`) stays on the board, opponent trash empty, Gallantmon at 15000 DP with Piercing live                                                    |

The lane-3 DP-maximum ruling cluster (Q3059–Q3061, Guilmon in the stack) is
deliberately not duplicated here.

#### Clause -> test -> IR

##### `[When Digivolving] Delete 1 of your opponent's Digimon with 8000 DP or less`

IR: `effects[0].actions[0]` — `Delete`, `target.filter { controller:
"opponent", kind: ["Digimon"], dp: { op: "lte", value: 8000 } }`, `count: 1`,
no `optional`.

- `digivolves from a Red Lv.5 source for 4 memory and deletes an 8000 DP
Digimon` — the only evolution test that goes through the public `digivolve`
  intent from an inert Red Lv.5 source (BT1-024 MetalTyrannomon). Endpoints:
  stack `["BT1-024"]`, top card `BT19-015`, current DP 12000, opponent battle
  area empty and the victim instance in the opponent's trash, memory
  `10 -> 8` (`-4` evolution cost, `+2` from this card's own [Your Turn]
  clause firing on the deletion it caused), hand exactly the bonus-draw card,
  deck empty, no pending decision.
- `refuses a Lv.4 source and a Blue Lv.5 source` — the illegal-source
  negative: BT1-014 Kokatorimon (Red Lv.4) and BT1-038 Monzaemon (Blue Lv.5)
  both return `{ ok: false, reason: "invalid-evolution" }`, memory and hand
  untouched.
- `leaves a 9000 DP Digimon alone ...` — the 8000/9000 boundary; the 9000 DP
  body keeps its DP and stays on the board.

##### `If this effect didn't delete, ... ＜Piercing＞ and +3000 DP until the end of your opponent's turn`

IR: `effects[0].actions[1..2]` — `GainKeyword` (Piercing) and `ModifyDP`
(+3000), both `duration: "untilOpponentTurnEnd"`, both gated on
`condition.kind: "ifThisEffectDidNotDelete"`, both `isSelf: true` /
`isSelfRef`.

- Three separate "didn't delete" routes, all natural digivolves:
  the 9000 DP out-of-range body, the undeletable Datamon (Q3071), and
  an opponent with no Digimon at all. Each asserts DP 15000, Piercing live,
  and — for the first two — memory unchanged at 6, proving the memory clause
  did not fire.
- `checks security with the granted Piercing after winning a battle, unlike
the deleting branch` — the keyword is proved by its rules consequence, not
  by a flag: Gallantmon (15000, Piercing) beats a suspended 9000 DP Digimon
  and the excess trashes one security card (`securityChecked` fires once,
  security 3 -> 2). The paired control on the same board shape takes the
  deleting branch (a pinned 8000 DP body), so Piercing is absent and the same
  battle leaves security at 3 with zero `securityChecked` events.
- `keeps the +3000 DP through the opponent's turn and loses it at that turn's
end` — the duration is read INSIDE the opponent's open Main phase
  (`runOneTurn` + `advance.waitForMainPhase(1)`): still 15000 with Piercing.
  After that turn closes and continuous effects recompute: 12000, no
  Piercing.

##### `[Your Turn] [Once Per Turn] When an opponent's Digimon is deleted, gain 2 memory`

IR: `effects[1]` — trigger `YourTurn`, `frequency: "OncePerTurn"`, one
`SubTrigger` on `onDeletionOf` with `sourceFilter { controller: "opponent",
kind: ["Digimon"] }` and `GainMemory 2`.

Both tests run on ONE real `engine.startTurnLoop()`, which passes the turn
itself. Nothing in this file writes `state.turnSeat`, and every deletion is a
battle outcome produced by a public `attack` intent — no injected timing and
no `deletePermanent` verb.

- `ignores the deletion of your OWN Digimon without consuming the once-per-turn
window` — proves the `controller: "opponent"` leg. Inside our own open Main:
  our 3000 DP body attacks their suspended 9000 DP body and dies; our trash
  holds exactly that instance and memory stays 0. The window is demonstrably
  untouched, because the very next attack — Gallantmon into their suspended
  2000 DP body — pays out +2 on the same turn.
- `stays silent on the opponent's turn and re-arms on your next own turn` —
  three consecutive turns of the same loop:
  - Turn 1 (ours): we attack the player with a 10000 DP bait body, which
    leaves it suspended and therefore a legal target on their turn. No
    opponent Digimon dies, so the window is still unspent.
  - Turn 2 (THEIRS): their own 3000 DP Digimon attacks the suspended bait
    through a seat-1 `attack` intent and is deleted. That is literally "an
    opponent's Digimon is deleted", but not on our turn: their attacker is
    confirmed gone from their battle area and in their trash, the bait
    survives, and memory is unchanged from the value captured before the
    battle. Their two survivors then attack our 1000 DP security bodies, win,
    and end the turn suspended.
  - Turn 3 (ours): the window is armed again. Gallantmon deletes the first
    suspended body in battle -> memory 0 -> 2. A second attacker deletes the
    second body in the same turn -> memory stays 2 ([Once Per Turn]), with
    both victim instances confirmed in their trash and no pending decision.

  The gate and the reset are proved against each other: the same board, the
  same deletion mechanism, the same clause — only the turn owner differs, and
  only the own-turn deletion pays.

### BT19-016 — Gaossmon

#### Card summary

- Blue Digimon, Lv.3 Rookie, play cost 3, DP 1000, Virus / Reptile /
  Blue Flare.
- Digivolve cost: Blue Lv.2 for 0.
- Printed clause (one clause, two timings): `[On Play] [On Deletion] By
placing 1 [Blue Flare] trait Digimon card from your hand under any of your
Tamers, ＜Draw 1＞.`
- No inherited effect.

#### Q&A ids

`node tools/kb/query.mjs card BT19-016` -> `(no knowledge-base entries)`, and
`docs/audits/BT19-reaudit/KB-INDEX.md` lists BT19-016 with a Q&A count of 0.
Confirmed with the tool, not assumed. No errata, no banlist entry.

The generic rule the card relies on — a "by doing X" cost that cannot be paid
means the effect does nothing — is exercised by the two unpayable-cost tests
below.

#### Clause -> test -> IR

IR: `effects[0]` (`OnPlay`) and `effects[1]` (`OnDeletion`), structurally
identical: one `Draw` action, `controller: "mine"`, `amount: 1`,
`optional: true`, with

```
cost: {
  kind: "place",
  target: { filter: { zone: "hand", controller: "mine", kind: ["Digimon"],
                      nameOrTrait: [{ tokens: ["Blue Flare"], match: "trait" }] },
            count: 1, from: ["hand"] },
  underFilter: { controller: "mine", kind: ["Tamer"] },
}
```

`match: "trait"` is the exact-trait mode the printed `[Blue Flare] trait`
wording requires (not the `traitContains` substring mode); the IR test asserts
it for both timings.

- `pays the cost and draws when played from hand for its play cost` —
  public `playCard` intent. Endpoints: the Tamer's stack holds exactly the
  BT19-020 instance, hand holds exactly the drawn card, deck empty, Gaossmon
  on the board, memory `10 -> 7` (play cost 3), no pending decision.
- `pays the cost and draws when deleted losing a public battle` — the
  `[On Deletion]` half is reached with no injected timing: Gaossmon (1000 DP)
  attacks a suspended 3000 DP body through the public `attack` intent and
  loses. Endpoints: Gaossmon in the trash, only the Tamer left on the board,
  Tamer stack = the placed BT19-020 instance, hand = the drawn card, deck
  empty.
- `may decline the placement cost, drawing nothing and moving no card` —
  `autoDeclineOptional`: Tamer stack empty, hand and deck untouched.
- `cannot pay with a hand Digimon that lacks the [Blue Flare] trait` — the
  near-miss peer BT1-027 Armadillomon (Blue Lv.3 Digimon, Mollusk, no Blue
  Flare) is the only hand card; with `autoAcceptOptional` on, nothing is
  placed and nothing is drawn.
- `cannot pay without a Tamer of your own, even when the opponent has one` —
  proves the `controller: "mine"` leg of `underFilter`: the opponent's
  BT19-081 Kiriha Aonuma is not a legal host, so the cost is unpayable.
- `places under a Tamer and never under a Digimon, whichever Tamer is
chosen` — a Tamer (ST1-12) and a Digimon (BT1-009) are both on the board;
  the card goes under the Tamer and the Digimon's stack stays empty, proving
  the `kind: ["Tamer"]` leg.
- `does nothing from inside a digivolution stack when the host is deleted` —
  the realistic evolution-stack case. Gaossmon sits under an inert Blue Lv.4
  host (BT1-037 Gorillamon); the host loses a public battle and the whole
  stack is trashed. Gaossmon prints no inherited effect, so its
  `[On Deletion]` must stay silent: the Tamer stack stays empty and hand and
  deck are untouched, with both cards confirmed in the trash.

`docs/audits/BT19-AUDIT.md` was not used as evidence.

#### Card summary

- Blue Digimon, Lv.3 Rookie, play cost 3, DP 1000, Vaccine / Tropical Fish /
  Aquatic.
- Digivolve cost: Blue Lv.2 for 0.
- Printed clause 1: `＜Evade＞`
- Printed clause 2: `[Rule] Trait: Has the [Aquatic] type.`
- Printed inherited clause: `＜Jamming＞.`

#### Q&A ids

| id    | ruling                                                                                                     | covered by                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| ----- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Q3074 | the `[Rule]` line is a special rule that always treats this card as also having the `[Aquatic]` type trait | `is Aquatic and has Evade; a plain Blue Lv.3 peer has neither` — `observe.hasEffectiveTrait(swimmon, "Aquatic")` is true and the printed `[Tropical Fish]` type is retained alongside it, while the near-miss BT1-027 Armadillomon reports false. See the caveat under Catalog discrepancies: the catalog already carries `Aquatic` in `types`, so this assertion cannot distinguish a printed type from a `GrantStatic` grant. |

Rules used, from `data/kb/rules/comprehensive.md` via
`node tools/kb/query.mjs rules`:

- §16-22-1 ＜Evade＞: by suspending a Digimon with this effect when it would
  be deleted, the deletion is prevented.
- §16-9-1 ＜Jamming＞: a Digimon with this effect is not deleted as a result
  of a battle with an opponent's Security Digimon (and only that).

#### Clause -> test -> IR

##### `＜Evade＞`

IR: `effects[0]` — `trigger: "Static"`, no actions,
`keywords: [{ keyword: "Evade" }]`. `Static` is correct here: the printed
line is a bare keyword, not a bracketed `[All Turns]` clause.

Proved by its rules consequence through a real opponent effect, never a
flag-only read:

- `survives an opponent's deletion effect by suspending, where the peer is
deleted` — seat 0 digivolves BT19-015 Gallantmon through the public
  `digivolve` intent; its `[When Digivolving] Delete 1 of your opponent's
Digimon with 8000 DP or less` is pinned onto Swimmon with
  `preferInstanceIds`. The engine raises an `evadePrompt`, seat 1 answers with
  the public `respondEvade` intent (`accept: true`), and the endpoints are:
  the same permanent id still on the board, `isSuspended === true`, opponent
  trash empty, battle area still 2, no pending decision.
- `is deleted when its controller declines Evade` — identical board,
  `accept: false`: Swimmon's instance is the only card in the trash and the
  battle area holds only the peer.
- `offers no Evade window for the near-miss peer, which is simply deleted` —
  the near-miss control. BT19-017 Sangomon is the same colour, level and DP
  (Blue Lv.3, 1000) and even prints the same `[Rule] Aquatic` line, but has
  no ＜Evade＞: no `evadePrompt` event is ever emitted and it goes straight to
  the trash while Swimmon is untouched.
- `keeps Evade with the top card only: a host it sits under does not gain
it` — ＜Evade＞ is not inherited; the BT19-019 host with Swimmon underneath
  reports no Evade.

##### `[Rule] Trait: Has the [Aquatic] type.`

IR: `effects[1]` — `trigger: "Rule"`, one `GrantStatic` with
`grant: "trait"`, `tokens: ["Aquatic"]`, `target.filter.isSelfRef: true`.

- `is Aquatic and has Evade; a plain Blue Lv.3 peer has neither` — Swimmon is
  Aquatic and still Tropical Fish; the near-miss BT1-027 Armadillomon (Blue
  Lv.3, Mollusk) is not, which proves the grant is self-scoped rather than
  board-wide.

##### Inherited `＜Jamming＞.`

IR: `effects[2]` — `isInherited: true`, `keywords: [{ keyword: "Jamming" }]`,
and the suite asserts this is the ONLY inherited effect on the card.

- `gives its evolution host inherited Jamming, which survives a lost security
battle` — the realistic evolution stack: BT19-019 Shellmon (Blue Lv.4,
  4000 DP, the printed digivolution line for Swimmon) with Swimmon as its
  digivolution card, attacking the player through the public `attack` intent
  into a security stack whose top card is a 5000 DP Security Digimon. The
  host loses the battle and survives (§16-9-1): host still on the board, own
  trash empty, the Security Digimon in the opponent's trash, no pending
  decision. The paired control is the same host with the near-miss BT19-017
  underneath instead — no Jamming, and it is deleted by the same battle.
- `does not extend Jamming to an ordinary Digimon battle` — the clause-scope
  proof. The same Jamming host attacks a suspended 5000 DP opponent Digimon
  and IS deleted, because §16-9-1 covers only battles against Security
  Digimon.
- `keeps Evade with the top card only ...` — the mirror direction: the host
  has Jamming and no Evade, the standalone Swimmon has Evade and no Jamming.

#### Card

Blue/Black Lv.4 Champion, Virus, [Dinosaur]/[Blue Flare], 5000 DP, play cost 5.
Digivolves from a Blue Lv.3 for 3 or a Black Lv.3 for 3.

Printed clauses:

1. `＜Rush＞`
2. `[On Deletion] If you have 1 or fewer Tamers, you may play 1 [Kiriha Aonuma] from your
hand without paying the cost.`
3. `Then, ＜Save＞.`
4. Inherited: `＜Reboot＞.`

#### Q&A covered

| Q4714 | The part after "then" is processed even when the "if" condition fails (2+ Tamers).        | `skips the play with 2 Tamers in play but still Saves to the stack bottom (Q4714, CR 4-3-2)` |

Q4714's question text says "[When Digivolving]"; its answer names this card's [On Deletion]
effect. The answer is what was tested — the card prints no [When Digivolving] clause.

#### Clause -> test -> IR

| Clause                                            | Test                                                                                                                                                           | IR                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| ------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| ＜Rush＞                                          | `attacks the turn it arrives while a plain peer that arrived with it may not`                                                                                  | `effects[0]` `Static` + `keywords: [Rush]`                                                                                                                                                            |
| [On Deletion] play [Kiriha Aonuma] free, ≤1 Tamer | `plays Kiriha ... (Q3076)`, `skips the play with 2 Tamers ... (Q4714)`, `plays <id> from hand: <bool>` (4 cases), `may decline ...`, `does nothing at all ...` | `effects[1].actions[0]` `PlayWithoutCost`, `payCost:false`, `from:["hand"]`, `optional:true`, `nameOrTrait[{match:"nameExact"}]`, `condition youHave {kind:["Tamer"], zone:"battleArea", countMax:1}` |
| Then, ＜Save＞                                    | every [On Deletion] test; bottom placement asserted in the Q4714 test                                                                                          | `effects[1].actions[1]` `PlaceUnder` `optional:true` + effect-level `keywords:[Save]`                                                                                                                 |
| Inherited ＜Reboot＞                              | `grants inherited ＜Reboot＞ only to the host it sits under`, `actually unsuspends its host during the opponent's unsuspend phase`                             | `effects[2]` `Static`, `isInherited:true`, `keywords:[Reboot]`                                                                                                                                        |
| Digivolution costs                                | `digivolves from a %s source for 3 with the bonus draw` (Blue Lv.3 / Black Lv.3), `refuses an illegal Green Lv.3 source`                                       | catalog `evoCosts`                                                                                                                                                                                    |

#### Defects fixed locally (IR changed — resync needed)

1. `match: "name"` (substring) for the bracketed exact `[Kiriha Aonuma]` ref -> `nameExact`.
   No catalog fixture discriminates the two modes for this token (the only card whose name
   CONTAINS "Kiriha Aonuma", EX4-062, prints "The name of this card/Tamer is also treated as
   [Kiriha Aonuma]/[Nene Amano]", so it satisfies the exact gate legitimately). The fix is
   therefore correctness-of-IR, not a behaviour change; the peer table pins both the
   qualifying and non-qualifying halves so a future regression to substring matching that
   DOES change behaviour is caught.
2. The `Then, ＜Save＞` placement carried `abortOnDecline: true` and no `optional` and no
   `keywords: [{ keyword: "Save" }]`. `abortOnDecline` on the last action of an effect is
   dead, so the ＜Save＞ was mandatory (comprehensive 16-20-3 makes it optional), and without
   the keyword the registration normalizer
   (`apps/api/src/engine/effects/interpreter/registration/normalize.ts`,
   `withSavePlacementDefaults`) did not default the `PlaceUnder` to `position: "bottom"`.
   The card therefore landed directly beneath the Tamer instead of at the stack bottom,
   inverting the order comprehensive 4-3-2 requires. Both confirmed red before the fix:
   removing the `keywords` block again fails `compiles every printed clause` and the
   bottom-placement assertion in the Q4714 test.
3. `condition.filter` for "you have 1 or fewer Tamers" gained `zone: "battleArea"` so the
   count cannot pick up permanents outside the battle area.

### BT19-023 — Huankunmon
