#### Card summary

Catalog (`packages/shared/src/cards/data/cards.json`): Blue Digimon, Lv5, Ultimate,
Vaccine, `[Aquatic]`, play cost 7, DP 7000, evoCosts Blue Lv4 at 3 memory, rarity C,
max 4 per deck.

Printed clauses:

1. `＜Blocker＞`
2. `[On Play] [When Digivolving] 1 of your Digimon can't be deleted by battle until
the end of your opponent's turn.`
3. Inherited: `[Your Turn] This Digimon's attack target can't be switched.`

No U+00A0 in either text field for this card (unlike BT19-024); the catalog test
asserts the exact bytes.

#### Q&A ids

`node tools/kb/query.mjs card BT19-023` → `(no knowledge-base entries)`, matching
`KB-INDEX.md` (Q&A count 0, no errata, not on the banlist). Confirmed with the tool
rather than assumed. No card-specific rulings to cover; the clauses are audited
against the comprehensive rules instead (CR §12-1-1 for the block/target-switch
interaction, §16-5 for ＜Blocker＞).

#### Clause → test → IR

- Clause 1 (`＜Blocker＞`) → `effects[0]`, `trigger: "Static"`,
  `keywords: [{ keyword: "Blocker" }]`, no actions.
  - Behaviour: `blocks a real attack on the player, and a peer without ＜Blocker＞
cannot`. Seat 1 declares a real `attack` on the player; the engine opens a block
    window; `declareBlock` with the inert 3000 DP Monodramon peer is REJECTED
    (`ok: false`), `declareBlock` with Huankunmon is accepted, and the redirected
    7000-vs-3000 battle deletes the attacker. Endpoints: seat 1 battle area empty,
    seat 0 battle area `["BT1-009","BT19-023"]`, Huankunmon suspended, seat 0
    security still 1, no pending decision.
  - Near-miss on grant scope: `does not grant ＜Blocker＞ to another Digimon`.
- Clause 2 (`[On Play]`/`[When Digivolving]` battle-deletion protection) →
  `effects[1]`/`effects[2]`, `Restrict` `beDeletedInBattle`, target
  `{ controller: "mine", kind: ["Digimon"] }` count 1 (permanent targeting, so the
  battle area), `duration: "untilOpponentTurnEnd"` (a real `EffectDurationRef`,
  `packages/shared/src/effects/ir/durations.ts:8`).
  - `[On Play] protects the chosen Digimon through a real losing battle on the
opponent's turn`: real `playCard` intent (memory 10 → 3), the protection pinned
    onto one of two identical 3000 DP peers via `preferInstanceIds`. Then TWO real
    opponent attacks on the opponent's turn, each 12000 vs 3000, each declining the
    block window Huankunmon opens. The shielded peer survives with an empty trash;
    the exposed peer is deleted by the identical battle. Endpoints: trash
    `["BT1-009"]`, board `["BT1-009","BT19-023"]`, no pending decision.
  - `[When Digivolving] protects one Digimon, and the protection expires at the end
of the opponent's turn`: real `digivolve` intent from Blue Lv4 Xiquemon
    (BT19-021). Endpoints: memory 5 → 2 (the printed Blue Lv4 cost 3), stack
    `["BT19-021"]`, hand holds exactly the digivolve draw, restriction on the chosen
    peer only. The restriction is then asserted STILL ARMED while the opponent's turn
    is open, and GONE after `advance(s.engine).runTurn(1)` — the real turn loop, not
    an injected duration tick.
- Clause 3 (inherited `[Your Turn]` attack target can't be switched) → `effects[3]`,
  `trigger: "YourTurn"`, `isInherited: true`, `Restrict` `attackTargetChange` on
  `{ isSelfRef: true, isSelf: true }`, `duration: "permanent"` (re-derived每
  continuous pass and turn-gated by the `YourTurn` trigger).
  - `forbids an opposing ＜Blocker＞ from switching the target, unlike an identical
host without it`: two identical Kokatorimon hosts, one with BT19-023 in its
    digivolution cards. The restricted host attacks the player: NO
    `blockWindowOpened` event ever fires, MailBirdramon (printed ＜Blocker＞) stays
    unsuspended, and security drops by one. The plain host attacks: the SAME blocker
    opens a window, `declareBlock` succeeds, and the 12000-vs-5000 battle deletes it.
    This is the rules consequence (`combat/legality.ts:368` — a block IS an
    attack-target switch, CR §12-1-1), not a keyword flag read.
  - `does not restrict the host on the opponent's turn` — the `[Your Turn]` gate.
- Evolution: `refuses an illegal source: Blue Lv.3 and Red Lv.4 both fail the Blue

### BT19-024 — MarineBullmon

all injected timing.

#### Card summary

Catalog: Blue Digimon, Lv5, Ultimate, Data, `[Mollusk]/[LIBERATOR]/[Aquatic]`, play
cost 7, DP 7000, evoCosts Blue Lv4 at 3 memory, rarity R, max 4 per deck.

Printed clauses:

1. `＜Decode (Blue Lv.4)＞` — "When this Digimon would leave the battle area other
   than in battle, you may play 1 Blue Level 4 Digimon card from its digivolution
   cards without paying the cost."
2. `[On Play] [When Digivolving] You may place 1 Digimon card with [Aqua]/[Sea
Animal] in one of its traits from your hand as 1 of your Digimon's bottom
digivolution card.`
3. `[Rule] Trait: Has the [Aquatic] type.`
4. Inherited: `[End of Attack] [Once Per Turn] You may play 1 level 4 or lower
Digimon card with [Aqua]/[Sea Animal] in one of its traits from this Digimon's
digivolution cards without paying the cost.`

Both text fields contain U+00A0 immediately after `[Sea Animal]`; the catalog test
asserts the exact bytes (` in one of its traits`).

#### Q&A ids

| Id                                                                                   | Covered by                                                                                |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Q3058 (＜Decode＞ interrupts Puyoyomon's inherited return; the bounce still happens) | `interrupts Puyoyomon's inherited return and plays the Blue Lv.4 source for free (Q3058)` |
| Q3078 (the `[Rule]` always treats the card as having `[Aquatic]`)                    | `is always [Aquatic] and therefore feeds another card's [Aqua] trait filter`              |

#### Verification of the prior audit's ＜Decode＞ scoping claim

The prior audit restricted playback to the source Digimon's OWN stack. That is
CORRECT, and it was verified rather than trusted:

- Comprehensive rules 16-36-1: "you may play 1 specified Digimon card from **that
  Digimon's** digivolution cards". 16-36-2 makes it an immediate-type effect on the
  would-leave event; 16-36-3 makes the processing optional.
- Q3058's answer describes exactly this: ＜Decode＞ interrupts the inherited return,
  MarineBullmon still goes to the bottom of the deck, and the opponent's Digimon is
  still returned to hand — the bounce belongs to Puyoyomon's effect, not to Decode.
- Engine seam: the IR expresses the scoping as `target.filter.isSelfRef: true` with
  `from: ["digivolutionCards"]`. `targeting/loose.ts:385-393` reads `isSelfRef` on a
  hosted zone as "the candidate's host permanent IS the source permanent", so the
  neighbouring stacks are excluded. This is asserted behaviourally, not just read.

#### Clause → test → IR

- Clause 1 (＜Decode＞) → `effects[0]` keyword declaration (`trigger: "Static"`) plus
  `effects[4]`: `trigger: "AllTurns"`, `Replacement` with
  `event: "wouldLeavePlay"`, `leaveCause: "otherThanBattle"`,
  `sourceFilter: { isSelfRef: true }`, action `PlayWithoutCost` from
  `["digivolutionCards"]`, `payCost: false`, `playedByDecode: true`,
  `optional: true`, filter `{ isSelfRef: true, colors: ["Blue"],
levelComparison: { op: "eq", value: 4 } }`.
  - Positive (Q3058, real flow): seat 1 declares a real `attack`; Puyoyomon
    (BT19-002) in MarineBullmon's stack offers its `[Opponent's Turn]` effect, whose
    cost returns MarineBullmon to the bottom of the deck — a non-battle leave.
    Endpoints: MarineBullmon is the LAST card of a 3-card deck; Shellmon (BT19-019)
    is on the battle area with an empty stack; the Digi-Egg goes to the trash; the
    pinned level-3 opposing Digimon is in the opponent's hand; no pending decision.
  - Optionality (CR 16-36-3): `is optional: declining ＜Decode＞ trashes the Blue Lv.4
source instead`. The two nested optionals are answered individually through real
    `respondDecision` intents (yes to Puyoyomon, no to Decode) because one shared
    auto-responder cannot express that. Endpoints: MarineBullmon at the deck bottom,
    battle area EMPTY, trash `["BT19-002","BT19-019"]`.
  - Battle-leave negative: `does not activate when the leave IS a battle deletion`.
    A real 12000-vs-7000 attack on the suspended MarineBullmon; both cards land in
    the trash and nothing is played.
  - Filter and scope near-misses: `reads only its OWN digivolution cards, and only a
Blue Lv.4 one`. Its own stack holds Swimmon (Blue **Lv3**) and Kokatorimon
    (**Red** Lv4); a neighbouring Xiquemon holds the Blue Lv4 Shellmon. After the
    same real Puyoyomon route, nothing is played, the neighbour's stack is intact
    (`["BT19-019"]`), and all three of its own stack cards are in the trash.
- Clause 2 (`[On Play]`/`[When Digivolving]` bottom placement) → `effects[1]`/
  `effects[2]`, `PlaceUnder`, `optional: true`, `position: "bottom"`,
  target `from: ["hand"]` with
  `nameOrTrait: [{ tokens: ["Aqua","Sea Animal"], match: "traitContains" }]`,
  `underFilter: { controller: "mine", kind: ["Digimon"] }`.
  - `[On Play] places the chosen [Aqua] hand card under another of my Digimon and
leaves the near-miss in hand`: real `playCard` (memory 10 → 3). Endpoints: the
    target stack is `["BT19-018","BT19-019"]` — Swimmon landed BELOW the Shellmon
    already there, proving "bottom"; the `[Mini Dragon]` Monodramon stays in hand.
  - `[On Play] is optional: declining leaves both hand cards untouched`
    (`autoDeclineOptional`).
  - `[When Digivolving] places the card under the digivolving stack on the legal Blue
Lv.4 route`: real `digivolve` from Shellmon. Endpoints: top card BT19-024, stack
    `["BT19-018","BT19-019"]`, memory 5 → 2, hand holds exactly the digivolve draw.
  - Illegal source: `refuses an illegal evolution source` — Blue Lv3 and Red Lv4 are
    both rejected with board, hand and memory unchanged.
- Clause 3 (`[Rule]` `[Aquatic]`) → `effects[3]`, `trigger: "Rule"`, `GrantStatic`
  `grant: "trait"`, `tokens: ["Aquatic"]` on `{ isSelfRef: true }`.
  - `is always [Aquatic] and therefore feeds another card's [Aqua] trait filter`
    (Q3078): one MarineBullmon's `[On Play]` selects a SECOND MarineBullmon out of
    hand as an `[Aqua]`-trait Digimon card and places it as a digivolution card; the
    played permanent also reports the effective trait.
- Clause 4 (inherited `[End of Attack] [Once Per Turn]`) → `effects[5]`,
  `trigger: "EndOfAttack"`, `isInherited: true`, `frequency: "OncePerTurn"`,
  `PlayWithoutCost` from `["digivolutionCards"]` with `isSelfRef: true`,
  `levelComparison: { op: "lte", value: 4 }` and the same `traitContains` pair.
  - `plays exactly one eligible source per attack from its real host's stack, and the
counter resets on my next turn`: a real Xiquemon host whose stack is
    `[BT19-024, BT19-018, BT19-018, BT1-009]` declares a real `attack` on the player.
    One Swimmon is played for free; the Red `[Mini Dragon]` Monodramon and the Lv5
    MarineBullmon itself are never candidates. After a full opponent turn through
    `advance(s.engine).runTurn(1)`, the host attacks again and the SECOND Swimmon is
    played — the once-per-turn counter reset. Endpoints on stack contents, board
    contents and security count at each step.

#### Trait matching — catalog finding, not a defect

The IR matches `[Aqua]`/`[Sea Animal]` with `traitContains` (substring,
case-insensitive). That is the brief's rule for "with [X] in any of its traits", and
the catalog confirms it is the only workable reading here: **no card in the catalog
carries a bare `Aqua` trait** (0 cards), while 61 carry `Aquatic` and 12 carry
`Sea Animal`. The English `[Aqua]` token is exported as `Aquatic`. An exact trait
match would make clause 2 and clause 4 dead text. Recorded in a comment at the top of
the test file.

#### Defects found

None requiring an IR change. The module is a hand-fixed file whose header comment
already states the Q3058 reading, and that reading checks out against CR 16-36-1 and
the Q&A text. Checked against the brief's trap list: no `match: "name"` on a bracketed
name; the `[All Turns]` semantics of ＜Decode＞ use `trigger: "AllTurns"` (not
`Static`) on the replacement, with `Static` used only for the keyword declaration; the
`[Rule]` line has a `Rule`/`GrantStatic` node; the `levelComparison` object form IS
read for loose `digivolutionCards` candidates (`matching/definition.ts:135-142`), so
the lane-6 `playCost: { op, value }` trap does not apply here.

The prior test file proved ＜Decode＞ with `advance().fireSubTrigger` and
`advance().verb.deletePermanent`/`returnToHand`, the placement clauses with
`advance().fireForPermanent`, and the inherited clause with `fireForPermanent` twice.
All of that is gone: the current file contains no `advance.fire*` and no
`advance.verb` call.

#### Remaining gaps

- **Same-turn refusal of clause 4 is unreachable from public intents.** CR §11-2-3
  (`engine/actions/attack.ts:93` — `deps.attackedThisTurn`) caps each Digimon at one
  attack per turn, so an `[End of Attack] [Once Per Turn]` clause cannot be offered
  twice in a turn without an extra-attack grant, and no such grant is in this lane's
  fixture set. The reset across a real turn boundary IS proved. This is a rules
  limit, not an engine gap; nothing is retained red for it.
- The `[Rule]` node is behaviourally redundant with the catalog, which already lists
  `Aquatic` in `types`. The test proves the card is treated as `[Aquatic]` and that
  another card's `[Aqua]` filter accepts it, but it cannot isolate the grant from the
  printed trait.
- Clause 2's `underFilter` allows placing under MarineBullmon itself; only the
  "another of your Digimon" case is exercised.
- In `reads only its OWN digivolution cards…` the attacker's security check does not
  land within the settle window, so that test asserts the trash contents and the
  neighbour's stack rather than the security count. Not a defect in this card.

#### Cross-lane dependency

The ＜Decode＞ tests drive the leave event through **BT19-002 Puyoyomon**, which is
lane 1's card. It is at base and unmodified by me. If lane 1 changes BT19-002's IR,
three tests here (`Q3058`, the decline test and the own-stack test) may need their
fixture rechecked.

| Q3080 (exposed Tamer does not count)              | `does not bounce when ＜De-Digivolve＞ exposes a Tamer, leaving only 1 opposing Digimon (Q3080)`               |
| Q3081 (which cards the On Deletion play may take) | `[On Deletion] plays an eligible cost-5-or-less [Blue Flare]/[Xros Heart] card, then ＜Save＞s itself (Q3081)` |

Q3079 and Q3080 are the two halves of the same gate and are proved against the
same fixture shape, differing only in what `＜De-Digivolve 2＞` exposes: a Digi-Egg
(counts — the bounce resolves, then the Digi-Egg is trashed by rule processing)
versus a Tamer (does not count — no bounce, both opposing permanents remain).
Q3081 is proved as an OR over the two traits plus the cost-5 gate, with a
wrong-trait peer (BT19-021) and a right-trait-wrong-cost peer (BT19-025, cost 7)
left under the Tamer.

#### Defect fixed locally (IR CHANGED — resync needed)

The `OnDeletion` `PlaceUnder` is the printed `＜Save＞` keyword. The module carried
it as `optional: false` with no keyword declaration, and its header comment
asserted `＜Save＞` is mandatory. Comprehensive 16-20-3 says the processing from
`＜Save＞` is optional, and 4-22 makes the declared keyword the handle other cards
use for "a card with `＜Save＞` in its text". Fixed to `optional: true` plus
`keywords: [{ keyword: "Save", raw: "＜Save＞" }]`, matching the accepted BT19-008
shape. `BT19-026.ts` also gained `export` on `compiled`.

**This changes the IR**, so the persisted record in
`packages/shared/src/effects/effects.json` is stale for BT19-026 and
`BT19-catalog-sync.test.ts` will fail for that card until the coordinator resyncs.

The prior test suite proved `[On Play]`, `[When Digivolving]`, Q3079 and Q3080
only through `advance.fire*` injected timings, and its "declining the optional
source play still performs the independent Save" case relied on the blanket
`autoDeclineOptional` flag, which could not have distinguished a mandatory Save
from an optional one. Every clause is now driven by `playCard`, `digivolve`, a
real deletion or the real turn loop, and the two OnDeletion optionals are
answered individually by a small in-test decision script.

Verified as CORRECT (no change required):

- `AllTurns`, not `Static`, for the printed `[All Turns]` line.
- `duration: "permanent"` is a real `EffectDurationRef` (`ir/durations.ts`), so it
  does not silently expire at turn end.
- `playCostLte: 5` is the loose-card key form; the object form
  `playCost: { op, value }` would have been dropped (lane 6's BT19-013 trap).
- `zone: "underTamers"` on the target filter plus `from: ["underTamers"]` are
  consistent; `underTamers` is a zone alias for `underMyTamers`
  (`targeting/loose.ts:95-113`).

#### Remaining gaps

- `＜Save＞` places ZeigGreymon BENEATH the Tamer's existing digivolution cards.
  The tests assert that order, but no KB ruling states it for `＜Save＞` itself —
  comprehensive 16-21-6 states it only for `＜Material Save＞`. Recorded as engine
  behaviour, not as a proven rule.
- The `[On Deletion]` window is opened with `advance.verb.deletePermanent(...,
"byEffect")`. That is the production deletion primitive, not an injected
  timing, but the deletion is not sourced from another card's printed effect.
- The "2 or more Digimon" count is taken from the opponent's battle area only
  (`actions/digivolution.ts:51`); no ruling in this card's KB set exercises an
  opponent breeding-area Digimon, so that boundary is untested.

#### Catalog discrepancies

  the word "trait" is duplicated. The official line prints it once. Reported, not
  edited; the test asserts the catalog string as stored so the discrepancy stays
  visible.
- `effectText` stores one U+00A0 (non-breaking space); the test normalizes.

#### The prior audit's Decode scoping — verified, not assumed

The task asked whether restricting ＜Decode＞ playback to the source Digimon's own
stack is right. It is, on two independent grounds:

- Printed text: "from **its** digivolution cards".
- KB `data/kb/rules/comprehensive.md` §16-36-1 (via `node tools/kb/query.mjs rules
"Decode"`): "you may play 1 specified Digimon card from **that Digimon's**
  digivolution cards without paying the cost". §16-36-2 makes it an immediate-type
  effect on "would leave the battle area other than by a battle"; §16-36-3 makes it
  optional.

The IR encodes the scope as `target.filter.isSelfRef: true` on a
`from: ["digivolutionCards"]` pool. In a hosted zone that key means "host permanent
is the source", not "this instance"
(`interpreter/targeting/loose.ts:230` and `:389-393`). The engine additionally
force-scopes any `playedByDecode` play that names no host
(`interpreter/actions/play.ts:102-110`, `applyDecodeHostScope`), so the encoding is
belt-and-braces rather than wrong. The exemplar EX12-016 spells the same scope as
`hostFilter: { isSelfRef: true }`; both reach the same predicate, so I did not churn
the IR to match style. The scoping is now proved behaviourally against a second own
stack holding a legal Blue Lv.5 (see the Q3083 test below).

#### Q&A ids

#### Name / trait semantics — checked, not assumed

The printed gate is "with `[Aqua]`/`[Sea Animal]` **in one of its traits**", which is
the SUBSTRING form (the exact form is "with the [X] trait"). The IR uses
`nameOrTrait: [{ tokens: ["Aqua", "Sea Animal"], match: "traitContains" }]`, which is
the right key: `interpreter/matching/definition.ts:365` implements `traitContains` as
`traits.some(x => x.includes(token))` after `normalizeTrait` lower-cases and strips
whitespace and hyphens.

Consequences, confirmed against the catalog's actual trait vocabulary
(`Ancient Aquabeast`, `Aquabeast`, `Aquatic`, `Sea Animal`, `Sea Beast`):

- `"aquatic"` and `"aquabeast"` both contain `"aqua"` -> both QUALIFY. There is no
  trait literally named `Aqua`, which is why the printed wording is the substring
  form at all.
- `"seabeast"` does not contain `"seaanimal"` and contains no `"aqua"` -> [Sea Beast]
  does NOT qualify. This is the near-miss the brief called for, and it is now a real
  assertion rather than an argument.

Engine limitation noted while reading the seam, NOT a defect of this card: the
live-permanent path that unions continuously GRANTED traits into a trait predicate
(`interpreter/matching/permanent.ts:683-697`) only handles `match: "trait"`, not
`match: "traitContains"`. A trait granted at runtime would therefore be invisible to
this clause. It does not bite here because every qualifying trait in these fixtures is
printed in `cards.json` (including BT19-027's [Aquatic], see the discrepancy section).
Flagged for the coordinator as an engine-wide seam, not fixed from this lane.

#### Clause -> test -> IR

#### Peer / stack evidence

- Realistic evolution stack: BT2-027 Zudomon already carries BT1-030 Gomamon, and
  after the placement the stack is asserted in full order
  `["BT1-033", "BT1-030", "BT2-027"]` — the placed card at the BOTTOM, beneath the
  card's own natural digivolution sources. Position, not just membership.
- Near-miss peer, actively preferred: BT2-025 Ikkakumon [Sea Beast] is first in
  `preferInstanceIds` in the substring test and is still refused for the placement
  while remaining a legal UNSUSPEND target — so the refusal is the trait gate, not
  target scarcity.
- Positive substring peers: BT9-027 Divermon [Aquabeast] and BT19-027 Ryugumon
  [Aquatic] both qualify through `"aqua"`, and BT19-027 is the one actually placed.
- "your OTHER Digimon": the two clauses land on two different permanents in the main
  test (unsuspend the [Sea Beast] peer, place the [Sea Animal] one), and the source
  itself is never the placement cost.
- Keyword leak: the BT2-027 peer standing beside Xiangpengmon has
  `keywordAmount(SecurityAttack) === 0`, no ＜Blocker＞ and no [Aquatic] — and the
  ＜Blocker＞ leak is proved by a REFUSED `declareBlock`, not only by an observe read.

#### Defects found and fixed

None in the module.

What the PRIOR test file did wrong (rewritten, not preserved):

- ＜Security Attack +1＞ and ＜Blocker＞ were proved only by `observe(...)` reads.
  Per the brief, a keyword must be proved by its rules consequence; both are now
  proved by a real attack (two security checks) and a real block declaration (with a
  refused non-Blocker peer).
- Two of its four tests drove `advance.fireForPermanent(WhenDigivolving, …)`,
  injected timing, so the `[When Digivolving]` window was never entered through a real
  digivolution.
- No near-miss peer for the `[Aqua]`/`[Sea Animal]` substring gate — BT19-015
  Gallantmon was used as the "non-matching" card, which is a Red Lv.6 that also fails
  half a dozen other ways. The [Sea Beast] near-miss (the one case the substring rule
  actually turns on) was untested.
- The placement position was asserted as `stack` equality on a one-card stack, which
  cannot tell "bottom" from "top". It is now asserted on a two-card pre-existing stack.
- No illegal-source negative.

#### Retained reds

None. All 9 tests are green.

#### Remaining gaps

- The `[Rule]` `GrantStatic` node cannot be observed in ISOLATION for the same reason
  as BT19-027: the catalog already prints `Aquatic` in `types`. Its cross-card
  consequence is proved; the node itself is asserted structurally only.
- `match: "traitContains"` does not read runtime-GRANTED traits
  (`matching/permanent.ts:683-697` only unions granted traits for `match: "trait"`).
  Unreachable from this card's fixtures, but it means a future card that GRANTS
  [Aquatic] to a Digimon would not be placeable by this clause. Engine seam, out of
  lane.

#### Catalog discrepancies (reported, not edited)

`cards.json` gives BT19-028 `types: ["Holy Bird", "Aquatic"]`. Q3086 says the
`[Rule]` line treats the card "as if it **also** has the [Aquatic] type trait", so
[Aquatic] should not be on the printed type line — the catalog has folded the Rule
into `types`. Behaviourally identical, but it makes the `GrantStatic` node redundant.
Identical pattern on BT19-027 and BT19-019.

### BT19-029 — Tapirmon

Lane 13. Base `23eee9e5a`, branch `audit-bt19-reaudit`. **Module IR changed**
(`sourceFilter.isSelfRef: true` added), so `packages/shared/src/effects/effects.json`
is stale for this card and `BT19-catalog-sync.test.ts` will fail until the
coordinator resyncs. Test file rewritten to real-flow proof.

#### Card summary

Catalog (`packages/shared/src/cards/data/cards.json`): Yellow Digimon, Lv.3,
Rookie, Vaccine, Holy Beast, play cost 3, DP 1000, `evoCosts` Yellow Lv.2 at 0
memory, rarity C, `maxCountInDeck` 4. No `[Digivolve]` alternate route.

Printed clauses:

1. `[On Play] By trashing your top security card, gain 1 memory.`
2. Inherited: `[All Turns] [Once Per Turn] When this yellow Digimon with the
[Data]/[Witchelny] trait would leave the battle area by your opponent's
effects, by trashing your top security card, it doesn't leave.`

The catalog stores U+00A0 after "trait" in the inherited text; the catalog test
compares on normalized whitespace and says so.

#### Q&A ids

| Id                                                                 | Covered by                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Q3087 (only the Digimon carrying this card is protected)           | `protects only the Digimon carrying this card, not a matching sibling (Q3087)` — two yellow [Data] Lv.4 permanents, only one with Tapirmon underneath; the opponent's Volcanic Flare deletes the sibling and no security is paid. Also the trait/colour near-miss pair. |
| Q3095 (simultaneous would-leave effects, player chooses the order) | `lets the player order simultaneous would-leave effects, resolving <id> first (Q3095)` — BT19-041 Dynasmon (yellow [Data]) carrying BT19-029; `preferTriggerKeys` picks each branch and the two orders produce different, asserted security/trash contents.             |

#### Clause -> test -> IR

- Clause 1 -> `effects[0]`: `trigger: "OnPlay"`, `GainMemory` amount 1,
  `optional: true`, `cost.kind: "trash"` with
  `filter { controller: "mine", zone: "security", position: "top" }`.
  - `pays the printed On Play cost from a real hand play and gains exactly 1
memory` — public `playCard` intent. Endpoints: memory 5 -> 3 (3 play cost, +1
    effect), security left as exactly `secNext` and still face down, trash exactly
    `secTop`, hand left as the spare card, battle area exactly BT19-029,
    `assertNoLoudGap`.
  - `declining the optional On Play ...` — `autoDeclineOptional`: memory 5 -> 2,
    both security cards in printed order, empty trash.
  - `gains no memory when the security stack is empty ...` — unpayable cost, memory
    5 -> 2, no trash.
- Evolution (printed `evoCosts` only; no alternate/DNA/App Fusion route exists).
  - `publicly digivolves from a yellow Lv.2 source for the printed cost of 0` —
    ST22-01 Viximon in breeding, `digivolve` intent, memory stays 0, stack identity
    `[viximon]`, the digivolution bonus draw is the only hand card and the deck is
    emptied, and no On Play cost is paid (security untouched).
  - `refuses an illegal off-colour Lv.2 source and an illegal same-level source` —
    red BT1-001 Yokomon in breeding and a Lv.3 BT19-029 on the board are both
    rejected; hand, breeding top and memory unchanged.
- Clause 2 -> `effects[1]`: `trigger: "AllTurns"`, `isInherited: true`,
  `frequency: "OncePerTurn"`, `Replacement` with `event: "wouldLeavePlay"`,
  `leaveCause: "opponentEffect"`, `sourceFilter { isSelfRef: true, controllerDefault:
"mine", kind: ["Digimon"], colors: ["Yellow"], nameOrTrait: [Data | Witchelny,
match "trait"] }`, `cost` = trash the top security card.
  - Positive, both trait tokens: `prevents an opponent effect from removing a yellow
BT3-037/BT26-022 host ...`. The removal is a real BT2-091 Volcanic Flare played
    from the opponent's hand during the opponent's own Main phase inside
    `startTurnLoop`. Endpoints: host still on the board with its Tapirmon
    digivolution card, trash exactly the top security card, security exactly the
    remaining card.
  - Cost decline: `declining the prevention lets the opponent's effect delete the
host and pays nothing` — security untouched, host and Tapirmon both in trash.
  - Once per turn: `prevents only once per turn ...` asserts the intermediate state
    after the first Flare (host alive, one security paid) and then the second Flare
    in the SAME opponent turn deleting the host with no further payment.
  - Reset: `re-arms the once-per-turn prevention on the opponent's following turn`
    — three real turns through the loop; the second opponent turn prevents again.
  - Cause gate: `does not prevent a battle deletion ...` — a real attack into a
    20000 DP opponent Digimon deletes the host; nothing is paid.
  - Near misses: `does not protect BT1-051 (yellow Vaccine, neither trait)` and
    `does not protect BT1-014 (red [Data], not yellow)`.

#### Defect fixed locally

`sourceFilter` had no self-gate. `interpreter/actions/replacement.ts:238-241`
computes `protectsSelf` from `target.isSelf` / `filter.isSelfRef`; with neither
present the reaction installs with `protectsSelf === false` and falls to the
generic branch, which gates only on `protectsFilter.controller` — undefined here
(only `controllerDefault` was set). The clause therefore protected EVERY yellow
[Data]/[Witchelny] Digimon on either seat, contradicting Q3087. Adding
`isSelfRef: true` restores the printed "this Digimon" scope.

Verified load-bearing: with the line commented out, the Q3087 test fails
(`settle` never sees the sibling leave the board).

- The "would leave" wording covers bounce/return as well as deletion; only the

#### Defect fixed locally

`[Rika Nonaka]/[Calumon]` is a bracketed EXACT name reference, but the condition
used `match: "name"` — the substring gate (`interpreter/matching/definition.ts:360`
vs `:363`). Corrected to `nameExact`.

Honest limitation: the current catalog holds no card whose name CONTAINS
"Rika Nonaka" or "Calumon" as a proper substring, so the two modes are not
behaviourally distinguishable today. The change is a text-fidelity correction that
prevents a future longer-named card (a "Rika Nonaka & X" Tamer, the shape that
already exists for Tai Kamiya) from wrongly satisfying the condition. The
near-miss test proves the gate is a name gate at all, not the exact/substring
split.

#### Remaining gaps

- Q5462's discriminating case (original use cost >= 2, cost TO PAY reduced to 1 or
  less, trigger still fires) has no implemented card: every implemented
  payment-only reducer (BT26-098, BT10-103, BT10-098, BT21-093, P-219, EX5-072)
  leaves the paid cost at 3 or more, so the reduced and unreduced values both clear
  the printed threshold. The free-use test covers the same rule at the extreme
  (paid 0).
- Engine observation, not a defect of this card: cards printed "When you would use
  this card, reduce its use cost by N" (BT21-093, P-219, EX5-072) compile onto the
  `BeforePayCost` payment path, while "Reduce the memory cost of this card in your
  hand" (BT2-099, BT8-097) compile onto `wouldBePlayedSelfReducers`, which is the
  path `optionUseCost` reads. Q5461 treats both wordings as use-cost reductions. No
  implemented card of the first family can cross the "2 or more" line, so nothing is
  observable here; flagged for whoever owns `GameEngine.projectLooseUseCost`.
- External "reduce the play cost of your Option cards" effects fold into
  `modifiers.playCostFor`, which `projectLooseUseCost` also reads, so such an effect
  would lower the notified USE cost. Q5462 says a cost-to-pay reduction must not.
  No implemented card exercises it, so no test was written.

#### Catalog discrepancies

`inheritedEffectText` is missing the space after `[Once Per Turn]`
("`[Once Per Turn]When you use ...`"). Cosmetic; reported, not edited.

### BT19-035 — ShootingStarmon

Lane 15. Base main `23eee9e5a`, branch `audit-bt19-reaudit`. Module IR UNCHANGED;
only the test file was rewritten.

#### Card summary

Catalog (`packages/shared/src/cards/data/cards.json`): Yellow/Red Digimon, Lv4,
Champion, Data, Super Major + Xros Heart, play cost 5, DP 5000, evoCosts Yellow Lv3
and Red Lv3 at 3 memory. Rarity R, max 4 per deck.

Printed clauses:

1. `[Digivolve]Lv.3 w/[Xros Heart] trait: Cost 2` — alternate route.
2. `This card is also treated as [Starmons] for a DigiXros.`
3. `[All Turns] [Once Per Turn] When any of your [Xros Heart] trait Digimon are
played, give 1 of your opponent's Digimon ＜Security A. -1＞ and it gets -3000 DP
until the end of your opponent's turn.`
4. `[On Deletion] You may place 1 Digimon card with the [Xros Heart]/[Blue Flare]
trait from your hand or trash under any of your Tamers.`
5. Inherited: `[When Attacking] [Once Per Turn] If this Digimon has the [Xros Heart]
trait, 1 of your opponent's Digimon gets -2000 DP for the turn.`

#### Q&A ids

| Id                                                                                            | Covered by                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Q3089 (＜Material Save＞ cannot use this card even on a host whose DigiXros needs [Starmons]) | `counts as [Starmons] for a DigiXros, while a real [Starmon] does not (Q3089)` (positive half) and `cannot be saved by ＜Material Save＞ from its DigiXros host's stack (Q3089)` (the ruling's own negative) |
| Q3090 (the `[All Turns]` effect triggers on this card's own play)                             | `triggers on its own play, hits one opponent, and is once per turn (Q3090)`                                                                                                                                  |

Both are covered behaviourally. Neither is documented untestable.

#### Clause -> test -> IR

##### Clause 1 — alternate `[Digivolve]` route

IR: `digivolutionRequirement: [{ level: 3, traits: ["Xros Heart"], cost: 2,
isAlternate: true }]`.

- `takes the Cost 2 alternate route only from a Lv3 with the [Xros Heart] trait` —
  public `digivolve` with `useAlternateCost: true` from BT10-029 Starmons (Yellow
  Lv3, Xros Heart) pays 2 (memory 6 -> 4); the same intent from BT1-050 Liollmon
  (Yellow Lv3, no Xros Heart) silently falls back to the printed route and pays 3
  (6 -> 3). The memory delta is the only discriminator, as the brief requires.
  Source-stack identity and the evolution bonus draw are asserted on both.
- `refuses an illegal evolution source (a Lv4 and a blue Lv3)` — BT9-035 (Lv4) and
  BT1-030 (Blue Lv3) both return `{ ok: false, reason: "invalid-evolution" }`.

##### Clause 2 — treated as `[Starmons]` for a DigiXros only

IR: `trigger: "Static"`, `GrantStatic` with `grant: "name"`,
`tokens: ["Starmons"]`, `digiXrosOnly: true`, self target. The alias is read for a
HAND instance through `digiXrosOnlyNameAliasesFor`
(`engine/effects/interpreter/compiledCards.ts:46`) via `GameEngine.digiXrosDeps`.

- `counts as [Starmons] for a DigiXros, while a real [Starmon] does not (Q3089)` —
  a real `playCard` with a `digiXros` plan on BT10-013 Shoutmon X5. BT19-035 +
  BT10-008 Shoutmon is accepted (memory 10 -> 4: -2 per placed material) and both
  land in the stack by instance id. The near-miss peer BT9-035 "Starmon" (name is
  not "Starmons", trait is [Mutant]) is refused `invalid-material`.
- `cannot be saved by ＜Material Save＞ from its DigiXros host's stack (Q3089)` —
  a real battle deletes the X5; `digiXrosMatches` (`engine/combat/keywords.ts:247`)
  reads only `nameEn`, so only BT10-008 lands under the Tamer and BT19-035 goes to
  the trash. That is the exact board Q3089 rules on.

##### Clause 3 — `[All Turns] [Once Per Turn]` on an `[Xros Heart]` play

IR: `trigger: "AllTurns"` (not `Static` — the brief's trap), `frequency:
"OncePerTurn"` with a `sharedUseKey`, a `whenPlayed` SubTrigger gated by
`sourceFilter` `nameOrTrait [{ tokens: ["Xros Heart"], match: "trait" }]`, then
`GainKeyword SecurityAttack -1` and `ModifyDP -3000` on the SAME target
(`sameTarget: true`), both `duration: "untilOpponentTurnEnd"`.

- `triggers on its own play, hits one opponent, and is once per turn (Q3090)` —
  playing BT19-035 itself arms and fires the watcher: the pinned opponent goes
  6000 -> 3000 and to ＜Security A. -1＞, the bystander is untouched at 5000/0. A
  second [Xros Heart] play (BT19-033) in the same turn changes nothing.
- `ignores a played Digimon without the exact [Xros Heart] trait` — BT9-035 Starmon
  played with the watcher out leaves the opponent at 5000/0.
- `keeps the debuff through the whole opponent turn and drops it afterwards` — real
  `startTurnLoop()`; the state is read INSIDE the opponent's open Main phase
  (still -3000 / -1) and again inside the next own Main (back to 6000 / 0).

##### Clause 4 — `[On Deletion]` place under a Tamer

IR: `trigger: "OnDeletion"`, `PlaceUnder`, `optional: true`, target from
`["hand", "trash"]` with `nameOrTrait [{ tokens: ["Xros Heart", "Blue Flare"],
match: "trait" }]`, `underFilter` = your Tamers.

- `On Deletion places the chosen [Xros Heart] card from hand under a Tamer, not the
near miss` — deletion is a REAL battle (5000 into a suspended 7000 defender). The
  candidate is pinned by instance id, because ShootingStarmon itself is already in
  the trash when the effect resolves and also carries the [Xros Heart] trait
  (CR 4-14-1/2, the brief's trash trap). The [Mutant] near miss stays in hand.
- `On Deletion can take the card from the trash instead` — the trash half of the
  filter, taking the [Blue Flare] BT19-025 over the near miss.

##### Clause 5 — inherited `[When Attacking] [Once Per Turn]`

IR: `trigger: "WhenAttacking"`, `isInherited: true`, `frequency: "OncePerTurn"`,
`ModifyDP -2000` `forTheTurn`, `condition: selfHasTrait [Xros Heart]`.

- `inherited attack reduction needs an [Xros Heart] host and fires on a real attack`
  — a real `attack` intent from BT19-038 JaegerDorulumon (Xros Heart) with BT19-035
  in its digivolution cards drops the opponent 6000 -> 4000; the same stack under
  BT1-057 Sirenmon (no Xros Heart) leaves it at 6000.

### BT19-036 — Wizardmon (X Antibody)

Lane 16. Base `23eee9e5a`, branch `audit-bt19-reaudit`. **Module IR changed** (three
fixes below), so `packages/shared/src/effects/effects.json` is stale for this card and
`BT19-catalog-sync.test.ts` will fail until the coordinator resyncs.

#### Card summary

Catalog (`packages/shared/src/cards/data/cards.json`): Yellow/Purple Digimon, Lv4,
Champion, Data, types `Wizard` / `X Antibody` / `Witchelny`, play cost 6, DP 6000,
evoCosts Yellow Lv3 and Purple Lv3 at 3 memory.

Printed clauses:

1. `[Digivolve][Wizardmon]: Cost 0` — alternate route on an EXACT bracketed name.
2. `[On Play] [When Digivolving] Add your top security card to the hand.`
3. `Then, if [Wizardmon]/[X Antibody] is in this Digimon's digivolution cards, you may
place 1 yellow or purple Option card with cost of 5 or less from your hand as your
bottom security card.`
4. Inherited `[All Turns] [Once Per Turn] When this yellow Digimon with the
[Data]/[Witchelny] trait would leave the battle area by your opponent's effects, by
trashing your top security card, it doesn't leave.`

The catalog's inherited text carries U+00A0 between `[Witchelny]` and `trait`; the
catalog test asserts those exact bytes.

#### Q&A ids

| Id                                                    | Covered by                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| ----------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Q3091 (which cards can be placed as bottom security)  | `only %s is eligible among near-miss hand cards (Q3091)` — one eligible yellow (BT1-102) or purple (BT10-107) Option cost 2 against a cost-6 yellow Option (BT1-107), a green Option (BT1-108) and a yellow Digimon (BT1-045) in the same hand |
| Q3092 (which cards trigger the inherited effect)      | `keeps a yellow [Data] host on the board...`, `does not protect the controller's OTHER yellow [Data] Digimon`, `does not protect a yellow host without the [Data] or [Witchelny] trait`                                                        |
| Q3093 (placement still legal with no security to add) | `places the Option even when there is no security card to add to the hand (Q3093)`                                                                                                                                                             |

#### Clause -> test -> IR

- Clause 1 -> `compiled.digivolutionRequirement = [{ namesExact: ["Wizardmon"], cost: 0,
isAlternate: true }]`.
  - Positive: BT18-036 (Lv4 Yellow, named exactly `Wizardmon`) digivolved into with
    `useAlternateCost: true`; memory stays at 3 (the Lv3 evoCost of 3 was never charged),
    stack identity is the base instance, and the digivolution bonus draw landed.
  - Name near miss: BT12-078 `Wizardmon (X Antibody)` — a substring gate accepts it, the
    printed bracketed name does not. Refused; base unchanged, memory unchanged.
  - Illegal source: BT1-014 (Lv4 Red Kokatorimon) refused on the normal intent.
  - Normal route: BT1-045 (Lv3 Yellow) charges the printed 3 memory (5 -> 2).
- Clause 2 -> `SecurityManipulation { op: "toHand", toTop: true, amount: 1 }` on both
  `OnPlay` and `WhenDigivolving`. Proved through a public `playCard` intent (memory
  10 -> 4, top security instance id moves to hand, the second security card is now the
  only one left) and through public `digivolve` intents.
- Clause 3 -> `SecurityManipulation { op: "addBottom", optional: true, source.filter =
{ zone: "hand", kind: ["Option"], playCostLte: 5, colors: ["Yellow","Purple"] } }`
  gated by `selfHasInDigivolutionCards` over `[{ tokens:["Wizardmon"], match:"nameExact" },
{ tokens:["X Antibody"], match:"trait" }]`.
  - Name branch: digivolve from BT18-036. Bottom placement asserted by instance id —
    security ends `[second, option]`, not `[option, second]`.
  - Trait branch: digivolve from BT12-073 `Impmon (X Antibody)` (Lv3 Purple, normal
    route) — the trait alone satisfies the gate with no `Wizardmon` name anywhere.
  - Negative: digivolve from BT1-045 Tsukaimon (neither) — the Option stays in hand and
    only the security card moved.
  - Played from hand there are no digivolution cards, so the gate is false; the
    `plays on a public play` test asserts the Option is still in hand.
  - Optional: `autoDeclineOptional` leaves the Option in hand while clause 2 still runs.
- Clause 4 -> `AllTurns` / `isInherited` / `frequency: "OncePerTurn"` `Replacement`
  (`event: "wouldLeavePlay"`, `leaveCause: "opponentEffect"`, cost = trash own top
  security). Every case drives a REAL opponent effect: seat 1 plays BT14-100 Pummel
  Whack (`[Main] Delete 1 of your opponent's level 4 or lower Digimon`) inside their own
  Main phase through `startTurnLoop` + `waitForMainPhase(1)`; seat 1 also controls an
  inert purple Candlemon so the Option's colour requirement is met.
  - Protected: BT10-033 (Yellow, Data) with BT19-036 under it survives; `sec1` is in the
    trash and `sec2` is the only security card left.
  - `isSelfRef` proof: with a second yellow [Data] Digimon (BT3-037) on the same board
    and the deletion aimed at IT, that peer dies and no security is paid.
  - Trait negative: BT1-051 Reppamon (Yellow, Holy Beast / Vaccine) is deleted with
    security untouched.
  - Once per turn: two Pummel Whacks in one opponent Main — the first is prevented
    (one security card paid), the second deletes.
  - Cause negative: a real battle deletion on the opponent's turn (host attacks on its
    own turn to become suspended, then is attacked) is not prevented and costs no
    security.

#### Defects found and fixed locally

1. `match: "name"` for the bracketed `[Wizardmon]` reference in both timing effects ->
   `nameExact`. Not separately observable in today's catalog (every card whose name
   contains `Wizardmon` as a substring also carries the `X Antibody` trait, so the OR
   still passes), but it is the printed semantics and the same token feeds the
   digivolution route below.
2. `digivolutionRequirement.names` (substring) -> `namesExact`. Behaviourally proved:
   before the fix BT12-078 `Wizardmon (X Antibody)` could take the cost-0 route.
3. The inherited would-leave replacement had no `isSelfRef`, so it protected EVERY
   yellow [Data]/[Witchelny] Digimon its controller had, not "this Digimon"
   (printed text and KB Q3092). Added `isSelfRef: true`.

Mutation check: reverting fixes 2 and 3 in the module fails
`refuses the [Wizardmon] route for the name-substring peer Wizardmon (X Antibody)` and
`does not protect the controller's OTHER yellow [Data] Digimon`, so both fixes are
proved by behaviour, not only by IR shape.

No implemented card in the catalog reachable from this fixture prints "activate that card's [When Digivolving] effect" against an opponent-controlled Digimon; the engine seam is `DisableTimingEffect` + the `whenDigivolving` gate, shared with Q5536. Documented gap. |

#### Clause -> test -> IR

- Clause 1 -> `effects[0]` `trigger: "Counter"`, `isFromHand: true`,
  `keywords: [{ keyword: "BlastDigivolve" }]`. Proved twice through the real
  `respondCounter` intent inside an opponent attack's counter window (never a bare
  `digivolve`): the memory gauge is unchanged (cost fully waived) while the digivolution
  bonus draw still lands and the stack holds the base instance.
- Clause 2 -> `UseOptionWithoutCost { payCost: false, optional: true, filter: { kind:
["Option"], colorCount: 1, playCostLte: 5 }, condition: isYourTurn }` on both `OnPlay`
  and `WhenDigivolving`.
  - Public `playCard`: memory 10 -> 5 (Taomon's own cost only), BT1-102 in the trash and
    its own text resolved (＜Draw 1＞ per 2 security, the seeded top-deck card is in hand).
  - Near misses left in hand: BT12-104 (Yellow/Red, two colours) and BT1-107 (Yellow,
    cost 6).
  - Public `digivolve` onto BT1-051: memory 5 -> 2 (the printed evoCost only).
  - `autoDeclineOptional`: the Option stays in hand and the trash stays empty.
  - Turn exclusivity: on our own turn the opponent's Digimon has no ＜Security Attack＞
    modifier and no `whenDigivolving` restriction.
- Clause 3 -> `GainKeyword { keyword: SecurityAttack, amount: -1 }` plus
  `DisableTimingEffect { timings: ["whenDigivolving"], target.sameTarget: true }`, both
  gated by `isOpponentsTurn` and expiring `untilOpponentTurnEnd`.
  - Reached the only legal way: ＜Blast Digivolve＞ during the opponent's attack, so the
    `[When Digivolving]` timing genuinely resolves on their turn.
  - `sameTarget` proved by consequence, not by a flag: the unchosen attacker checks one
    security card normally, while the chosen Digimon later attacks and checks NONE
    (1 - 1 = 0) and cannot activate its `[When Digivolving]` effect.
- Clause 4 -> `WhenAttacking` / `isInherited` `ModifyDP { amount: -4000, duration:
"forTheTurn" }`. A realistic stack (BT1-051 host with BT19-037 under it) attacks
  through a public `attack` intent inside the turn loop: exactly one of two opponent
  Digimon drops 9000 -> 5000, the other is untouched, and the modifier is gone when read

- Clause 5 (ACE Overflow ＜3＞) -> catalog `isAce` / `overflowMemory`, proved by
  behaviour: Taomon attacks a suspended 20000-DP wall, dies in battle, and memory drops

None in the IR. The prior audit's test file was rebuilt: it proved the timings with

#### Defects found and fixed (both in `BT19-038.ts`, both change the IR)

1. **`suspended: false` on both Suspend targets (introduced by the prior audit).**
   The printed text is "Suspend 1 of your opponent's Digimon" with no "unsuspended"
   qualifier, and selection is never gated on whether the action will change
   anything — comprehensive §15-15-5-1 explicitly chooses a card that cannot even be
   affected for this exact effect ("Even if a card that isn't affected by effects is
   chosen for an '[On Play] Suspend 1 of your opponent's Digimon' effect, it isn't
   suspended"). The filter removed an already-suspended Digimon from the candidate
   set, which is a rules error and also a strategic one (the controller may want to
   spend the choice on the suspended Digimon and leave the fresh one alone).
   Proof: `may choose an ALREADY suspended Digimon for the suspension` asserts the
   already-suspended permanent is IN the offered candidate set and that picking it
   leaves the unsuspended peer untouched. Under the old IR the candidate set excludes
   it and the test fails.

2. **`grant: "nameForDigiXros"` made the printed alias dead.** `grantStatic.ts:49`
   accepts both spellings for the board-side ledger, but the DigiXros MATERIAL check
   reads `digiXrosOnlyNameAliasesFor` (`interpreter/compiledCards.ts:46-57`), which
   only recognises `grant: "name"` + `digiXrosOnly: true` — the BT19-012 form. With
   the old IR, DigiXrosing BT19-010 with BT19-038 in the [Dorulumon] slot is refused
   `invalid-material`, i.e. the card's second printed line did nothing. Switched to
   the BT19-012 form; behaviour is otherwise identical (`grantStatic.ts` routes both
   to `grantNameTrait(..., { digiXrosOnly: true })`).

Not changed, deliberately: the two `Restrict` targets keep `controllerDefault:
"opponent"` rather than `controller: "opponent"`. `matching/permanent.ts:149` reads
`filter.controller ?? filter.controllerDefault`, so the seat scope is enforced either
way; the test proves it instead of churning the IR — both recorded candidate sets are
asserted to exclude my own Digimon.

### BT19-039 — SkullBaluchimon

Card lane 17. Base main `23eee9e5a`, branch `audit-bt19-reaudit`.

resyncs.

The previous test file proved every clause through injected timing
(`advance.fireForPermanent`, `advance.fireSubTrigger`) and injected suspension state.
It has been replaced end to end with public intents and the real turn loop.

#### Card summary

Catalog: Yellow/Purple Digimon, Lv.5, Ultimate, Data, `types: [Undead, X Antibody]`,
play cost 7, DP 7000, `evoCosts: [{ Yellow, 4, 4 }, { Purple, 4, 4 }]`.

Printed clauses:

1. `[On Play] [When Digivolving] By trashing your top security card, delete 1 of your
opponent's level 4 or lower Digimon and gain 1 memory.`
2. `[On Deletion] ＜Recovery +1 (Deck)＞.`
3. Inherited: `[All Turns] [Once Per Turn] When your security is reduced, you may
unsuspend this Digimon.`

No errata, no banlist entry.

#### Q&A ids

`node tools/kb/query.mjs card BT19-039` -> `(no knowledge-base entries)`. Confirmed
with the KB tool, as the brief requires; `docs/audits/BT19-reaudit/KB-INDEX.md` lists
none for this card either. The clauses were therefore checked against the
comprehensive rules directly:

- §15-7-1 / §15-7-2: "By X, Y" is an OPTIONAL processing condition. The player chooses
  whether to execute it, and if they do not, nothing after the condition happens.
- §15-9-1: everything after the condition is mandatory processing — the player cannot
  choose to skip part of it.

#### Defect found and fixed (`BT19-039.ts`, changes the IR)

The generated IR modelled the memory gain as a SECOND optional action
(`{ kind: "GainMemory", amount: 1, optional: true, abortOnDecline: true }`) in both
the `OnPlay` and `WhenDigivolving` effects. That let a player pay the security cost,
delete a Digimon and then decline the memory — mandatory processing offered as a
choice (§15-9-1), and a second prompt the card never prints. Removed both flags; the
cost gate stays on the `Delete` action, where `optional: true` + `abortOnDecline: true`
is the correct encoding of §15-7-1/§15-7-2 (`abortOnDecline` there is live, not dead:
it is not the last action).

#### Clause -> test -> IR

| Clause                      | Test                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     | IR                                                                                                                                 |
| --------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 1 (On Play)                 | `pays with the TOP security card, deletes only the level 4 or lower Digimon and gains 1 memory on a real play` — public `playCard`; the trashed card is asserted by instance id and the remaining security by order; the opponent's Lv.5 near-miss peer survives; gauge 10 -> 3 (play cost) -> 4 (the clause's +1); no `actionRejected` event.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           | `OnPlay` `Delete` with `cost: { kind: "trash", zone: "security", position: "top" }`, then `GainMemory 1`                           |
| 1 (When Digivolving)        | `resolves the same clause on a public digivolve from a yellow Lv.4, with the source in its stack` — public `digivolve` intent from BT1-051 (Yellow Lv.4, cost 4): gauge 4 -> 0 -> 1, the source is the only digivolution card, the bonus draw lands, security and trash asserted by instance id.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         | `WhenDigivolving`, same actions                                                                                                    |
| 1 (declining the condition) | `declining the optional processing condition stops the deletion AND the memory gain` — gauge moves only by the play cost, security untouched card-for-card, the opponent's Lv.4 still on the board. This is the test the IR fix is for: under the old IR the memory gain was a separate prompt.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          | `optional: true` + `abortOnDecline: true` on the `Delete`                                                                          |
| 2 `＜Recovery +1 (Deck)＞`  | `＜Recovery +1 (Deck)＞ moves exactly the top deck card to the top of security when it loses a real battle` — a real attack into a 12000 DP wall; exactly the top deck card moves, it lands on TOP of the existing security card (asserted by instance id), the second deck card is now the top, and SkullBaluchimon itself is in the trash.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             | `OnDeletion` `keywords: [{ Recovery, amount: 1 }]`                                                                                 |
| 3 inherited                 | `inherited clause unsuspends its host once per turn, only for the controller's own security, and resets next turn` — four real turns through `startTurnLoop`. My attack reduces the OPPONENT's security and raises no prompt (the "your security" direction). Their first attack reduces mine: one prompt, host unsuspends. Their second attack in the same turn: security drops again, still exactly one prompt ([Once Per Turn]). Next round of turns: the host is suspended by attacking again, their attack raises the second prompt and unsuspends it (the per-turn use reset). The peer with no BT19-039 in its stack never moves. | `AllTurns` `SubTrigger whenSecurityRemoved` -> `Unsuspend` self, `optional: true`, `frequency: "OncePerTurn"`, `isInherited: true` |
| 3, watcher scope            | `does not arm the inherited watcher from the top card of a stack` — `observe.subscriptions("whenSecurityRemoved", …)` finds the watcher on the host and none on the permanent whose TOP card is BT19-039.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                | `isInherited: true`                                                                                                                |

The seat direction comes from the engine default, not from the IR: with no
`sourceFilter.controller`, `interpreter/actions/subTrigger.ts:235` watches the
source's own seat. That default is what the four-turn test proves.

#### Open rules question (documented, not asserted)

If the opponent has no level 4 or lower Digimon, `runAction.ts:516` skips the whole
action before offering the optional condition, so the controller can neither pay the
security card nor take the memory. Comprehensive §15-7 does not obviously permit that
shortcut — a player may generally choose to pay an optional processing condition and
then perform as much of the following processing as possible. No Q&A on this card
settles it, and I did not want to bless either reading with a passing assertion, so
there is no test for the empty-target case. Flagging it for the coordinator: it is an
engine-wide question (every "By X, delete 1 …" card), not specific to BT19-039.

#### Defects found and fixed locally

1. **The compound "atomic both-security" cost was wrong.** The prior module modelled
   `by trashing the top card of your security stack, trash the top card of your opponent's
security stack` as one `kind: "compound"` cost of two trashes, so an opponent with an empty
   security stack made the whole clause do nothing. The printed text makes only YOUR card the
   cost; the opponent's trash is part of the payload, alongside the +6000 DP. Fixed to
   `cost: { kind: "trashSecurityTop" }` plus a `trashSecurityTop` action with
   `controller: "opponent"`. Contrast BT19-043, whose "by trashing BOTH players' top security
   cards" genuinely is atomic and is confirmed so by KB Q3096 — the two cards read differently
   and must compile differently.
2. **Substring `names` on a bracketed `[Digivolve][Dynasmon]` route.** `names: ["Dynasmon"]`
   is a substring gate, so "Dynasmon (X Antibody)" — this very card — could take the cost-1
   route. Changed to `namesExact: ["Dynasmon"]` (the same trap lane 5 found on BT19-012 and
   lane 16 found on BT19-036). Proved by the near-miss test.
3. **Substring `match: "name"` in the digivolution-card gate.** `[Dynasmon]` is bracketed, so
   the reference is exact: changed to `match: "nameExact"`.
4. **`optional: true` on a mandatory "by doing" cost.** The clause prints no "may"; the Rule
   Manual treats "by doing" as a processing condition. The optional prompt was removed, so the
   clause now fires whenever it is payable.
5. **A dead test assertion.** The prior test's recovery case asserted
   `toHaveLength(count === 2 ? 3 : 3)` — the same value on both branches, so it could not fail.
   Replaced with an `it.each` that asserts the recovered card's instance id and the deck size.
6. The prior suite proved clause 4 almost entirely through `advance().fireForPermanent`
   (injected timing, no behavioural credit). Every clause is now driven through public intents:
   `digivolve`, `attack`, `declareBlock`, and `startTurnLoop` / `runOneTurn`.

No test is retained red; no engine gap was found.

- Near-miss for the exact-name route: `BT19-042` "Dynasmon (X Antibody)" as the base — the name

- Realistic evolution stack: BT1-057 (Lv.5) -> BT19-041 Dynasmon -> BT19-042 by the cost-1

- ＜Raid＞'s "you may" is answered by `autoAcceptOptional`; the decline branch is not asserted.

General rulings that decide the two target filters:

#### Clause -> test -> IR

- `compiled.effects[0]` (`OnPlay`) and `compiled.effects[1]` (`WhenDigivolving`) carry the same
  two ordered actions, asserted in a loop:
  1. `Suspend`, count 1, filter `{ controller: "opponent", kind: ["Digimon"] }` — no
     `suspended` key anywhere in the compiled card.
  2. `Restrict`, `restriction: "unsuspend"`, `duration: "untilOpponentTurnEnd"`, count 1,
     filter `controller: "opponent"`, `kind: ["Digimon"]`,
     `nameOrTrait: [{ tokens: ["Data"], match: "trait" }]`. `[Data]` is an attribute, which
     `cardData.staticTraitsOf` folds into traits, so `match: "trait"` (exact token) is right.
     `untilOpponentTurnEnd` is a real `EffectDurationRef` and is proved to expire at that boundary
     rather than silently at the next turn end.
- `[On Play]`: public `playCard` intent inside a real `startTurnLoop` main phase. Endpoints:
  memory 4 -> 0, card gone from hand, played permanent unsuspended with an empty stack, the
  scripted [Data] target both suspended and restricted, and three peers untouched — a second

  prove the attribute filter is exact and the counts are 1, not "all".

  BT1-013 stays suspended through seat 1's own unsuspend phase while an unrestricted suspended
  [Data] control (BT1-028, seeded `suspended: true`) stands up in the same phase. The
  restriction is gone once seat 1's turn ends, and the Digimon is still suspended on our next
  turn. Turn changes are driven by `waitForMainPhase` / `endPhase`, never by writing
  `state.turnSeat`.

  suspension and the fresh peer stays unsuspended and unrestricted. This is the assertion the
  removed `suspended: false` filter used to fail.
- Independence of the two halves: with no [Data] Digimon at all, the suspension still lands and
  nothing is restricted; with no opponent Digimon at all, the play still resolves (memory 0,
  one permanent on our board) and nothing errors.
- `[When Digivolving]`: public `digivolve` intent from BT1-067 Palmon (Green Lv3) inside a real
  main phase — memory 5 -> 3 (printed cost 2), the source retained as the only digivolution

- Stack case: Chamblemon has no inherited effect, so under a realistic stack
  (Palmon -> Chamblemon -> BT19-052 Vespamon) a real attack by the host suspends nothing and
  restricts nothing while still checking one security card. `inheritedEffectText` is asserted
  `undefined` in the catalog test.

Both Suspend filters carried `suspended: false` from the prior audit. The printed text names no

unverified; the module and the previous test were re-checked from the catalog and the KB.

#### Card summary

Green/Black, Lv.4, Virus, Cyborg / X Antibody / Royal Base / LIBERATOR / Insectoid,
4000 DP, play cost 4, evo costs Black Lv.3 = 3 and Green Lv.3 = 3.

Printed clauses:

1. `[Digivolve]Lv.3 w/[Royal Base] trait: Cost 2`
2. `[Security] [All Turns] All of your [Royal Base] trait Digimon get +1000 DP.`
3. `[All Turns] [Once Per Turn] When any of your other Digimon with the [Royal Base] trait
would leave the battle area by effects, by placing this Digimon as the face-up bottom
security card, they don't leave.`
4. `[Rule] Trait: Has the [Insectoid] type.`
5. Inherited: `[All Turns] This Digimon gets +1000 DP.`

Clause 2 is the BT18/BT19 "Royal Base" security-resident family (BT18-044, BT18-046,
BT19-045, BT23-038, BT23-042 print the identical line). `[Security]` here marks a
persistent effect whose source is a FACE-UP card in the security stack, not a
security-check trigger: `builderForTrigger`
(`apps/api/src/engine/effects/interpreter/effect.ts:321-327`) routes `isSecurity` +
`YourTurn|OpponentsTurn|AllTurns` to the `securityStatic` builder, whose base guard is
`isSecuritySource` (face-up in security, `effects/context.ts:86-88`).

during the opponent's real Main phase inside `engine.startTurnLoop()` (BT8-097 Crimson
Blaze, BT2-091 Volcanic Flare), and every battle is a real `attack` intent. No
`advance.fire*` and no `advance.verb.deletePermanent` is used anywhere in this file; the
previous test proved both prevention branches with `verb.deletePermanent("byEffect")`,
which cannot distinguish an effect cause reached through a real resolution. No
`s.state.turnSeat` write either; the opponent's turn is reached through the loop.

#### Findings

1. **No IR defect found.** Every filter, trigger, duration and cost key in the module is a
   key the engine actually reads. Specifically checked against this run's trap list:
   `match: "trait"` is the exact-trait form the bracketed `[Royal Base]` reference needs;
   the trigger is `AllTurns`, not `Static`; `duration: "permanent"` is a real
   `EffectDurationRef`; `sourceFilter.leaveReason: "effect"` is a supported alternative
   encoding of `leaveCause: "byEffect"`; the `[Rule]` line has a `Rule`/`GrantStatic` node.
2. **The previous test's claim "all and only controller Royal Base Digimon" was untested** —
   its fixture had no opponent permanent at all, and no near-miss trait. Both are now
   asserted.
3. **The `[Rule]` node is redundant but harmless.** The catalog already lists `Insectoid` in
   `types` for BT19-048, so the trait gate would pass without `effects[2]`. Unlike
   BT19-018/019 (whose catalog `types` lack the granted type) there is no way for a test to
   separate the node from the catalog fact. The node is kept because the line is printed;
   the cross-card consequence test proves the trait is effective either way.
4. **`[Once Per Turn]` is not behaviourally observable on this card.** The cost of the
   prevention is placing the source itself into the security stack, so after one use the
   source is no longer on the battle area and can never be asked a second time — in the same
   turn or any later one. The frequency is asserted structurally on the IR; there is no
   board state in which a second same-turn refusal could be observed. Not a defect, and not
   evidence either: recorded honestly here rather than dressed up as a behavioural pass.
5. **Testkit note (not a defect).** An opponent Option needs a matching-colour permanent on
   the player's own board (`color-requirement-unmet`), and an attack needs a SUSPENDED
   defender; the battle-deletion case therefore attacks on my own turn into a seeded
   suspended wall rather than seeding my own Digimon suspended (which would stand up at my
   unsuspend phase).

No engine gap was found, so no test is retained red.

#### Catalog discrepancies

None. The catalog text, colours, level, DP, cost, types and attributes match the printed
card; the effect text carries non-breaking spaces, which the test normalizes before
comparing (the same convention as BT19-029).

#### Card summary

Green/Black, Lv.5, Vaccine, Machine / Xros Heart, 7000 DP, play cost 7, evo costs Green
Lv.4 = 4 and Black Lv.4 = 4.

Printed clauses:

1. `[Digivolve]Lv.4 w/[Xros Heart] trait: Cost 3`
2. `This card is also treated as [Ballistamon] for a DigiXros.`
3. `[On Play] [When Digivolving] 1 of your Digimon can't be returned to the hand or deck and
gets +3000 DP until the end of your opponent's turn.`

#### Verification of the prior audit's hand/trash change

Confirmed correct and load-bearing. `runPlaceUnder`
(`apps/api/src/engine/effects/interpreter/actions/placeUnder.ts:398-409`) resolves the
loose-card source zones as `action.from` > `action.target.from` > `target.filter.zone` >
the legacy sweep `["hand", "trash", "deck"]`. The module carries
`target.from: ["hand", "trash"]`, which is read, and without it the fallback would reach
the deck the card never names. Behaviour is asserted, not just the field: the deletion test
seeds an eligible BT19-047 Ballistamon in the DECK and biases the auto-responder toward it
(`preferInstanceIds`), and it is still never placed.

`advance.fireForPermanent` (injected timing, worth at most 1 in Behaviour), proved the
inherited Blocker by writing `s.state.turnSeat = 1` (injected state, a named trap in this
run), and proved the DigiXros alias only by reading `effectiveNames`. All three are
replaced.

#### Findings

1. **No IR defect found.** Trigger names, the two duration strings, the restriction name,
   the trait match mode, the DigiXros grant shape and the loose-card source field are all
   keys the engine reads. `trigger: "Static"` for the DigiXros alias is correct — the line
   is not a printed `[All Turns]` clause, and the alias must be readable while the card is
   still off the battle area.
2. **[On Deletion] behaviour the previous test mis-framed.** The deleted AtlurBallistamon is
   itself in the trash when its own `[On Deletion]` resolves (CR 4-14-1/2) and it is itself a
   Digimon card with the [Xros Heart] trait, so it is a legal candidate for its own effect.
   The near-miss test therefore asserts the SELF card by instance id as the only placement
   when the hand holds a wrong-trait card, and every hand/trash test pins the intended
   candidate with `preferInstanceIds` instead of relying on candidate order.
3. **A "can't be returned" Digimon can still be chosen as a bounce target.** BT15-090 and
   BT19-092 resolve, the Option is spent, and the move simply does not happen —
   `filterBouncePrevented` sits at the primitive, not at targeting. Because "nothing moved"
   is also what an effect with no legal target looks like, each protection test is paired
   with a control run on the same card and the same preference, where the unprotected peer
   IS returned. Not a defect; recorded so the pass is not read as stronger than it is.
4. **Testkit notes (not defects).** An opponent Option needs a matching-colour permanent on
   its controller's board; and an attack needs a suspended defender, so the deletion tests
   attack a seeded suspended wall on my own turn.

No engine gap was found, so no test is retained red.

None. Fields and text match the printed card. The effect and inherited text carry
non-breaking spaces, which the test normalizes before comparing.

##### Evidence notes

- **Route cost.** The alternate route is discriminated by the memory delta, not by
  `{ok:true}`: memory 5 -> 2 (cost 3) on the Royal Base source, memory 5 -> 1 (cost 4)
  on the colour route. Digivolution-card identity is asserted by instance id, and the
  bonus draw is asserted by hand and deck contents.
- **Near miss vs illegal source.** BT1-073 Kabuterimon is Green, Lv.4 and `[Insectoid]` —
  everything the route wants except `[Royal Base]` — and the route intent is rejected
  with `invalid-evolution` while the colour route still works. BT1-014 Kokatorimon (Red
  Lv.4) is rejected on both, with board, memory and hand unchanged.
- **Blocker is proved by its rules consequence, not by a flag.** Inside the opponent's
  real Main phase (turn loop, no `turnSeat` injection) the opponent attacks the player;
  `declareBlock` with BT1-066 Tentomon (Green `[Insectoid]`, no `[Royal Base]`) is
  rejected, `declareBlock` with BT19-045 FunBeemon is accepted, and the endpoint is the
  redirected battle: FunBeemon in the trash, security count unchanged. The same board on
  my own turn grants nothing, and a face-down copy of the card grants nothing.
- **Deletion ceiling.** Three parameterised boards (0, 1, 2 face-up security cards) each
  assert both endpoints: the play-cost-at-the-ceiling target is in the opponent's trash
  and the next cost up is still on the board, with the played Vespamon on my board and
  memory at 0. The `When Digivolving` copy is proved through a real `digivolve` intent.
- **`[Rule]` trait.** The catalog already prints `Insectoid` in `types`, so the
  `GrantStatic` node is redundant with the catalog rather than load-bearing (recorded as
  a catalog observation below, not a defect). The consequence is still proved
  cross-card: BT9-100 Grandis Scissor unsuspends "1 of your Digimon with `[Insectoid]`
  in its traits" (`match: "trait"`, exact) and forces it to attack. Vespamon is chosen
  and attacks; BT1-013 Muchomon, suspended and available but not `[Insectoid]`, is never
  a candidate and stays suspended.
- **Peer / stack.** The inherited clause runs under a realistic host: BT19-053
  QueenBeemon with `BT18-044 / BT18-046 / BT19-052` beneath it — the printed
  FunBeemon -> Waspmon -> Vespamon -> QueenBeemon line. Battle 1 of the turn trashes the
  opponent's top security card (asserted by instance id); a second battle in the same
  turn, reached publicly by playing BT9-100, trashes nothing; after a real opponent turn
  the budget refreshes and a third battle trashes again. The opponent's survivor is put
  back into an attackable state by having it attack during the intervening turn, per the
  set brief.

other than in battle, you may place those Digimon face-up at the bottom of your

##### Evidence notes

- **Route cost.** Memory 5 -> 2 (cost 3) from BT18-052 CannonBeemon with a real two-card
  digivolution stack, with the stack's instance ids and the bonus draw asserted. The
  near miss BT1-076 MegaKabuterimon (Green, Lv.5, `[Insectoid]`, no `[Royal Base]`) is
  rejected with `invalid-evolution` and then digivolves by colour for 4; BT1-022
  Garudamon (Red Lv.5) is rejected outright with board, memory and hand unchanged.
- **"reduced by 8", not "free".** The cost-reduction test plays a second BT19-053 (play
  cost 12) out of face-up security and asserts memory 6 -> 2. The once-per-turn test uses
  BT19-052 (play cost 8) and asserts memory does not move at all — the two together pin
  the modifier at exactly 8.
- **Once per turn through the real loop.** Attack 1 plays one Vespamon; a second attack in
  the same turn, reached publicly by playing BT9-100 Grandis Scissor, plays nothing; after
  a real opponent turn a third attack plays the second Vespamon. The second face-up
  Vespamon sits in security the whole time, so the refusal is the frequency gate and not a
  missing candidate.
- **Near misses for clause 3.** A face-up BT1-066 Tentomon (Green `[Insectoid]`, no
  `[Royal Base]`) and a face-DOWN BT19-052 are both ignored: after the attack the board
  still holds only QueenBeemon, security is unchanged by instance id, and memory is
  unchanged.
- **＜Alliance＞ (Q3106).** Real attack; the engine's `alliancePrompt` lists the Digimon
  the `[When Attacking]` clause just played out of security as an eligible ally;
  `respondAlliance` on it suspends it and QueenBeemon's DP reaches 20000 (12000 + 8000).
  The battle-scoped bonus is sampled through the `onEvent` hook because it expires with
  the battle.
- **Clause 4 with a real opponent effect.** The leave event is the opponent publicly
  playing BT2-018 MetalGreymon (`[On Play] Delete all of your opponent's Digimon with
4000 DP or less`) inside their own Main phase. No `advance.verb.deletePermanent`
  anywhere. Endpoints: my battle area empty, the two `[Royal Base]` Digimon (QueenBeemon
  herself included — Q3107) at the bottom of security in that order and face up, and the
  near-miss BT1-066 Tentomon in the trash. No selection decision is raised, matching
  Q3108's "affects all Digimon without having to choose them".
- **"you may" and "other than in battle".** Declining the optional sends both Digimon to
  the trash and leaves security untouched. A real battle deletion (a 20000 DP attacker
  killing QueenBeemon on the opponent's turn, after she suspended herself attacking on
  mine) also sends her to the trash with security unchanged — `leaveCause:
"otherThanBattle"` proved from both sides.
- **Q3099 / Q5304.** BT19-048 ForgeBeemon and BT19-045 FunBeemon share the board with a
  4000 DP QueenBeemon; `preferTriggerKeys: ["BT19-048"]` puts ForgeBeemon's replacement
  first. Endpoint: security becomes
  `[BT1-009 (face down), BT19-048, BT19-053, BT19-045]` with the last three face up, the
  battle area empty and the trash empty — ForgeBeemon paid itself into security to save
  the others, and QueenBeemon's clause then still placed every affected Digimon, exactly
  as the ruling describes.
- **Peer / stack.** Near-miss peers appear in every filter test (Tentomon and
  MegaKabuterimon for the `[Royal Base]` trait, a face-down copy for `faceUp`), and the
  digivolve test runs QueenBeemon on a real FunBeemon/Waspmon/CannonBeemon stack and
  reads ＜Alliance＞ and `[Insectoid]` off the resulting permanent.
