#### Defects fixed locally

The previous test file proved clause 4 only through `advance().verb.deletePermanent(...,
"byEffect")` and `"byBattle"` and clause 3 only through
`advance().fireForPermanent(EffectTiming.OnUseAttack, ...)`; it covered none of the nine
listed Q&A ids by name, seeded no deck or opponent security, used no near-miss peer, and
proved the cost reduction only as "memory did not change" against a card whose reduced
cost is 0 (which "play for free" would satisfy equally). All of that is replaced by real
opponent effects, real attacks and the real turn loop, with the cost modifier pinned by a
12-cost card.

No IR change was needed: every clause behaves correctly as compiled, including the
hand-written fixes recorded in the module header.

#### Retained reds

None. All 14 tests are green; nothing is `it.fails` or `it.skip`.

#### Remaining gaps

- Q3111 is proved only in the persistent-`[Security]` form, because no `[Royal Base]`
  Digimon prints a check-time `[Security]` clause (see the caveat above). A future card
  that does would give the stronger proof.
- The `[Rule] Trait` node is redundant with the catalog, which already lists `Insectoid`
  in `types`; its own necessity is therefore unprovable from this card alone.
- The `Q3099/Q5304` test reads BT19-048's compiled module, which lane 3's owner is
  editing concurrently. If that lane changes ForgeBeemon's replacement shape, this test
  is the one that will notice; the assertion is written against the ruling's endpoint,
  not against ForgeBeemon's internals.

#### Catalog discrepancies

None against the official card. Same observation as BT19-052: `types` already contains
`Insectoid`, making the printed `[Rule]` line redundant with the catalog data.

##### Peer / near-miss evidence

The `[When Digivolving]` test seats three permanents at once: the opponent's
suspended `BT1-011`, the opponent's unsuspended `BT1-015`, and our OWN suspended
`BT1-009`. Only the opponent's suspended body reaches the deck bottom (asserted by
instance id, at the deck's last position); both near misses are asserted still in
their battle areas. That separates the `suspended: true` gate from the
`controller: "opponent"` gate in one board.

The evolution-stack case is a real `digivolve` intent from `BT19-050` Rapidmon
(Green Lv.5): the resulting permanent keeps `stack == [Rapidmon instance]`, memory
falls 6 -> 1, the hand shows exactly the bonus-draw card, and the `SecurityAttack`
grant reads 1 on the evolved permanent.

#### Evidence standards notes

  open Main phase; no `advance.fire*` and no `s.state.turnSeat` write. `s.state.memory`
  is set inside the open Main phase as an arrange step only.
- Endpoints asserted by instance id (deck bottom, stack, battle area, hand), plus
  memory, security count, and `s.state.pendingDecision === undefined`.
- Fixtures use inert main-deck Digimon (`BT1-009`..`BT1-015`); no Digi-Egg in any
  deck or security, no numeric `security: <n>` form; both seats hold security so no
  digivolve or attack trips the security win check.

  from a three-card stack), not only by the `keywordAmount` read.

##### Peer / near-miss evidence

- Filter near miss: `near-miss peers: reveals with no [Knightmon] text and no
[Twilight] trait add nothing` reveals `BT19-046` Chamblemon (Vegetation),
  `BT1-011` Agumon Expert (Dinosaur) and `BT19-044` Terriermon (Beast). None of the
  three names, traits or prints `[Knightmon]` or `[Twilight]`. Hand and the Tamer's
  stack are unchanged and all three reveals reach the deck bottom in order.
- Positive discrimination inside one board: the Q3113 fixture pairs `BT18-058`
  Kotemon, which qualifies only through the TEXT arm (it literally prints
  "1 card with [Knightmon] in its text"), with `BT10-058` Monitamon, which qualifies
  only through the `[Twilight]` TRAIT arm. Both arms of the `orPrevious` union are
  therefore exercised by distinct cards.
- Evolution stack / inherited: the Reboot test builds the stack with a real
  `digivolve` intent — Monitamon -> `BT19-058` SkullKnightmon (Black Lv.3 base,
  cost 3) — asserts `stack == [Monitamon instance]`, then suspends the host by a
  real attack, ends Main, and reads inside the opponent's own open Main phase (after
  THEIR unsuspend phase). The host is unsuspended; the near-miss peer `BT1-009`,
  suspended the same way by its own real attack and carrying no `Reboot`
  (`observe().hasKeyword(..., "Reboot") === false`), is still suspended.
  This is the "prove a keyword by its rules consequence, not a flag" requirement.

#### Evidence standards notes

- No `advance.fire*`, no `advance.verb.deletePermanent`, no `s.state.turnSeat` write.
  The previous suite used `verb.deletePermanent` for all three On-Deletion cases and
  set `turnSeat = 1` plus `runOneTurn()` for Reboot; both are replaced.
- Deletion is a real battle loss (Monitamon, DP 1000, attacks a suspended `BT1-013`,
  DP 5000).
- Reveal endpoints are computed from the live deck at Main open
  (`deckAtMain`), so the assertions do not depend on whether the first turn draws.
- Both seats hold security; no Digi-Egg sits in any deck or security; the breeding
  fixtures use `s.ready()` + intent rather than the turn loop, because seating a

##### Peer / near-miss evidence

- Trait near miss: `BT1-009` Monodramon carries `[Mini Dragon]`, not
  `[Dragonkin]`/`[Cyborg]`. It is revealed alongside real matches and is refused —
  proving the exact `match: "trait"` gate rather than a substring one ("Dragon" is a
  substring of both, "Mini Dragon" is not the trait).
- Kind/trait near miss for the second category: `BT19-089` Red Card is an Option
  card with no `[Device]` trait, so the `orFilters` Option arm must reject it.
- Positive control in the same board: `EX2-062` Ryo Akiyama — a different printing
  of the same exact name — IS taken, so the `nameExact` arm matches on the printed
  name, not on a card id.
- Evolution stack / inherited: `inherited [All Turns] ...` builds the stack with a
  real `digivolve` intent — Monodramon -> `BT19-060` Strikedramon (Black Lv.3 base,
  cost 2) — asserts `stack == [Monodramon instance]`, then reads `currentDP` 6000
  (printed 5000 + 1000) inside our own open Main phase AND inside the opponent's own
  open Main phase, which is what separates `[All Turns]` from `[Your Turn]`.
  A second `BT19-060` sits on the same board with nothing under it and reads 5000 in
  both windows.

#### Evidence standards notes

- No `advance.fire*`, no `s.state.turnSeat` write. The previous suite proved the
  `[On Play]` reveal twice through `fireForPermanent(EffectTiming.OnPlay, ...)` and
  proved the inherited `[All Turns]` clause by assigning `s.state.turnSeat = 1` and
  calling `advance().recompute()`; both are replaced by the real turn loop.
- The opponent's turn is reached with `startTurnLoop()` + `endMainPhaseIfOpen(0)` +
  `waitForMainPhase(1)`, and closed with `surrender` + `await loop` — never
  `runTurn(1)` after `runTurn(0)`.
- Reveal endpoints are computed from the live deck at Main open (`deckAtMain`).
- Both seats hold security; no Digi-Egg in any deck or security; a spare playable
  card sits in hand so Main does not auto-pass. Breeding fixtures use `s.ready()` +
  intent, because a seeded `breeding` permanent stalls `advance.waitForMainPhase`.
- `BT19-060`'s own `[When Digivolving]` optional (play 1 `[Ryo Akiyama]`) is answered
  with `autoDeclineOptional`, so it cannot perturb the asserted DP endpoints.

"nameExact" }]` (bracketed name = exact, not the substring `match: "name"` trap),

excludeToken: true`, `optional: true`.

### BT19-059 — DeadlyAxemon

Lane 25. Base main `23eee9e5a`, branch `audit-bt19-reaudit`.
Module IR unchanged; only `BT19-059.test.ts` was rewritten. No effects.json resync needed.

#### Card summary

Catalog: Black/Purple Digimon, Lv.4, Champion, Virus, types Dark Animal / Twilight,
play cost 4, DP 4000, evoCosts Black Lv.3 and Purple Lv.3 at 3 memory. Rarity C,
max 4 in deck. No printed `[Digivolve]` line.

Printed clauses:

1. `＜Retaliation＞` (main)
2. `[On Deletion] ＜Save＞.`
3. Inherited: `＜Reboot＞.`

#### Q&A ids

`node tools/kb/query.mjs card BT19-059` -> `(no knowledge-base entries)`: no Q&A,
no errata, no banlist row, matching `KB-INDEX.md` ("0 / None"). Confirmed with the
tool, recorded in the test file header.

Rules read for the keywords: comprehensive §16-13 (＜Retaliation＞: a trigger effect
that deletes the battled opponent's Digimon when the Digimon with this effect is
deleted in battle) and §16-11 (＜Reboot＞: unsuspends during the opponent's unsuspend
phase; persistent).

#### Clause -> test -> IR

- Clause 1 -> `effects[0]`: `Static` with `keywords: [{ keyword: "Retaliation" }]`.
  A bare printed keyword, not an `[All Turns]` clause, so `Static` is right.
  - Proof by rules consequence: a 5000 DP attacker attacks the suspended
    DeadlyAxemon. It loses the battle and is deleted, and §16-13 takes the attacker
    with it. Endpoints: both battle areas empty, DeadlyAxemon's instance id is the
    only card in seat 1's trash, seat 0's trash holds exactly the attacker card, and
    seat 1's security is untouched (a permanent-target attack does not check
    security).
  - Negative control: an identical 4000 DP peer (BT1-014 Kokatorimon) in the same
    position leaves the attacker alive and seat 0's trash empty.
- Clause 2 -> `effects[1]`: `OnDeletion`, `keywords: [{ keyword: "Save" }]`,
  `PlaceUnder` with `underFilter { controller: "mine", kind: ["Tamer"],
excludeToken: true }`, `optional: true`. With the keyword present,
  `withSavePlacementDefaults` applies and the card lands at the BOTTOM (CR 4-3-2).
  - Positive: the resulting Tamer stack is `[self, pre-existing]` by instance id, the
    card is not in the trash, and an opponent-controlled Tamer (BT19-083) on the same
    board stays empty — the `controller: "mine"` gate.
  - Decline: the card is in the trash and the Tamer stack is empty.
- Clause 3 -> `effects[2]`: `Static`, `isInherited: true`, `keywords: [{ keyword:
"Reboot" }]`. `interpreter/effect.ts:636-643` treats this as the Reboot marker and
  grants the keyword permanently; the engine consumes it in
  `GameEngine.unsuspendRebootForSeat`.
  - Realistic stack case through the real turn loop: two identical BT1-014
    permanents on seat 0, one carrying a BT19-059 digivolution card. Both are
    suspended the real way — by attacking on their controller's turn — then
    `startTurnLoop()` + `endMainPhaseIfOpen(0)` + `waitForMainPhase(1)` reaches seat
    1's genuine unsuspend phase. Only the host stands back up; the bare twin stays
    suspended. No `turnSeat` write, no injected unsuspend.
- Evolution routes -> the printed evo costs. Black Lv.3 (BT2-052) and Purple Lv.3
  (BT2-067) both cost exactly 3 (9 -> 6 -> 3) with the base's instance id as the
  single stack entry and the two bonus draws visible in hand and deck; Green Lv.3
  (BT1-064) is refused on both the plain and the `useAlternateCost: true` intent.

The only Advance-Surface uses are `advance().verb.deletePermanent(..., "byEffect")`
for the ＜Save＞ tests and the turn-loop helpers `waitForMainPhase` /
`endMainPhaseIfOpen`. No `fire` / `fireTiming` / `fireSubTrigger`. Fixtures carry no
Digi-Egg and no numeric `security: <n>`.

##### Testkit note recorded during this lane

In the ＜Reboot＞ test, seat 0's Main auto-passes as soon as its last legal action is
spent, and the turn hand-over happens inside the very `settle` that observes the final
suspension — so reading `isSuspended` after that settle sees the post-unsuspend value
and proves nothing. The test therefore samples the mid-turn state through the
`onEvent` hook while `state.turnSeat === 0`, the same technique
`BT17-033.test.ts` uses for a during-battle DP value. This is the same class of trap
as the brief's "Start-of-Main tests that read memory only after `runTurn` completes".

#### Clause -> test -> IR

- **Clause 1 ＜Material Save 1＞** -> `effects[0]` `trigger: "Static"`,
  `keywords: [{ keyword: "MaterialSave", amount: 1 }]`.

- **Clause 2 ＜De-Digivolve1＞** -> `effects[1]/[2]` action 0, `kind: "DeDigivolve"`,

- **Clause 3 conditional deletion** -> `effects[1]/[2]` action 1, `kind: "Delete"`,
  `optional: true`, `condition { kind: "digiXrosCount", minimum: 2 }`,
  `filter { controller: "any", kind: ["Digimon","Tamer"], playCostLte: 3 }`.
  Three-way proof: fires on a 2-material DigiXros and takes the controller's own
  cost-2 Digimon (Q3124) while leaving the cost-5 BT19-020 peer alone; does NOT

  does NOT fire on a normal digivolve even though a matching cost-3 target is on

  `PlayWithoutCost`, `from: ["underMyTamers"]`, `payCost: false`, `optional: true`,
  `levelComparison { op: "lte", value: 4 }`,
  `nameOrTrait [{ tokens: ["Knightmon"], match: "text" }]`.

- **Clause 5 [DigiXros -2]** -> `digiXrosRequirementFor("BT19-063")`

### BT19-064 — Justimon: Blitz Arm

Lane 27. Base `23eee9e5a`. **Module IR changed** (`names` -> `namesExact` on the
printed `[Digivolve]` route), so `packages/shared/src/effects/effects.json` is

#### Card summary

Catalog: Black Digimon, Lv.6, Mega, Vaccine, Cyborg, play cost 6, DP 11000,
evoCosts Black Lv.5 at 3 memory, `isAce: true`, `overflowMemory: 4`.

Printed clauses:

1. `[Digivolve][Justimon: Accel Arm]/[Justimon: Critical Arm]: Cost 1`
2. `[Hand] [Counter] ＜Blast Digivolve＞`
3. `[On Play] [When Digivolving] This Digimon gains ＜Blocker＞ and isn't affected
by your opponent's Digimon's effects until the end of your opponent's turn.`
4. `[When Digivolving] [When Attacking] [Once Per Turn] By trashing 1 Option card
in the battle area, unsuspend this Digimon.`
5. ACE `Overflow ＜-4＞` (catalog-driven: `isAce` + `overflowMemory`).

#### Q&A ids

| Id                                                                                                             | Covered by                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Q3126 ("1 Option card in the battle area" = an Option a _place this card in the battle area_ effect put there) | IR assertion `placedInBattleAreaByEffect: true` in the catalog/IR test, plus the two behavioural payment tests, which only ever pay with a `placedByEffect` Option permanent. See "Remaining gaps" for why the false case cannot be seeded. |
| Q3127 (either player's Option card is a legal cost)                                                            | `trashes the OPPONENT's placed Option to unsuspend itself (Q3127)` — the only Option on the board is seat 1's; it is trashed to seat 1's trash by instance id and the controller's own trash stays empty.                                   |

#### Clause -> test -> IR

- **Clause 1 alternate route** -> `digivolutionRequirement`
  `[{ namesExact: ["Justimon: Accel Arm", "Justimon: Critical Arm"], cost: 1, isAlternate: true }]`.
  Both named bases (BT11-073, BT10-067) digivolve for exactly 1 memory (10 -> 9)
  with stack identity, hand size and bonus draw asserted. The fallback test
  digivolves from BT19-063 (Black Lv.5) with `useAlternateCost: true` and shows
  the memory delta is 3, not 1 — `{ok:true}` alone would not have discriminated
  the two routes. Illegal sources EX8-054 `Justimon (X Antibody)` (Black Lv.6,
  wrong name, wrong level for the normal route) and BT1-014 (Red Lv.4) are both
  rejected as `invalid-evolution`.
- **Clause 2 ＜Blast Digivolve＞** -> `effects[0]` `trigger: "Counter"`,
  `isFromHand: true`, `keywords: [{ keyword: "BlastDigivolve" }]`.
  Proved inside the real production turn loop: on the opponent's turn the plain
  digivolve intent is refused `not-your-turn`; the opponent then declares a real
  attack, and the same intent with `useBlastDigivolve: true` succeeds with the
  memory unchanged (the cost waiver, `actions/digivolve.ts:662`).
- **Clause 3 ＜Blocker＞ + immunity** -> `effects[1]/[2]`:
  `GainKeyword { Blocker }` and `Restrict { restriction: "beAffected",
fromSourceKind: ["Digimon"], byOpponentEffectsOnly: true }`, both
  `duration: "untilOpponentTurnEnd"` (a real `EffectDurationRef`).
  - Grant vs peer: `hasKeyword` / `isRestrictedByEffect` true on the digivolved
    Digimon and false on an ungranted peer Digimon on the same board.
  - Immunity consequence: on the opponent's REAL turn they play BT1-055 Angemon
    (`[On Play] 1 of your opponent's Digimon gets -3000 DP for the turn`) pinned
    onto the immune Digimon — nothing moves. A second test pins the identical
    effect onto the unprotected peer, which loses its full 3000 DP. That pairing
    is what makes the first reading protection rather than a dead effect.
  - Blocker consequence: a real opponent attack aimed at the player is taken by
    the granted blocker through a real `declareBlock` intent; the 3000 DP
    attacker is deleted and the security stack is untouched.
  - Duration: the grants are still live at the moment the opponent's effect
    resolves and are both gone once the loop returns to the controller's Main.
- **Clause 4 [Once Per Turn] unsuspend** -> `effects[3]` (`WhenDigivolving`) and
  `effects[4]` (`WhenAttacking`), both `frequency: "OncePerTurn"` with
  `sharedUseKey: "ir-shared-0"`, action `Unsuspend` on `isSelfRef` with a
  `trash` cost over `{ zone: "battleArea", controllerDefault: "any",
kind: ["Option"], placedInBattleAreaByEffect: true }`.
  - Q3127 payment on the opponent's Option (above).
  - Shared once-per-turn: digivolving onto a suspended base pays one Option and
    unsuspends; the same turn's attack cannot pay again — the second Option
    survives and the attacker ends the attack suspended.
  - Real turn-loop reset plus the printed consequence: attack 1 pays and
    unsuspends (so a second attack is legal), attack 2 finds the use spent and
    stays suspended, and after a full opponent turn the next own turn's attack
    pays the second Option.
  - No-Option control: with only Digimon permanents on the board the attack still
    resolves, nothing is trashed, and the attacker stays suspended.
- **Clause 5 ACE Overflow ＜-4＞** -> catalog `isAce`/`overflowMemory: 4`.
  Proved behaviourally: the ACE loses a real battle to a seeded suspended 20000
  DP wall and memory moves 4 to the opponent (3 -> -1), with the permanent and
  its digivolution card in the trash.

#### Defect fixed

`digivolutionRequirement` used `names`, which is the SUBSTRING gate
(`engine/cards/cardData.ts:482-484`, "[X] in its name"). The printed route
`[Justimon: Accel Arm]/[Justimon: Critical Arm]` is a bracketed exact reference
and must use `namesExact` (`cardData.ts:491-494`), which reads the exact-name
channel only. Fixed in `BT19-064.ts`.

Honest limitation: with the current catalog the change is not behaviourally
discriminable. No printed card's name CONTAINS "Justimon: Accel Arm" or
"Justimon: Critical Arm" without being that card, and no card is printed as
"also treated as [Justimon: Accel Arm]", so both modes accept and reject exactly
the same bases today. The tests assert both legal routes, the normal-route
fallback cost and the illegal sources under the corrected gate; the IR assertion
in the catalog test pins the mode itself.

#### Remaining gaps

- **Q3126's false case cannot be seeded.** A Board Spec Option permanent with
  `placedByEffect: false` is the illegal state that §17-1-3-2-2's rule sweep
  exists to clean up: the engine removes it from the battle area before the cost
  is ever offered, so it cannot serve as a "still on the board but not choosable"
  near-miss. The nearest available control is the Digimon-only board, which is
  tested. The predicate itself is asserted on the IR.
- **Immunity is applied at resolution, not at targeting.** The immune Digimon is
  still offered in the `chooseTargets` candidate list for an opposing Digimon's
  effect (observed: both permanents offered), and the effect simply does nothing
  when it lands on it. This matches the "can't be returned" pattern in the trap
  list rather than the candidate-pool exclusion described in
  `conformance/ch15-03-targeting-and-selection.test.ts:296`. Not a defect in this
  card's IR; flagged for whoever owns that seam.
- `abortOnDecline: true` sits on the sole action of both once-per-turn effects
  and is dead (lane 4/lane 8 finding). Left alone deliberately: removing it would
  churn the IR for no behavioural change.

#### Testkit note for the coordinator

An `async` helper that `return`s the running turn loop AWAITS it — the test then
hangs for the full 15 s vitest timeout. The helper here returns `{ loop }`.
Separately, a value with a `forTheTurn` / `untilOpponentTurnEnd` duration read
after `settle` on the opponent's turn is already expired, because their Main
auto-passes as soon as they have no legal action left; these tests read such
values through `setupEngine`'s `onEvent` hook at `effectResolved` instead.

#### Catalog discrepancies

None. The catalog carries `isAce: true` and `overflowMemory: 4` even though the
`effectText` field does not spell out the ACE/Overflow line; that matches how
every other ACE card in the catalog is stored and the behaviour is correct.

#### Q&A ids

`node tools/kb/query.mjs card BT19-065` reports 2 entries, matching `KB-INDEX.md`.

| Q&A   | Ruling                                                                     | Test                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| ----- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Q3128 | The `[On Play]`/`[When Digivolving]` delete may also hit YOUR OWN Digimon. | "Q3128: the same clause may delete YOUR OWN level 5 Digimon" — the only legal target on the board is seat 0's own Lv.5, and it lands in seat 0's trash.                                                                                                          |
| Q3129 | The inherited redirect may pick a Digimon that is not affected by effects. | "Q3129: the redirect still lands on a Digimon that cannot be affected by effects" — a `beAffected` restriction is armed on the [Composite] Digimon through the production restriction primitive, and the redirect still moves the attack off the player onto it. |

Comprehensive rules consulted for clause 4 (`node tools/kb/query.mjs rules
"DigiXros"`): §7-2-2-1 reduces the play cost by the printed amount **for each card
placed**, and §7-2-2-4 lets the player place **any number** of the specified cards
(only 0 is forbidden once declared). That settles the two shapes that looked
suspicious in the IR: `count: 1` really is the per-material discount (not a material
count), and there is correctly no minimum-material floor for "5 … cards" — only the
`maxMaterials: 5` cap.

#### Clause -> test -> IR

- Clauses 1 -> `effects[0]` (`OnPlay`) and `effects[1]` (`WhenDigivolving`), each a
  single `Delete` with
  `target.filter { kind: ["Digimon"], levelComparison: { op: "lte", value: 5 } }`,
  `count: 1`. No `controller` predicate — that absence is exactly what Q3128 needs,
  and it is asserted in the IR test and proved behaviourally.
  - `[On Play]` positive: a public `playCard` intent for 11 memory (12 -> 1) deletes
    the opponent's Lv.5 (into their trash) and leaves the Lv.6 peer on the board by
    permanent id. No `actionRejected` event.
  - Level near-miss: the Lv.6 HiAndromon on the same board is never chosen.
  - `[When Digivolving]` positive: a public `digivolve` intent from a Black Lv.5
    base deletes the opposing Lv.5, memory 8 -> 5, the base instance id is the single
    stack entry, and the digivolution draw lands in hand.
- Clause 2 -> `effects[2]`: `OnDeletion` / `PlayWithoutCost`,
  `filter { controller: "mine", kind: ["Digimon"], levelComparison lte 5,
nameOrTrait [{ tokens: ["Cyborg","Composite"], match: "trait" }] }`,
  `from: ["trash"]`, `payCost: false`, `optional: true`. `match: "trait"` is the
  exact-trait form the printed "with the [X] trait" wording requires. Loose-card
  matchers do read `levelComparison` (`interpreter/matching/definition.ts:139-147`);
  only the object `playCost: {op,value}` form is dropped for loose cards, and this
  card does not use it.
  - Positive through a real battle: Machinedramon (11000) attacks a suspended 12000
    DP wall, is deleted, and BT2-060 Megadramon (Lv.5 [Cyborg]) enters the battle
    area as a fresh permanent with an empty stack.
  - Near-miss peers in the same trash: BT2-064 HiAndromon (Lv.6 [Cyborg] — wrong
    level) and BT10-064 Gogmamon (Lv.5 [Rock] — wrong trait) both stay in the trash,
    asserted by instance id, alongside the deleted Machinedramon.
  - Decline (`autoDeclineOptional`): the Megadramon stays in the trash and the
    battle area is empty.
- Clause 3 -> `effects[3]`: `Rule` / `GrantStatic`, `grant: "trait"`,
  `tokens: ["Composite"]` — the `Rule`/`GrantStatic` node the brief's trap list
  requires for a printed `[Rule] Trait:` line, not a comment.
  - Cross-card consequence: `observe(...).hasEffectiveTrait` reads Composite on a
    Machinedramon permanent and not on a Lv.5 [Rock] peer sharing the board (which
    does read its own `Rock` trait, so the observation is not vacuous). This is the
    same trait token clause 5's redirect filter and clause 4's DigiXros recipe read.
- Clause 4 -> `digiXrosRequirement`: one slot, `levelComparison lte 5`,
  `nameOrTrait [{ tokens: ["Cyborg","Composite"], match: "trait" }]`,
  `differentCardNumbers: true`, `count: 1`, `maxMaterials: 5`.
  - Positive: a public `playCard` intent carrying `digiXros.materialInstanceIds`
    with five different-numbered Lv.5-or-lower [Cyborg]/[Composite] cards (including
    BT3-059 and ST5-05 — the SAME name Commandramon on different card numbers, which
    the "different card numbers" wording allows). Memory 6 -> 0 (11 - 5 x 1 = 6), all
    five instance ids are under the played permanent, the spare hand card is
    untouched, and `[On Play]` still fired and deleted the opposing Lv.5 — proving
    the DigiXros play is a play (§7-2-2-7).
  - Negatives, each rejected with memory and hand unchanged: a 6th material
    (`maxMaterials`), two prints of the same cardId (`differentCardNumbers`), a
    non-[Cyborg]/[Composite] material, and a Lv.6 [Cyborg] material.
- Clause 5 -> `effects[4]`: `OpponentsTurn`, `isInherited: true`,
  `frequency: "OncePerTurn"`, a `SubTrigger` on `whenOpponentAttacks` wrapping a
  `RedirectAttack` whose target filter is
  `{ controller: "mine", kind: ["Digimon"], nameOrTrait [{ tokens:
["Composite","Wicked God"], match: "trait" }] }`, `optional: true`.
  - Realistic stack + real turn loop: seat 0 has a BT1-014 host carrying a BT19-065
    digivolution card, a 7000 DP [Composite] Deltamon, and a deliberately WEAK
    2000 DP non-[Composite] peer. `startTurnLoop()` + `waitForMainPhase(0)` +
    `endMainPhaseIfOpen(0)` + `waitForMainPhase(1)` reaches seat 1's real turn (no
    `turnSeat` write). Seat 1's 3000 DP attacker declares an attack on the PLAYER;
    the redirect moves it onto the Deltamon, which wins: seat 0's security is still
    3, seat 0's trash is empty (so the weak peer was not the chosen target — had the
    trait filter leaked, that peer would have died), and seat 1 lost the attacker.
  - `[Once Per Turn]`: a second attack on the same opponent turn is NOT redirected
    and takes a security card (3 -> 2), with seat 0's board unchanged.

Every behavioural test uses public intents (`playCard`, `digivolve`, `attack`,
`declareBlock`-free, `surrender`) or the real turn loop. The single Advance-Surface
use is `verb.restrict(..., "beAffected", ...)` in the Q3129 test, which ARMS the
board state the ruling is about; the clause itself is still exercised by a real
opponent-turn attack. No injected timing, no `turnSeat` write. Fixtures use inert
main-deck Digimon; no Digi-Egg in deck or security, no numeric `security: <n>`.

None found in the module IR. Every shape the prior typed revalidation corrected is
confirmed correct against the catalog and the comprehensive rules:

- `count: 1` + `maxMaterials: 5` for `[DigiXros -1] 5 … cards` — correct per
  §7-2-2-1 (per-card discount) and §7-2-2-4 (any number, capped by the printed 5).
- `match: "trait"` (exact) on both trait filters — correct for "with the [X] trait".
- `Rule` + `GrantStatic` for the `[Rule] Trait:` line — the required node kind.
- `OpponentsTurn` + `frequency: "OncePerTurn"` for the printed
  `[Opponent's Turn] [Once Per Turn]` — not the `Static` trap.

The pre-existing test file (46 lines) was replaced: it asserted an IR skeleton and
proved exactly one clause with a single "the opponent's battle area is empty" check.
It had no catalog assertion, no Q&A coverage, no `[When Digivolving]` branch, no
`[On Deletion]` test, no DigiXros test at all, no evolution route or illegal source,
no near-miss peer and no inherited-effect test. No red tests retained.

#### Remaining gaps

- Q3129 is proved against an `UnaffectedByEffects`-style `beAffected` restriction
  armed through the production primitive rather than a printed card that grants it.
  No inert card in the catalog prints that immunity, so a card-driven fixture would
  drag a second card's whole clause set into this test.
- The redirect's `optional: true` decline branch is not separately tested: the
  redirect and the `[On Deletion]` play are both optional, and a blanket
  `autoDeclineOptional` cannot separate two optionals in one flow (brief trap,
  lane 11). The decline branch IS tested for the `[On Deletion]` clause.
- The DigiXros cost is proved at exactly 5 materials. A 3-material DigiXros (legal
  per §7-2-2-4, cost 8) is not exercised.
- `[Rule] Trait` is proved by the effective-trait observation and by the redirect
  filter it feeds. A cross-card case where another card's printed `[Composite]`
  filter reads a Machinedramon permanent is not built.

#### Catalog discrepancies

The catalog stores this card's text with **U+00A0 (non-breaking space)** separators:
in `inheritedEffectText` before "you may change", and twice in the DigiXros header
line (`[DigiXros<U+00A0>-1]` and `[Composite]<U+00A0>trait`). Content matches the
official printing; only the separator bytes differ. The test normalizes U+00A0 to a
plain space before comparing and says so inline. Not edited — catalog is out of
lane scope.

Second (non-)discrepancy worth recording: `types` already contains `Composite`
alongside `Machine`, so the `[Rule]` grant is redundant with the catalog rather than
load-bearing. It is still the correct IR node — the printed line must compile to
something — and the behaviour is identical either way.

#### Defects fixed locally

1. **＜Save＞ was untagged.** The `OnDeletion` effect carried a bare positionless
   `PlaceUnder`. `withSavePlacementDefaults`
   (`apps/api/src/engine/effects/interpreter/registration/normalize.ts:115-126`)
   only defaults `position: "bottom"` on an effect whose `keywords` include
   `Save`, so `runPlaceUnder` read `belowTop: action.position !== "bottom"` as
   true and `primitives.ts:2065` pushed the card directly BENEATH the Tamer's top
   card instead of at the bottom — inverting the stack and the inherited effects it
   grants (CR 4-3-2, 16-20). Fix: `keywords: [{ keyword: "Save", raw: "＜Save＞" }]`.
   Proof it mattered: with the tag removed, `＜Save＞ places the card at the BOTTOM
…` and the IR test fail (3 failed | 11 passed).
2. **DigiXros recipe was uncapped.** A single-slot recipe with no `maxMaterials`
   accepts any number of matching materials (`materialsSatisfyRecipe`,
   `apps/api/src/engine/actions/digiXros.ts:536-556`; the cap check is at
   `:290-294`), so two [Nene Amano] cards bought -4 on a recipe that prints one
   material. Fix: `maxMaterials: 1`, matching the BT21-021 / BT18-065 precedent.
   Proof: without it, `refuses the near-miss Tamer …` fails.

#### Retained reds

None. No `it.fails` / `it.skip` in this file.

#### Remaining gaps

- The `[Rule] Trait: Has [Composite] type.` line is redundant against this
  catalog: `types` already lists `Composite`, so the `GrantStatic` node cannot be
  isolated behaviourally — the trait consequence is proved, but it would hold with
  the node deleted. See the catalog note below.
- The `[Twilight]/[Composite]` trait gate is proved exact only by construction: no
  printed trait in the catalog has "Twilight" or "Composite" as a strict substring,
  so there is no near-miss trait peer to separate `match: "trait"` from
  `traitContains`.
- `PlayWithoutCost.target.filter` narrows to `kind: ["Tamer"]`, which the printed
  text does not say. Every card named exactly "Nene Amano" is a Tamer today, so it
  is unobservable; left alone rather than churning the IR.

#### Catalog discrepancies

- `types` for BT19-068 is `["Unidentified", "Twilight", "Composite"]`, i.e. the
  `[Rule]`-granted `[Composite]` is already folded into the printed type list. On
  the physical card the `[Rule]` line exists precisely because `[Composite]` is NOT
  in the printed type box. Reported, not edited (catalog is out of lane scope).

   `declining the 'by deleting' condition …` and the IR test fail
   (2 failed | 12 passed).

#### Card

#### Rulings

Q3133 mechanism: the redirect targets the source's OWN side, and
`isPermanentUnaffectable` (`interpreter/matching/permanent.ts:858-867`) returns false whenever
`source.ownerSeat === permanent.controllerSeat`, so an own-side "isn't affected by effects"
grant cannot remove the Digimon from the pool. The test seeds that grant through the
production `restrict` primitive and shows the switch still lands.

| Same on digivolve                 | "[When Digivolving] fires off a real Purple Lv5 stack for 3 memory and draws 1"                  | `WhenDigivolving` -> same action                                                                       |
| "You may"                         | "[On Play] declining the optional revive leaves the trash untouched"                             | `optional: true`                                                                                       |

| "with the [Royal Knight] trait"   | same test (candidate sets recorded; ST13-12 Knightmon never offered)                             | `nameOrTrait: [{ tokens: ["Royal Knight"], match: "trait" }]` — exact, per the brief's name/trait rule |
| `[Once Per Turn]`                 | same test (second attack of the same opponent turn is not switched)                              | `frequency: "OncePerTurn"`                                                                             |
| Evolution routes / illegal source | "[When Digivolving] ..." and "refuses an illegal digivolution source"                            | catalog `evoCosts`                                                                                     |

Evidence notes:

- The redirect is proved through the real turn loop: my wall is suspended by attacking the
  player on my own turn (a seeded `suspended: true` would stand up at my unsuspend phase), then

### BT19-073 — LordKnightmon (X Antibody)

#### Card

Purple/Black Lv6 Mega, Virus, Holy Warrior / X Antibody / Royal Knight. Play cost 12, DP 12000,
evolution costs: Black Lv5 for 4, Purple Lv5 for 4. No inherited text.

Printed clauses:

1. `[Digivolve][LordKnightmon]: Cost 1`
2. `＜Collision＞.`
3. `＜Piercing＞`
4. `[When Digivolving] For each of your Digimon, ＜De-Digivolve1＞ 1 of your opponent's Digimon.`
5. `Then, until the end of their turn, 1 of their Digimon can't digivolve.`
6. `[All Turns] While [LordKnightmon]/[X Antibody] is in this Digimon's digivolution cards, all
of your Digimon with [Knightmon] in its text gain ＜Alliance＞ and get +3000 DP.`

#### Rulings

| Q&A   | Question                                                                                                                                                                        | Test                                                                                          |
| ----- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Q3134 | With 2 of my Digimon, how many opponent Digimon can ＜De-Digivolve 1＞ affect? (A: 1 — you choose 1 opponent Digimon, then give IT ＜De-Digivolve 1＞ for each of your Digimon) | "Q3134: de-digivolves ONE opponent Digimon once per your Digimon, then locks a DIFFERENT one" |

Supporting rules: Q4568 (a scaled ＜De-Digivolve 1＞ is the peel repeated, not ＜De-Digivolve N＞ —
the engine implements it as a repetition, `interpreter/actions/digivolution.ts:24-48`), and
comprehensive §16-30 for ＜Collision＞ (all opponent Digimon gain ＜Blocker＞ and the opponent must
block when able).

The prior audit's "independent selection" for the digivolve lock is CORRECT against the print:
"Then, ... 1 of their Digimon can't digivolve" is a fresh choice, not the ＜De-Digivolve＞ target.
The Q3134 test proves it by scripting the two decisions onto two different opponent Digimon and
asserting that only the second one is restricted.

#### Defects fixed in the module

1. `digivolutionRequirement` used the SUBSTRING gate `names: ["LordKnightmon"]` for the printed
   bracketed `[Digivolve][LordKnightmon]` route. Substring matching lets this card's own print
   ("LordKnightmon (X Antibody)") serve as its own source. Changed to
   `namesExact: ["LordKnightmon"]` (the trap lanes 16 and 19 recorded).
   Proof: "refuses its own print as a source" and "charges the normal Lv5 cost of 4 when the
   base is not exactly [LordKnightmon]" (a `useAlternateCost: true` that silently falls back
   costs 4, not 1).
2. The `[All Turns]` condition matched `[LordKnightmon]` with `match: "name"` (substring).
   Changed to `match: "nameExact"`. This one is not behaviourally separable on the current
   card pool — the only card whose name contains but does not equal "LordKnightmon" is
   BT19-073 itself, which satisfies the same condition through its `X Antibody` trait — so it
   is a correctness fix backed by the IR assertion only.
3. Q3134 violation. `DeDigivolve` carried `bindAs: "deDigivolveTarget"`, which nothing reads on
   a non-`SelectBind` target, and the engine re-resolves the target on every scaled repetition.
   The observed behaviour was one target choice PER repetition, so two of my Digimon let the
   effect peel two DIFFERENT opponent Digimon — the exact case Q3134 answers with "1 Digimon".
   Fixed inside the card: a leading `SelectBind` binds the single opponent Digimon, and
   `DeDigivolve` resolves through `fromSelectionRef: "deDigivolveTarget"`, so each repetition
   peels the same Digimon.

#### Clause -> test -> IR

| ----------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `[Digivolve][LordKnightmon]: Cost 1`                        | "takes the printed [LordKnightmon] route for 1 memory" (memory 10 -> 9, stack identity, draw)                                                   | `digivolutionRequirement: [{ namesExact: ["LordKnightmon"], cost: 1, isAlternate: true }]`                                  |
| exactness of that route                                     | "charges the normal Lv5 cost of 4 ..." and "refuses its own print as a source"                                                                  | same                                                                                                                        |
| ＜Collision＞                                               | "＜Collision＞ forces the block and ＜Piercing＞ sends the excess into security" (`declineBlock` refused, a plain Digimon blocks)               | `Static` effect, `keywords: [{ keyword: "Collision" }]`                                                                     |
| ＜Piercing＞                                                | same test (blocker deleted, opponent security drops)                                                                                            | `Static` effect, `keywords: [{ keyword: "Piercing" }]`                                                                      |
| ＜De-Digivolve 1＞ per your Digimon on ONE opponent Digimon | "Q3134: ..." (2 of my Digimon peel the chosen victim to its bottom card; the other opponent Digimon keeps its full stack)                       | `SelectBind` + `DeDigivolve { amount: 1, scaling { per: 1, filter mine Digimon, unit: "cards" } }`                          |
| "Then ... 1 of their Digimon can't digivolve"               | "Q3134: ..." (independent target) and "keeps the digivolve lock through the opponent's own turn"                                                | `Restrict { restriction: "digivolve", duration: "untilOpponentTurnEnd" }`                                                   |
| lock duration and effect                                    | "keeps the digivolve lock ..." (on the opponent's real turn the locked Digimon's digivolve intent is refused while an unlocked peer's succeeds) | same                                                                                                                        |
| `[All Turns]` gate                                          | "[All Turns] grants nothing without [LordKnightmon]/[X Antibody] in the digivolution cards"                                                     | `condition { kind: "selfHasInDigivolutionCards", nameOrTrait: [nameExact LordKnightmon, trait X Antibody] }`                |
| ＜Alliance＞ + 3000 DP to your [Knightmon]-in-text Digimon  | "[All Turns] buffs only your own [Knightmon]-in-text Digimon while the gate holds"                                                              | `GainKeyword { Alliance }` + `ModifyDP { 3000 }`, `nameOrTrait: [{ tokens: ["Knightmon"], match: "text" }]`, `count: "all"` |

itself 12000 -> 15000 with ＜Alliance＞ (its own name carries [Knightmon]); the near-miss peer
BT12-069 Footmon stays 9000 with no ＜Alliance＞; the opponent's identical ST13-12 stays 7000.

- the 10-trash branch really is an `instead` branch, not an extra deletion

- the result really is the opponent's TOP security card, not an arbitrary one
  (proved by asserting the surviving security order by instance id).

`abortOnDecline: true` on the sole action of the `[When Attacking]` effect is dead
(lane 4 / 008 finding). It was left in place rather than churning the IR, since
removing it would trigger a needless `effects.json` resync.

The prior test file was replaced: it asserted only IR shape plus one deletion
scenario, used no turn loop, proved neither evolution route, neither the Blast
Digivolve keyword nor the whole `[When Attacking]` clause.

#### Remaining gaps

- **Same-turn refusal for `[Once Per Turn]` is not proved behaviourally.** The
  clause is `[When Attacking]`, and an attacker suspends when it attacks. There is
  no public intent that unsuspends a permanent mid-turn, so a second attack by the
  same Digimon in the same turn cannot be reached through public intents; a second
  copy of the card would carry its own per-permanent counter and prove nothing.
  What IS proved: the frequency is on the effect in the IR, and the clause fires
  again on the controller's next own turn driven by the real turn loop (unsuspend
  phase included), with the intermediate turn-1 endpoint asserted.
- ＜Blast Digivolve＞ is exercised through the production counter window and the
  `blast-digivolve:<permanentId>` effect key; the KB's Q3056-style exclusions do
  not apply to this card (it prints no stack-count route).

#### Catalog discrepancies

None. The catalog print matches the official card, including `isAce: true` and
`overflowMemory: 5`, which the `effectText` itself does not spell out (the same
shape as BT19-050).

#### Defects

##### Fixed: the `[Digivolve]` route used the substring gate

`BT19-075.ts` carried `digivolutionRequirement: [{ names: ["Millenniummon"], cost: 2 }]`.
`names` is the SUBSTRING gate (`apps/api/src/engine/cards/cardData.ts`), so it also
matched `BT19-101 ZeedMillenniummon`, letting a Lv.7 ZeedMillenniummon act as a
cost-2 base for a card that prints the bracketed exact name `[Millenniummon]`.
Changed to `namesExact: ["Millenniummon"]`.

The fix is discriminated, not merely asserted: reverting the field to `names` and
re-running `near miss: ZeedMillenniummon only CONTAINS 'Millenniummon', so no route
accepts it` fails with `expected true to be false` on the digivolve intent — i.e.
the old IR really did accept the illegal base. Restored to `namesExact` afterwards.

Because `digivolutionRequirementsFor` reads `compiledEffects` (which
`registerIrCard` overwrites at import time), the change takes effect for the
engine, and `packages/shared/src/effects/effects.json` is now stale for this card.

##### Confirmed correct (previously unverified)

- `chooser: "opponent"` on the hand trash matches Q3135.
- The Tamer count is scaled off `trashedThisEffect`, not off any board or hand total.
- The would-leave replacement carries `sourceFilter.isSelfRef` (without it,
  `replacement.ts:238-241` takes the generic branch and would protect both seats).
- The watcher observes both seats' other Digimon and Tamers and uses the canonical
  `SecurityManipulation op "trashTop" controller: "opponent"` operation.

The prior test file was replaced: it seeded a Digi-Egg in security, drove the
watcher through `advance.verb.deletePermanent` (injected timing, no behavioural
credit), and proved neither evolution route, the replacement, the `[Once Per Turn]`
frequency, nor the scaling.

#### Remaining gaps

- Same-turn refusal for clause 4 IS proved (two Tamer deletions inside one
  `[On Play]` resolution trash only one security card). The next-own-turn RESET is
  not proved separately; the two-deletions-one-security case plus the IR frequency
  field are what stand behind it.
- The engine's `op: "trash"` / `op: "trashTop"` are aliases
  (`interpreter/actions/security.ts:143-144`); this module uses `trashTop`, its
  lane-mate BT19-074 uses `trash`. Cosmetic, no behaviour difference.

#### Catalog discrepancies

None. Play cost 15 is genuine (the card is intended to be digivolved into), which
is why the `[On Play]` tests set memory inside the open Main phase before playing.

#### Card summary

Catalog (`packages/shared/src/cards/data/cards.json`): White Digimon, Lv.5, Ultimate,
Vaccine, `[Fairy]` `[Xros Heart]`, play cost 5, DP 4000, `evoCosts: []`.

Printed clauses:

1. `[Digivolve][Shademon]: Cost 2`
2. `[On Play] Reveal top 3 cards of your deck. Add 1 card with the [Xros Heart]/[Blue
Flare]/[Twilight] trait from among to your hand. Return the remaining to the bottom of
deck. Then, you may play 1 Tamer card with a play cost of 4 or less from your hand
without paying the cost.`
3. `[On Deletion] ＜Save＞.`

#### Rules read

- `node tools/kb/query.mjs card BT19-076` -> "(no knowledge-base entries)", matching
  `KB-INDEX.md` (0 Q&A). No ruling was claimed without that check.
- White (`comprehensive 2-4-2`): one of the seven ordinary colours; it carries no special
  play or evolution rule. Only _level-less_ cards get special handling (`2-9-2`), and
  BT19-076 prints Lv.5, so it plays and digivolves normally. The level-less rules matter for
  BT19-077 / BT19-078 in this lane, not here.
- ＜Save＞: `comprehensive 16-20-3` (optional placement under one of your Tamers) and
  `CR 4-3-2` (a card placed under a Tamer that already has cards under it goes to the
  BOTTOM of the stack).

#### Q&A ids

| Id            | Covered by                                                                                            |
| ------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| (none listed) | KB query returns no entries; ＜Save＞ is proved against `comprehensive 16-20-3` / `CR 4-3-2` instead. |

#### Clause -> test -> IR

- **Clause 1** -> `digivolutionRequirement: [{ namesExact: ["Shademon"], cost: 2, isAlternate: true }]`.
  - `digivolves from a [Shademon] base for cost 2, keeping the source under it and drawing 1`:
    BT19-068 Shademon base, `useAlternateCost: true`, `alternateRequirementIndex: 0`.
    Memory 5 -> 3 (the cost-2 route is what discriminates it), source instance id under the
    new top, `currentDP` 4000, one bonus draw, and the deck untouched otherwise — proving
    digivolving is not playing, so the `[On Play]` reveal never ran.
  - `also accepts the other printing ... but refuses an unrelated Lv.4 base`: BT5-065 (a second
    printing whose printed name is exactly `Shademon`) qualifies; BT1-014 Kokatorimon, a Lv.4
    base with no name match, is refused — the catalog prints no primary `evoCosts`, so no
    route at all reaches it.
- **Clause 2** -> `effects[OnPlay].actions[0]` `RevealAdd` (`revealCount: 3`,
  `rest: "deckBottom"`, add filter `nameOrTrait` tokens `["Xros Heart","Blue Flare","Twilight"]`
  with `match: "trait"` — printed as traits, so exact trait match is correct) and
  `actions[1]` `PlayWithoutCost` (`from: ["hand"]`, `payCost: false`, `optional: true`,
  `kind: ["Tamer"]`, `playCostLte: 4` — the scalar loose-card key, not the dropped
  `playCost: {op,value}` object form).
  - `adds the trait match, bottoms the rest in order, and plays a cost-4-or-less Tamer for
free`: deck top `BT10-058` (`[Twilight]`/`[Xros Heart]`) is added; near misses `BT1-012`
    `[Bird]` and `BT1-013` `[Avian]` go to the deck bottom in reveal order (exact deck order
    asserted); `BT19-081` Kiriha (play cost 3) is played for free; `BT13-095` Marcus Damon
    (play cost 5) stays in hand. Memory 10 -> 5 (the 5 play cost only), no pending decision.
  - `adds nothing when none of the 3 reveals carries the trait`: all three bottomed, hand
    empty, memory still 10 -> 5.
  - `leaves the Tamer in hand when the optional play is declined`: `autoDeclineOptional`
    unambiguously answers this effect's ONE optional (the reveal/add is mandatory).
- **Clause 3** -> `effects[OnDeletion]` `keywords: [{ keyword: "Save" }]` plus a real
  `PlaceUnder` (`target.isSelf`, `underFilter` `controller: "mine", kind: ["Tamer"]`,
  `optional: true`, `position: "bottom"` supplied by the registration normalizer).
  - `＜Save＞s itself to the bottom of a Tamer's stack after losing a real battle`: Luminamon
    (4000 DP) attacks a seeded suspended 5000 DP opponent wall on its own turn and loses the
    battle. The Tamer's stack becomes `[luminaInstanceId, olderInstanceId]` — bottom-first, so
    the ＜Save＞d card is at the BOTTOM (CR 4-3-2). Trash empty.
  - `goes to the trash instead when its controller has no Tamer`: the opponent's Tamer is not
    a legal host ("your Tamers"); Luminamon lands in the trash and the opposing Tamer's stack
    stays empty.

#### Peer / stack proof

- Near-miss trait peers in the reveal (`BT1-012` `[Bird]`, `BT1-013` `[Avian]`) and a
  near-miss cost peer for the Tamer play (`BT13-095`, play cost 5).
- Near-miss ＜Save＞ host: an _opponent-controlled_ Tamer that must not receive the card.
- Realistic stack: the ＜Save＞ test seeds the Tamer with an existing digivolution card, so the
  bottom-placement rule is asserted against a non-empty stack rather than an empty one.
- Evolution peer: BT5-065, a different card number with the same exact printed name.

#### Defects found and fixed locally

1. **`[On Deletion] ＜Save＞` was dead.** The effect carried `keywords: [{ keyword: "Save" }]`
   with `actions: []`. `withSavePlacementDefaults`
   (`apps/api/src/engine/effects/interpreter/registration/normalize.ts:115`) only defaults the
   POSITION of an existing `PlaceUnder`; nothing in the engine synthesizes the placement from
   the keyword alone (`rg '"Save"' apps/api/src/engine` finds only the keyword token list, the
   combat regex and that normalizer). The card was therefore trashed on deletion. Fixed by
   adding the `PlaceUnder` action in the BT19-020 / BT19-022 shape.
2. **`[Digivolve][Shademon]` used the substring gate.** `names: ["Shademon"]` -> `namesExact`
   (lane 5 / BT19-012 finding). No live near-miss exists in the catalog today (nothing is
   named `*Shademon*` without being exactly `Shademon`), so this is correctness hardening
   rather than an observed misbehaviour; it is asserted structurally.

#### Remaining gaps

- The `namesExact` change has no behavioural near-miss because the catalog has no card whose
  name merely contains "Shademon". Asserted structurally only.

#### Catalog discrepancies

- `evoCosts: []` on a printed Lv.5 Digimon: the catalog records no primary digivolution
  requirement, so the `[Digivolve][Shademon]` route is the card's only way onto the board by
  evolution. Not verified against the physical card; reported, not edited.
- `effectText` reads "Add 1 card ... from among to your hand" — the catalog text is missing
  "them" ("from among them"). Cosmetic; the parse is unaffected. Reported, not edited.

### BT19-077 — Calumon

Lane 32. Base `23eee9e5a`, branch `audit-bt19-reaudit`. Module IR CHANGED (resync needed);
test file rewritten.

#### Card summary

Catalog: White Digimon, **no level** (`level` absent), Unknown form / attribute / type,
play cost 3, DP 1000, `evoCosts: []`.

Printed clauses:

1. `[Security] You may play 1 Digimon card with 2000 DP or less from your hand without
paying the cost.`
2. `[Main] By suspending this Digimon, 1 of your Digimon may digivolve into a Digimon card
in the hand with the digivolution cost reduced by 2.`
3. `[All Turns] This Digimon can't attack or block.`
4. `[On Deletion] Place this card on top of your security stack.`

#### Rules read

- White (`comprehensive 2-4-2`): an ordinary colour, no special play rule.
- **No level** (`comprehensive 2-9-2`): "Cards that have no level displayed, or with 'Lv.－'
  shown, are treated as having no level." Consequences proved below: the battle-area rule
  sweep for level-2-or-lower Digimon never reaches it, and no ordinary digivolution route
  targets it (nothing is "one level higher" than no level) — it only ever reaches the board
  through a play (its own play cost, or the `[Security]` clause of another card).
- `CR 13-1-8-4`: "A card revealed from a security check is placed in the trash unless it
  belongs to an area."
- `CR 14-2-3`: "Security Digimon aren't deleted even when they lose a battle." This decides
  the interaction below.

#### Q&A ids

| Id                                                                                        | Covered by                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Q3136 (can't activate the `[Main]` at the same time as another digivolving effect, P-103) | `suspends itself to digivolve another Digimon from hand for 2 less, keeping the base stack` — the engine has no intent that expresses two simultaneous `[Main]` activations: `activateEffect` names one `effectKey` on one source and resolves it to completion. The test asserts the one-at-a-time model directly: a second `activateEffect` on the same key is refused once the suspend cost is spent. Documented as untestable beyond that, because the ruling restates the activation model rather than card behaviour. |
| Q6243 (checked from security: `[Security]` activates, THEN it battles)                    | `plays a 2000-DP-or-less Digimon free from the security check, then battles the attacker (Q6243)` — both halves asserted in one flow.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |

#### Clause -> test -> IR

- **Clause 1** -> `effects[Security].actions[0]` `PlayWithoutCost`, `from: ["hand"]`,
  `payCost: false`, `optional: true`, filter `controller: "mine", kind: ["Digimon"],
dp: { op: "lte", value: 2000 }`.
  - The `dp` OBJECT form is read for loose hand cards against the PRINTED DP
    (`interpreter/matching/definition.ts:207`), so this is **not** an instance of the lane-6
    dropped-`playCost`-object trap. Verified by source and by behaviour.
  - `plays a 2000-DP-or-less Digimon free from the security check, then battles the attacker`:
    real opponent turn through `startTurnLoop` + `waitForMainPhase(1)` + a public `attack`
    intent. `BT1-012` Biyomon (2000 DP) is played; `BT1-009` Monodramon (3000 DP) is never a
    candidate and stays in hand. "Without paying the cost" is read at the exact instant of the
    play via the `onEvent` hook (`memoryAtPlay === memoryBeforeCheck`), not after the turn
    hand-off. The 1000 DP attacker then ties the 1000 DP Security Digimon and is deleted.
- **Clause 2** -> `effects[Main].actions[0]` `Digivolve`, `from: ["hand"]`, `payCost: true`,
  `reduceCost: 2`, `cost: { kind: "suspend", target.isSelf }`.
  - `suspends itself to digivolve another Digimon from hand for 2 less, keeping the base
stack`: `activateEffect` through the public intent. Calumon ends suspended (the cost was
    really paid); the base `BT1-014` Kokatorimon (Lv.4, already carrying `BT1-009` as a
    digivolution card) becomes `BT1-024` MetalTyrannomon, whose printed Lv.4 route costs 3 —
    reduced by 2 it costs 1, so memory 3 -> 2. Stack asserted by instance id bottom-first
    (`[older, base]`), `currentDP` 10000, one bonus draw, no pending decision, no loud gap.
  - `abortOnDecline: true` sits on the sole action and is dead (lanes 4/8 finding); left
    untouched rather than churning the IR.
- **Clause 3** -> `effects[AllTurns].actions[0]` `Restrict`, `restriction: "attackOrBlock"`,
  `duration: "permanent"`. Trigger is `AllTurns`, not `Static` — the printed marker is
  `[All Turns]`.
  - `attackOrBlock` is expanded by the interpreter into the two enforced restrictions
    `attack` and `block` (`interpreter/actions/restrictions.ts:108`); `observe().isRestricted`
    is asserted on both, and on an unrestricted peer for contrast.
  - `refuses a real attack declaration ...`: the public `attack` intent is rejected, security
    untouched, Calumon unsuspended; the same board's `BT1-009` then attacks successfully.
  - `refuses a real block declaration in the opponent's open block window`: a real ＜Blocker＞
    peer (`EX6-012`) is seeded so the window genuinely opens; `declareBlock` with Calumon is
    refused, then the same window accepts the peer and the block redirects the attack away
    from security.
- **Clause 4** -> `effects[OnDeletion].actions[0]` `SecurityManipulation`,
  `op: "placeAsSecurity"`, `controller: "mine"`, `toTop: true`, **no `source`**.
  - `returns to the top of its owner's security stack when deleted in a real opponent-turn
battle`: Calumon is suspended the only way the card allows (paying its own `[Main]` cost)
    on its controller's turn, stays suspended into the opponent's real turn, and is attacked
    by a 5000 DP Digimon. Security becomes `[calumon, previousTop, ...]` by instance id, and
    the card is never in the trash.

#### Defects found and fixed locally

**`[On Deletion]` placed nothing when Calumon was deleted from the battle area.** The action
carried `source: { filter: { isSelfRef: true }, count: 1, isSelf: true }`. That branch of
`apps/api/src/engine/effects/interpreter/actions/security.ts` resolves PERMANENTS
(`resolvePermanentTargets` at :375, then `topInstanceIds`; `if (ids.length === 0) return`),
and the permanent is already gone by the time an `[On Deletion]` effect resolves, so the card
went to the trash instead. The self form is `source` OMITTED (`security.ts:363-370`:
`ctx.source.permanent()?.topCard?.instanceId ?? ctx.source.instanceId`), which survives the
deletion — the idiom BT2-040 Ophanimon uses for the identical printed sentence. Fixed.

#### Engine behaviour confirmed correct (initial test expectation was wrong)

A Security Digimon that loses its battle does **not** trigger `[On Deletion]`. `CR 14-2-3`
says Security Digimon aren't deleted even when they lose, and `CR 13-1-8-4` sends the checked
card to the trash instead; `battleSecurityDigimon`
(`apps/api/src/engine/security/securityCheck.ts:366-405`) implements exactly that and
documents both rules. The Q6243 test now asserts this: after the battle the security stack is
the two untouched cards and Calumon is in the trash — it does **not** come back on top. No red
is retained; the engine is right.

  `BT1-012` (2000 DP) is.
- Restriction near misses: an unrestricted attacker peer (`BT1-009`) and an unrestricted
  ＜Blocker＞ peer (`EX6-012`) on the same board, both asserted through real intents.
- Realistic stack: the `[Main]` digivolve runs onto a base that already carries a
  digivolution card, and the resulting three-card identity is asserted by instance id.

#### Remaining gaps

- Q3136 has no direct behavioural expression: the intent surface cannot request two
  simultaneous `[Main]` activations. Covered by the one-at-a-time assertion and documented.

#### Catalog discrepancies

- `forms`, `attributes` and `types` are all `["Unknown"]` and `level` is absent. Consistent

  is not a level-2-or-lower Digimon, so the battle-area rule sweep never removes it. Verified
  behaviourally, not assumed — a Digi-Egg without DP/level seeded on the battle area is swept
  before the first intent (lane 28 finding), and this one is not.

| The inherited watcher installs under DP-bearing Digi-Egg hosts such as `EX2-007 Mother D-Reaper` | **Confirmed**, and tightened: `observe().subscriptions("whenOpponentAttacks", motherPermanentId)` is empty during the controller's own Main and holds exactly one subscription during the opponent's Main — `[Opponent's Turn]` scopes the install.                 |
| The attack subject is filtered to an opponent's Digimon                                          | **Confirmed and correct** against the printed "When any of your **opponent's** Digimon attack": `sourceFilter: { controller: "opponent", kind: ["Digimon"] }`. Proved behaviourally by a controller-side attack on the controller's own turn that does not fire it. |

#### Clause -> test -> IR

- **Clause 1** -> `effects[OnPlay].actions[0]` `ModifyDP`, `amount: -1000`,

nameOrTrait: [{ tokens: ["Mother D-Reaper"], match: "nameExact" }] } }`.

    public `activateEffect`. Two Mothers are on the board; the blocked one carries `EX2-049`,

digivolution cards for a DigiXros.`

#### Catalog discrepancies

The catalog separates `[Xros Heart]` from `trait` in clause 2 with U+00A0, not a plain space.
The identity test asserts the exact bytes (` ` escape) and says so in a comment. No edit
made; reported only.

#### Q&A ids

| Q3139 (cards may come from under a Tamer other than this one)         | `Q3139: the material may sit under a DIFFERENT Tamer than the one being suspended` and its near-miss `Q3139 near-miss: naming the non-expander host Tamer as the expander is rejected` |

#### Clause -> test -> IR

- **Clause 1** -> `effects[0]` `StartOfYourTurn` / `SetMemory { value: 3 }` gated on
  `condition { kind: "memoryAtMost", value: 2 }`. Confirmed correct against the printed text

  - Negative: memory 6 stays 6.

mode: "instead", optional: true }` with

match: "trait" }], hasDigiXrosRequirement: true }`, wrapping
  `DigiXrosMaterialZoneExpansion { zones: ["underTamers"], duration: "forTheTurn",
cost: suspend self }`. See "Defect fixed" below.

  `underTamerMax: 100`, **no** `underTamerHostScope`, so any of the player's Tamers may host —

"invalid-material" }` with the board and memory untouched; an already-suspended BT19-079

#### Peer / stack proof

- **Near-miss peer for the trait gate**: BT10-088 Kiriha Aonuma is the same printed shape with
  **no** trait gate (`appliesTo: () => true`). The same MadLeomon play that BT19-079 refuses is
  accepted with Kiriha as the expander, with the material landing in the stack and Kiriha
  suspended. The refusal is therefore BT19-079's own `[Xros Heart]` gate, not a generic
  DigiXros restriction.
- **Near-miss peer for the host**: BT19-080 Takato Matsuki, a red Tamer with no expander
  registration, hosts the material in the Q3139 test (accepted, and it is _not_ the permanent
  that suspends) and is rejected as `invalid-expander` when named as the expander itself.
- **Realistic board**: every DigiXros fixture uses real recipe material (BT10-008 Shoutmon
  filling a named slot of BT10-009 / BT11-009), and Q3140 runs two Tamers, two under-Tamer
  materials and two different DigiXros cards in one turn with the memory ledger asserted at
  each step (12 -> 5 -> 1).

#### Defect fixed locally

The `[All Turns]` clause was modelled as a **bare `AllTurns` action** — `optional: true`,
`DigiXrosMaterialZoneExpansion` with a suspend cost — with no `Replacement` wrapper and no
`sourceFilter`. Consequence, observed: on any board with BT19-079 the clause offers its
"by suspending this Tamer" cost at every `[All Turns]` window, and accepting it suspends the
Tamer with no DigiXros in sight. In the harness this showed up as the Tamer already suspended
before the first play intent in **six** separate fixtures (including one that plays a DigiXros
card entirely from hand and never touches the Tamer).

Fix: adopt the shape its two printed siblings already use — BT19-087 Nene Amano and EX10-064,
both "when a … Digimon with DigiXros requirements would be played, by suspending this Tamer …":
`Replacement { event: "wouldBePlayed", mode: "instead", optional: true }` with a `sourceFilter`
carrying `kind: ["Digimon"]`, the `[Xros Heart]` trait token (`match: "trait"`, exact — the
printed wording is "with the … trait") and `hasDigiXrosRequirement: true`. `zones` moved from
`digivolutionCards` to `underTamers` to match the printed "under your Tamers" and both peers
(`interpreter/actions/play.ts:649-662` accepts either token for the under-Tamer quota, so this
is a fidelity change, not a behaviour change), and `duration` from `untilOpponentTurnEnd` to
the peers' `forTheTurn`.

The registry entry in `packages/shared/src/cards/zoneExpanders.ts` was **not** touched (it is
outside this lane's allowed edits and was already correct: `[Xros Heart]` gate, `underTamerMax`
100, unrestricted host scope).

#### Retained reds / engine gaps

None. All 16 tests are green.

#### Remaining gaps

- The `[All Turns]` clause is proved through the direct `playCard` DigiXros verb and its
  registry consumer, which is the production path a player uses. The IR `Replacement` node
  itself is asserted structurally and by the absence of the spurious suspend; no card in the
  set drives a DigiXros play through the _effect_ play path, so that branch is unexercised.
- Q3140 uses two copies of BT19-079 because the printed cost suspends the Tamer. A single copy
  cannot legally expand twice in one turn, so "each of those cards" is proved per-Tamer rather
  than per-copy of one Tamer; that matches the cost, not a limitation of the test.

[{ tokens: ["Growlmon", "Gallantmon"], match: "name" }] }`, then

cost: suspend self, target.sourceRef: "triggerSubject" }` and
  `Attack { attackPlayer: true, mandatory: true, target.sourceRef: "triggerSubject" }`.
  - `match: "name"` (substring) is **correct** here: the printed wording is "with
    [Growlmon]/[Gallantmon] **in its name**", the substring form. A bracketed `[Name]`
    reference would have needed `namesExact`. Checked explicitly against the set's known trap.
  - `abortOnDecline: true` is **live**, not the dead form the set has seen elsewhere: a second
    action (`Attack`) follows it, and the decline test proves the attack does not happen.
  - Positive (Growlmon, Lv.3 -> Lv.4): the base permanent keeps its identity, the Lv.3 instance
    id is the only card in its stack, `observe().hasKeyword(perm, "Raid")` is true, the Tamer
    is suspended (the paid cost), the attacker is suspended, one of the opponent's three
    security cards is checked, and an `attackDeclared` event names the base permanent.
  - Q3141: exactly one `optional` decision is raised across the whole resolution.
  - Cost declined (`autoDeclineOptional`): no Raid, Tamer unsuspended, attacker unsuspended,
    opponent's security untouched — the whole clause aborts.

  `PlayWithoutCost { payCost: false, from: ["security"], target: { isSelfRef: true } }`.

    attacks the player; the Tamer's instance id is the only permanent on seat 1's board, gone
    from security, not in the trash, memory unchanged (cost 4 not paid).

    stays face down in security.

- **Realistic evolution stack**: the Gallantmon test seeds a Lv.5 WarGrowlmon with a Growlmon
  already underneath and asserts the post-digivolve stack by instance id, bottom-first

  **seat 1's real turn**, reached through `startTurnLoop()` + `waitForMainPhase(1)` (no
  `turnSeat` injection) and closed with `surrender` + `await loop`. No Raid, Tamer unsuspended,
  seat 0's security untouched.

#### Defects

##### Fixed in this lane (module IR)

1. **The [All Turns] clause was modelled as the wrong node.** It carried a `PlaceUnder` with
   `target { zone: "underTamer", count: "all", upTo: true }` and `asDigiXrosMaterial: true`.
   That describes a card-moving action the printed clause never performs. The clause widens the
   DigiXros material _source zones_; how many materials are placed is fixed by the played card's
   DigiXros recipe, never by a player-chosen subset of what sits under the Tamers — so the
   `count: "all", upTo: true` shape the previous typed revalidation introduced is not supported by
   the printed text or by Q3142–Q3144. Replaced with the canonical
   `Replacement(wouldBePlayed) → DigiXrosMaterialZoneExpansion { zones: ["underTamers"] }`, the
   exact shape its printed sibling BT19-079 (Taiki Kudo) carries.
2. **The paid condition on clause 1 was mandatory.** "By placing …, gain 1 memory" is a paid
   processing condition and paying it is the controller's choice (comprehensive 15-7-4). Without
   `optional: true` the placement was forced on every Main-phase entry that had a legal hand card.
   Added `optional: true`; both branches are now proved.
3. `from: ["hand"]` made explicit on the place cost (the interpreter already defaults to the hand,
   so this is documentation of the printed zone rather than a behaviour change; the trash near-miss
   test pins it either way).

##### Retained red

None. The seam below was closed by the coordinator during this lane; all 15 tests pass.

##### Engine/shared seam found and closed by the coordinator

The audit originally landed `it.fails("Q3142/Q3143: an under-Tamer material is legal when
BT19-081 is suspended")` because the `[All Turns]` permission was inert at the real play seam:

- Seam: `packages/shared/src/cards/zoneExpanders.ts`, `DIGIXROS_ZONE_EXPANDERS` /
  `digiXrosZoneExpanderFor`, read by `apps/api/src/engine/actions/digiXros.ts` (~line 240) when a
  play intent names `expanderPermanentIds`.
- BT19-081 had **no entry** in that registry. The `DigiXrosMaterialZoneExpansion` node records
  `["underTamers"]` in the per-seat ledger, but `digiXros.ts` reads only `trash` out of that
  ledger (`ledgerZones.includes("trash")`), so an under-Tamer material was refused as
  `{ ok: false, reason: "invalid-expander" }`.

The coordinator added
`"BT19-081": { appliesTo: (def) => hasAnyTrait(def, ["Blue Flare"]), underTamerMax: 100, trashMax: 0 }`
with **no** `underTamerHostScope` (Q3143: any of your Tamers may host) and rebuilt shared. The
`it.fails` is now a plain `it` and passes: the under-Tamer card lands as a digivolution card of the
played Digimon, BT19-081 suspends, and the hosting Tamer does not. `packages/shared` was outside
this lane, so the registry edit is the coordinator's, not this lane's.

The temporary control test that pinned the old refusal
(`today the under-Tamer material is refused because BT19-081 is not a registered expander`) has
been removed — it asserted the pre-fix result and would now fail by design. The two durable
controls stay:

- `peer control: BT10-088, which IS registered, legalizes an under-Tamer material for the same play`
  — an independent expander reaching the same endpoint.
- `the trait gate is per registration: BT19-079's [Xros Heart] gate refuses this [Blue Flare] card`
  — the gate BT19-081's own registration inverts.
- `without naming any expander, an under-Tamer material is illegal for every seat` — the
  permission is not ambient.

`EX4-062` was tried first as the peer control and rejected: its own `[All Turns]` effect is a bare
`AllTurns` with an unconditional suspend cost, so it suspends itself on any All-Turns window and
is then refused as `invalid-expander` (not this lane's card; noted for whoever audits EX4-062).

#### Remaining gaps

- Q3144 ("triggers for each qualifying card played") has no dedicated test. The printed suspend
  cost limits a single copy to one play per turn anyway, so the repeat case needs two BT19-081
  copies; the sibling BT19-079 already covers it on the identical seam.
- The `[Blue Flare]` gate of clause 2 is proved at the IR level, by the positive under-Tamer play
  on a `[Blue Flare]` DigiXros card, and by the BT19-079 `[Xros Heart]` contrast. A negative that
  names BT19-081 itself as the expander for a non-`[Blue Flare]` DigiXros card would tighten it

cosmetic: **no card in the catalog carries a trait spelled exactly `Aqua`** — the printed reference

excluded from its own Tamer's ability. Changed both refs to `match: "traitContains"`
(`interpreter/matching/definition.ts`, `matchNameOrTrait`). Every [Aquatic] fixture in the test
file is a live proof: all of them fail under the old shape.

`levelComparison { op: "lte", value: 5 }` on a hand-card target was checked against the
loose-card seam and is honoured there (`definitionMatchesFilter`, definition.ts ~line 143) — it is
_not_ an instance of the `playCost: { op, value }` object-form trap, which affects only play-cost
keys on loose cards. The level-gate near-miss test proves it behaviourally.

plain space. No edit made; the catalog test asserts the NBSP is present and that the text
matches the print once normalised, so the discrepancy is pinned rather than hidden.

Nothing else diverges: name, colours, kinds, cost, DP, `evoCosts: []`, `maxCountInDeck`,
`securityEffectText` all match the print.

#### Clause -> test -> IR

- **Clause 1** -> `effects[0]` `OnPlay` / `RevealAdd { revealCount: 3, add: [Digimon
name-substring, Option name-substring], rest: "deckBottom" }`.
  - Positive: a real `playCard` intent from hand pays 3 (memory 3 -> 0), the Tamer lands on
    the battle area, both hits reach the hand, and the single non-hit is the **last** card of
    the deck (asserted by instance id, behind the pre-existing bottom marker).
  - Near-miss (name): two Green Digimon carrying none of the four names and a Yellow Option
    without `[Plug-In]` ⇒ nothing added, all three at the bottom in reveal order.
  - Partial: only the Digimon hit present ⇒ exactly one card added, the Option near-miss
    returned.
  - The gates are `match: "name"` (substring), which is the printed `"in its name"` form. A
    `namesExact` gate here would be **wrong** — it would refuse `[Sakuyamon: Maid Mode]`. The
    IR test states this.
- **Clause 2** -> `effects[1]` `YourTurn` / `SubTrigger { event: "whenOptionUsed",
fireCondition: { kind: "triggerOptionCostAtLeast", value: 2 } }` -> `GainMemory { amount: 1,
cost: { kind: "suspend", target: { filter: { isSelfRef: true }, isSelf: true } },
optional: true }`.
  - Threshold: a real cost-2 Option play (BT1-102) suspends the Tamer and gains 1; the cost-1
    peer (ST3-13) does neither. Both runs assert the exact memory arithmetic
    (`5 − cost + gain`) and the suspend flag.
  - Declined: with `autoDeclineOptional` the cost is not paid, memory is only `5 − 2 = 3` and
    the Tamer stays unsuspended.
  - Repeat within one turn: the Tamer is already suspended, so the second cost-2 Option in the
    same turn yields no memory; the opponent's whole turn passes through the real loop
    (`startTurnLoop` + `waitForMainPhase` + `endPhase`) and the Tamer stands back up at our own
    unsuspend phase, after which a third Option pays again.
  - `[Your Turn]` gate: seat 1 plays BT1-102 on its own turn (with its own yellow permanent for
    the colour requirement) and nothing fires; `state.memory` moves only by seat 1's payment.
  - `abortOnDecline: true` is present on the sole action of the effect and is therefore dead
    (brief's known trap for 008/016). Left untouched — removing it would churn the IR for no
    behavioural change.
- **Clause 3** -> `effects[2]` `Security` / `PlayWithoutCost { target: { isSelfRef: true },
payCost: false }`, `isSecurity: true`.
  - Proved through a **real security check**: seat 0 attacks the player with a 3000 DP
    Monodramon, seat 1's top security card is BT19-083, and it arrives on seat 1's battle area
    with `state.memory` unchanged (no cost paid) and the rest of the security stack intact.
    Its own `[On Play]` also resolves off that play — both name hits reach seat 1's hand and
    the non-hit goes to seat 1's deck bottom.

None in the module. The pre-existing test file was 91 lines: one shallow `[On Play]` smoke
test and one large `toMatchObject` IR snapshot. The `[Your Turn]` watcher and the `[Security]`
clause had **no** behavioural coverage at all, and no near-miss, cost-threshold, opponent-turn
or unsuspend-reset case existed. The whole file was rewritten.
